providers.description: Allbirds is a sustainability-focused footwear and apparel brand known for its wool and tree-fiber shoes, selling direct-to-consumer through its Shopify-powered online store at allbirds.com. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Addition and added to the API Evangelist network. While Allbirds publishes no traditional developer program, its storefront exposes a real agent-commerce surface: a live Shopify Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) MCP server for catalog search, cart, and checkout; OpenID Connect / OAuth 2.0 Customer Accounts authentication; and an /llms.txt agent-instructions document. This profile captures that agent-native commerce and authentication surface.

providers.name: Noda
providers.description: Noda (formerly Infogrid) is an agentic AI platform for commercial real estate building operations. It functions as an always-on AI virtual building engineer that connects to a portfolio's building management systems (BMS), IoT, weather, and utility data, continuously detects faults and energy waste, identifies root causes, generates quantified savings recommendations, and executes authorized setpoint and load adjustments — tying every action to measured, audit-ready ROI. The platform processes 100M+ data points daily and reports 15-25% annual energy reduction across deployed assets. Trusted by owners and operators of 400M+ square feet including Hilton, JLL, CBRE, Macerich, Cousins, DivcoWest and Salesforce. ISO 27001 certified and hosted on AWS in the United States. Backed by Northzone. Noda exposes no public developer API; onboarding is enterprise/demo-based.

providers.name: AES Corporation
providers.description: The AES Corporation is a Fortune 500 global energy company that generates and distributes electrical power. AES operates a diverse portfolio of renewable, thermal, LNG, and battery storage facilities across multiple countries, serving utilities, industrial facilities, and end users. AES is the largest global supplier of clean energy to corporations in the Americas and operates 34.7 GW globally with $12.2 billion in annual revenue. The company serves 18.7 million household equivalents through utilities in Indiana, Ohio, and El Salvador. AES also co-founded Fluence Energy, a leading energy storage and software platform company.

providers.name: WindBorne Systems
providers.description: WindBorne Systems operates a global constellation of long-duration Global Sounding Balloons and pairs that proprietary in-situ atmospheric data with WeatherMesh, its AI-based numerical weather forecast model. The WindBorne Data API serves real-time balloon observations, soundings, super-observations, constellation and flight-path metadata, point and gridded WeatherMesh forecasts, tropical-cyclone tracks, and population-weighted heating/cooling degree-day insights. Access is via a Bearer API key over REST, an official Python library and CLI, and a hosted Model Context Protocol server for AI agents.

providers.name: Bellwether Coffee
providers.description: Bellwether Coffee is a Berkeley, California coffee-technology company founded in 2013 by Ricardo Lopez that designs and manufactures an all-electric, ventless, automatic commercial coffee roaster. The Bellwether Shop Roaster (SCA Best New Product 2024) roasts 1.5 kg per batch on a standard 240V/30A circuit with no gas line, exhaust, or construction, and is paired with a complete coffee business program: a traceable Green Coffee Marketplace with ready-made roast profiles, cloud-connected roast automation and inventory software, custom retail packaging and labels, and ongoing service. Bellwether has raised roughly $92.7M across eight rounds and serves 500+ customers across 26 countries. It publishes no public developer API, but does maintain a genuine machine-readable web surface: an RFC 9727 /.well-known/api-catalog linkset, a structured facts.json, an llms.txt, and Content Signals AI-usage declarations in robots.txt.

providers.name: Jupiter Intelligence
providers.description: Jupiter Intelligence is a climate risk analytics company founded in 2017 and headquartered in San Mateo, California. Built by climate scientists, Jupiter delivers decision-grade physical and extreme-weather risk intelligence to banks, insurers, asset managers, corporates, and public-sector institutions. Its flagship platform, ClimateScore Global, translates physical climate exposure across multiple perils, scenarios, and time horizons out to 2100 into finance-linked, audit-ready metrics that support underwriting, capital planning, portfolio management, and regulatory disclosure. Products include ClimateScore Global, RiskSignal, Adaptation Hub, Entity Modeling, MetricEngine, Compliance Hub, and the MRM Accelerator. Jupiter is delivered as a SaaS application, an enterprise API, and tailored analytics support. It is SOC 2 Type 2 certified and backed by investors including DCVC.

providers.name: Koloma
providers.description: Koloma is a Denver, Colorado based natural (geologic) hydrogen exploration and production company founded in 2021 by Pete Johnson and Tom Darrah, PhD, with a research laboratory in Columbus, Ohio. The company applies subsurface geoscience, proprietary data and data-driven exploration methods — airborne geophysics, passive acoustic and magnetotelluric surveys, and lab characterization of rock, liquid and gas samples — to locate and produce naturally occurring hydrogen generated by serpentinization deep within the Earth. Koloma operates in the United States and internationally, including Koloma Australia and exploration operations in the Philippines, and is backed by Amazon Climate Pledge Fund, Breakthrough Energy Ventures, Khosla Ventures, Mitsubishi Heavy Industries and United Airlines. Koloma publishes no public developer platform, API documentation or SDKs; its only machine-readable agent surface found in this pass is a Wix-platform Model Context Protocol endpoint plus an llms.txt served from the Koloma California regional site.

providers.name: Complir
providers.description: Complir is the AI infrastructure for product compliance, described by the company as "Vanta for physical products." Its AI agents map product data, analyse compliance risks, generate audit-ready documentation, and track regulatory changes across every market a brand sells in - covering GPSR, ESPR, EPR, REACH, RoHS, PPWR, EUDR, CE/UKCA marking, Digital Product Passports and 100+ other frameworks across 40+ markets. The platform maps each SKU to its regulatory requirements, produces translations, labels, warnings, declarations of conformity and technical files, verifies marketing claims, and offers native Adobe Illustrator/InDesign plugins plus a natural language interface for querying compliance data. Founded in 2024 (Gustav Bang, Marc Kaa Brejner, Tine Kuhnel) and part of Y Combinator's Spring 2026 batch, Complir monitors 100,000+ products for international retailers including Flying Tiger Copenhagen, Konges Sloejd, Matas and COOP.

providers.name: JOLT
providers.description: JOLT is a Sydney-headquartered electric vehicle charging network operator that builds and runs free-to-start kerbside DC fast chargers across Australia, and has since extended the same model into New Zealand, Canada, the United Kingdom and the United States. Its charge points deliver the first 7kWh of each day's charging at no cost — around 45km of range in roughly 15 minutes over CCS2 or CHAdeMO — funded not by the driver but by the digital out-of-home advertising screens mounted on the charger itself, which makes JOLT simultaneously a charge point operator and a media network selling audience reach to advertisers. It sits in the energy value chain as a downstream infrastructure and demand-side player: it buys electricity (claiming 100% GreenPower green-certified wind and solar), owns and operates the charging assets on public and retail land in partnership with governments and hosts such as Transport for NSW, Ausgrid and major grocery retailers, and monetises the dwell time rather than the kilowatt-hour. Its API posture is honestly closed. JOLT publishes no developer programme, no API documentation, no OpenAPI or other machine-readable contract, and no open data feed; the only public HTTP surfaces on its domains are a marketing WordPress install (whose custom jolt/v1 REST namespace exposes a single VAT form endpoint) and an api.joltcharge.com host that serves a static redirect to the mobile app rather than any API. It is not a designated data holder under the Australian Consumer Data Right for energy — it does not appear in the CDR Register's energy data holder brands — so the CDR energy mandate that compels Australian electricity retailers to expose standardised usage and tariff data does not reach it, and no OCPP, OCPI, ISO 15118 or Green Button/ESPI conformance is published. All customer charging data, session history and audience analytics are reachable only through the JOLT consumer app or a sales conversation.

providers.name: Ecorobotix
providers.description: Ecorobotix SA is a Swiss agricultural technology company founded in 2011 and headquartered in Yverdon-les-Bains, Switzerland, building AI-driven ultra-high-precision (UHP) crop-care equipment. Its flagship ARA smart sprayer combines Plant-by-Plant AI detection with UHP-Spray-Technology to scan a field, classify crops versus weeds in under 250 milliseconds, and place treatment on a roughly six-by-six centimetre target, cutting herbicide and plant-protection input volumes by up to 95 percent compared with broadcast spraying. The product family spans the ARA620 and ARA595 UHP sprayers for row and vegetable crops, the ALBA UHP sprayer for turf, and a library of crop-specific algorithms for broccoli, carrots, onions and chicory. More than 1,000 ARA units have been deployed across Europe, the United Kingdom, North America, South America and Australia/New Zealand. Machine telemetry, treatment maps and fleet data are delivered to customers through the Ecorobotix cloud portal, which is backed by an authenticated REST API; that API is not offered as a public developer program.

providers.name: Meshcrafts
providers.description: Meshcrafts, operating publicly as CURRENT (Current Eco AS, formerly Meshcrafts AS, of Oslo, Norway), is a charge point management system (CPMS) provider for electric vehicle (EV) charging infrastructure. Its cloud platform lets location owners and charge point operators manage EV charging points, handle payment and invoicing, apply smart energy management and load balancing, and offer white-label charging experiences to drivers. The platform is hardware-agnostic and OCPP (Open Charge Point Protocol) certified for OCPP 1.6 and OCPP 2.0.1, including Advanced Security, and advertises 99% uptime. Current was the first in the Nordics to reach OCPP 2.0.1 CORE and Advanced Security. The company is backed by 500 Global and surfaced in the API Evangelist network through that portfolio.

providers.name: EcoSoul Home
providers.description: EcoSoul Home is a direct-to-consumer sustainable home-essentials brand selling compostable and eco-friendly tableware — plates, bowls, hot cups, cutlery, napkins, bagasse and areca-leaf products — plus everyday household goods made from renewable materials. The brand sells online through its Shopify storefront (and via major retail marketplaces) with the mission of replacing single-use plastic in the home. Backed by Accel, EcoSoul was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead and enriched from its public agent-native commerce surface: a published /llms.txt (agents.md) instruction file, Shopify Customer Accounts OpenID Connect for authentication, and a Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) MCP endpoint that lets buyer-approved AI shopping agents search the catalog, build carts, and complete checkout via Shop Pay, Google Pay, or card.

providers.name: Enervee
providers.description: Enervee operates an AI-powered white-label marketplace platform that helps utilities and government energy programs scale energy efficiency across 39 million-plus households in North America. Its stack spans a utility-branded online store for efficient appliances and equipment across 40-plus product categories (HVAC, water heaters, heat pumps, smart thermostats, EV chargers), the Enervee Score - a proprietary 0-100 energy-efficiency rating updated daily - Eco Financing embedded lending at checkout through national bank partners, and Instant Rebates that automatically stack utility, government, and manufacturer incentives at checkout. Enervee is a portfolio company of Obvious Ventures. No public developer API or documentation surface is currently published; this profile captures the company's public security, trust, and identity posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Cato Digital
providers.description: Cato Digital is a sustainable bare metal cloud provider that repurposes large-scale, second-life servers from hyperscalers like Meta and NVIDIA to deliver AI & GPU servers (up to 512GB VRAM), ephemeral application servers, and build-your-own storage arrays at 60-75% below major cloud providers. Led by CEO Dean Nelson, the company operates on a "use what we have before we build more" circular-economy principle, tapping underutilized data center capacity and clean energy, and is a founding member of the Infrastructure Masons Climate Accord. Customers provision and manage infrastructure through the Cato console rather than a public developer API.

providers.name: CPower, Inc.
providers.description: CPower Energy is a commercial and industrial (C&I) virtual power plant (VPP) operator that helps organizations monetize the flexibility of their energy assets through demand response and distributed energy resource (DER) programs. Its CPower CONNECT platform lets customers view, manage, and unlock revenue from energy assets while supporting grid reliability and sustainability goals. CPower serves data centers, crypto mining, healthcare, education, retail, commercial real estate, industrial operations, and the public sector, and has operated distributed energy programs across the U.S. since 2015. CPower was acquired by NRG Energy and operates a combined C&I VPP platform. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio-adjacent deep-tech lead and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; CPower publishes a customer portal and a security and compliance posture but no public developer API at this time.

providers.name: Crux
providers.description: Crux is a capital platform for the clean economy, connecting clean energy and manufacturing developers with buyers, lenders, and investors. Its marketplace facilitates the sale of transferable clean energy tax credits created under the Inflation Reduction Act, alongside debt capital markets, tax equity, and preferred equity solutions and advisory services. Crux pairs a transaction platform and secure data room with market intelligence drawn from tens of billions of dollars in deal data, serving project developers, manufacturers, tax credit buyers, banks, tax advisors, and legal teams. The company is backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead. Crux operates a customer application but does not publish a public developer API or OpenAPI at this time.

providers.name: Nexamp
providers.description: Nexamp is a Boston-based clean energy company, founded in 2007 by two U.S. Army veterans, that develops, builds, owns and operates distributed solar generation and battery storage across the United States and is one of the country's largest fully integrated community solar providers. The company runs end-to-end: project development and acquisition, engineering and design, construction, asset operations, and subscriber management for residential and commercial community solar customers, alongside power purchase agreements, land leasing for solar farm hosts, energy storage, and standalone development and asset-management services. Customer-facing software is delivered through the community.nexamp.com subscriber portal and the portal.nexamp.com Decarbonization Platform. As of the 2026-08-01 enrichment pass Nexamp publishes no public developer program, API documentation, SDKs, or machine-readable API contract; the api.nexamp.com host that exists is gated behind Microsoft Entra ID and is not publicly documented.

providers.name: Build
providers.description: Build is an AI-native operating partner for the built world, pairing autonomous AI agents (its "Dougie" platform) with deep domain expertise to accelerate commercial real estate and infrastructure development. The platform automates mission-critical development workflows including site selection, due diligence, underwriting, investment-committee memos, test-fit analysis, market and zoning research, environmental diligence, and ESG reporting. Build serves institutional clients across data centers, industrials, energy, power, office, telecommunications, mixed-use, hotels, and multifamily. Backed by Index Ventures; profiled in the API Evangelist network. Build is a services company and does not currently publish a public developer API.

providers.name: HAMAMA
providers.description: Hamama is a West Sacramento, California consumer-products company that makes it easy to grow fresh microgreens at home. Founded by two MIT-trained mechanical engineers, Hamama sells self-watering microgreen grow kits and its signature pre-seeded "Seed Quilts" (non-GMO, mostly Certified Organic) that sprout edible greens in 7-10 days with nothing more than a single addition of water, no soil, pesticides, or fertilizer required. The company sells grow kits, ceramic trays, Seed Quilt refills, green-onion and mushroom kits, and accessories directly to consumers through its Shopify storefront, offers flexible subscribe-and-save refill plans, and supports growers with Growing Guides, recipes, a rewards program, and a Grow Coach customer-support team.

providers.name: Nuvolo
providers.description: Nuvolo is a modern Integrated Workplace Management System (IWMS) and Enterprise Asset Management provider that delivers its Connected Workplace suite natively on the ServiceNow platform. It unifies facilities and space management, real estate and lease administration, capital planning and projects, maintenance and work management, healthcare technology management (HTM), GxP and life-sciences asset management, refrigeration management, sustainability and energy, and OT security into a single cloud platform. Nuvolo serves healthcare, life sciences, public sector, retail, and education organizations, helping them manage the full lifecycle of their assets, spaces, and facilities with mobile access and real-time reporting. Backed by Insight Partners.

providers.name: Plan A
providers.description: Plan A is a Berlin-based sustainability technology company providing certified carbon accounting and ESG management software that helps businesses measure, report, and reduce their greenhouse gas emissions. The platform is built on GHG Protocol standards, is SOC 2 Type II certified, and offers AI-enhanced emissions intelligence, supplier engagement, decarbonisation planning, and regulatory reporting (CSRD/ESRS). Plan A operates enterprise data integrations via custom APIs but does not publish a public developer platform, OpenAPI specification, or API reference. Backed by HV Capital and Lightspeed Venture Partners; surfaced to the API Evangelist network as a VC-portfolio lead and enriched with verified public identity and web properties.

providers.name: Waste Connections
providers.description: Waste Connections is the third-largest integrated provider of solid waste services in North America, serving approximately nine million residential, commercial, and industrial customers across 46 U.S. states and six Canadian provinces. The company provides non-hazardous waste collection, transfer, disposal, and recycling services, primarily in exclusive and secondary markets. Waste Connections is investing in AI-powered dynamic routing and expanding customer connectivity features through its online customer portal.

providers.name: Arka
providers.description: Arka is a custom packaging company that lets ecommerce brands design, order, and ship eco-friendly custom boxes, mailers, and sustainable packaging online. Arka offers low minimums, fast turnaround, and plug-in integrations with commerce platforms including Shopify, BigCommerce, and Square so merchants can reorder packaging alongside their fulfillment workflow. Arka's storefront runs on Shopify and exposes a modern agent-commerce surface — a published /llms.txt, an agentic-discovery sitemap, OIDC/OAuth 2.0 discovery for the Shopify Customer Account API, and a Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) MCP endpoint that lets AI shopping agents search the catalog, build carts, and complete buyer-approved checkouts. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and profiled here as part of the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Standard Industries
providers.description: Standard Industries is a privately-held global industrial company headquartered in New York City and tracing its origins to 1886. The company operates a portfolio of building solutions, performance materials, logistics, real estate, and investment businesses, with more than 20,000 employees and approximately $11 billion in annual revenues. Standard Building Solutions includes GAF (North America's largest roofing manufacturer), GAF Energy (Timberline Solar nailable solar shingles), BMI Group (Europe's largest pitched and flat roofing manufacturer, with brands including Braas, Monier, Icopal, Wolfin, and Redland), Siplast (specialty roofing and waterproofing for iconic structures), SGI (mining and mineral processing), Schiedel (flue, stove, and ventilation systems), and Standard Logistics. Performance Materials is anchored by W. R. Grace & Co., which produces catalysts, engineered materials, process technologies, and fine chemicals. Standard Investments deploys capital across public equities and early-to-growth venture investments. Winter Properties is a vertically integrated real estate firm with more than 100 years of history in New York City. Standard Industries does not publish a public developer API or developer portal at the corporate level; technology integration with customers and partners is handled inside the individual operating companies (most notably GAF and Grace).

providers.name: Indigo Agriculture
providers.description: Indigo Agriculture is a Boston-based agriculture-technology company combining microbial seed and foliar treatments (biotrinsic) and on-farm seed treatment hardware (CLIPS) with two large supply-chain programs: Carbon by Indigo, a soil-carbon program that pays growers for verified carbon credits using Indigo's proprietary measurement, reporting, and verification (MRV) stack; and Source by Indigo, a Scope-3 program that connects consumer-goods buyers to sustainably grown crops with greenhouse-gas, water, and low-carbon-biofuel outcome reporting. Indigo does not publish a public developer portal; partner and supply-chain integrations are negotiated directly through their team.

providers.name: Twaice
providers.description: TWAICE (TWAICE Technologies GmbH) is a Munich-based battery analytics software company. Its predictive analytics platform turns BMS data from battery energy storage systems (BESS) and electric-vehicle fleets into actionable insights for performance management, warranty management, safety monitoring, digital commissioning, and BESS reporting, alongside a battery simulation model library for engineers. Customers include BESS asset owners and operators, IPPs, utilities, automotive and bus/truck OEMs, and battery manufacturers. TWAICE is ISO 27001 certified, holds the automotive TISAX label, and is backed by investors including Creandum and Speedinvest. It publishes no public API or developer program; the platform is a closed SaaS.

providers.name: Bureau of Land Management
providers.description: The Bureau of Land Management (BLM) is a U.S. government agency responsible for managing vast stretches of public lands across the country, primarily focused on activities like outdoor recreation, livestock grazing, mineral development, and energy production, aiming to sustain the health and diversity of these lands for future generations.

providers.name: CO2 AI
providers.description: CO2 AI is an enterprise sustainability platform that helps organizations measure, reduce, and report carbon emissions across their entire value chain. It combines trustworthy emissions data, AI-powered workflows, and supply-chain collaboration to baseline and track Scope 1, 2, and 3 corporate footprints, compute audit-ready product carbon footprints (PCF) at scale across thousands of SKUs (PACT, TfS, PEF, ISO aligned), engage suppliers for primary data, and build decarbonization plans ranked by Marginal Abatement Cost. Backed by Partech and surfaced to the API Evangelist network as a climate-sector company profile. No public developer API is published as of this enrichment pass; the profile captures the company's security, trust, and legal surface.

providers.name: Spire Global
providers.description: Spire Global operates a constellation of more than 100 LEMUR nanosatellites collecting maritime AIS, aviation ADS-B, GNSS-RO weather profiles, and RF geolocation data, and offers Space Services for hosted payloads and managed satellite missions. Its data products are exposed as developer-friendly APIs: Spire Maritime 2.0 (now operated by Kpler) delivers vessel-tracking AIS through a GraphQL endpoint; Spire Aviation publishes REST APIs and real-time streams for flight metadata, live ADS-B tracking, historic positions, and event feeds; Spire Weather and Climate provides RESTful weather and ocean data APIs including 30 years of maritime weather history; and Spire Space Services exposes a developer portal for managed satellite operations. Spire's APIs are documented at product-specific subdomains and authenticated with API keys.

providers.name: Biome Makers
providers.description: Biome Makers is a global agricultural technology company founded in 2015 and headquartered in El Macero, California, that uses soil microbiome DNA sequencing and machine learning to measure and restore soil health. Its BeCrop platform decodes the functionality of soil microbial communities across 200+ crops in 56+ countries, delivering agronomic recommendations, agricultural-input validation, and supply-chain sustainability benchmarking to farmers, ag retailers, CPG companies, and research labs. Products include BeCrop Farm, BeCrop Test, BeCrop Trials, and BeCrop Rate. BeCrop is accessible via API for large-scale partner integrations, though the developer API is partner-gated and no public OpenAPI specification is currently published.

providers.name: Growatt
providers.description: Growatt New Energy is a global manufacturer of solar PV inverters, energy storage systems, and smart energy management products for residential, commercial, and utility-scale installations. Growatt operates the ShineServer / ShinePhone cloud monitoring platform and publishes a token-authenticated Open API (V1) that lets third-party systems read plant and device telemetry, retrieve historical energy data, and read or write inverter parameters for MIN (TLX) string inverters and SPH (MIX) hybrid inverters across regional endpoints. Originally surfaced as a portfolio company of IDG Capital; enriched from Growatt's public developer surface.

providers.name: Base Power
providers.description: Base Power (Base Texas REP, LLC, PUCT License #10338) is an Austin, Texas home energy company that pairs an installed home battery (40–80 kWh) with retail electricity service across Texas and Illinois. The battery powers a home automatically during outages with no manual switch and helps lower the energy bill: batteries charge when grid demand is low and send power back to the grid when demand is high (grid-balancing), and that grid revenue helps keep member energy rates low. Base can be the retail electricity provider with or without a battery, works with existing solar, and serves the Oncor, CenterPoint, AEP Texas, TNMP, CoServ, GVEC, Farmers Electric, and El Paso Electric areas in Texas plus ComEd in Illinois. Led by CEO Zach Dell and co-founder Justin Lopas; named to the TIME100 Most Influential Companies (2026); backed by Andreessen Horowitz, Lightspeed Venture Partners, Addition, Bond Capital, Ribbit Capital, and Spark Capital. This profile was enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; Base publishes no public developer API.

providers.name: Bureau of Safety and Environmental Enforcement
providers.description: The Bureau of Safety and Environmental Enforcement (BSEE) works to promote safety, protect the environment, and conserve resources offshore through vigorous regulatory oversight and enforcement.

providers.name: FlexGen Power Systems
providers.description: FlexGen Power Systems is a Durham, North Carolina energy storage technology company founded in 2009 that designs, integrates and operates grid-scale battery energy storage systems (BESS) and the software that runs them. Its flagship product is HybridOS, a hardware-agnostic energy management system (EMS) for multi-source, multi-site battery and solar portfolios, alongside HybridOS Control BMS (a US-built battery management system), a solar power plant controller (PPC), EMS retrofit, activation and lifecycle services, and data-center power solutions. FlexGen has been named a BloombergNEF Tier 1 energy storage company, acquired Clean Energy Services (CES) and the assets of Powin, and states that HybridOS exposes automated APIs and historian data API access to customers. No public developer portal, API reference or machine-readable specification is published; the HybridOS API surface is reached only through customer deployments and the login-gated FlexGen customer portal.

providers.name: Kayrros
providers.description: Kayrros is an environmental-intelligence and geospatial-AI company that independently tracks human activity and its physical footprint worldwide by combining satellite imagery, alternative data, and machine learning. Its products span energy markets — crude oil and jet fuel intelligence, LNG, renewables, solar and battery-storage construction monitoring, industrial and on-road energy demand, and stockpiles — and environmental risk — methane emissions via Methane Watch, wildfire risk, forest-carbon and deforestation monitoring, and carbon accounting. Kayrros delivers asset-level data feeds, APIs, and dashboards to traders, operators, financial institutions, regulators, insurers, and the public sector. The company was acquired by Energy Aspects in May 2026.

providers.name: Valyuu
providers.description: Valyuu is an Amsterdam-founded embedded recommerce service provider offering a plug-and-play trade-in platform that businesses integrate to buy back, resell, and recycle used consumer electronics such as smartphones, tablets, and smartwatches across Dutch, German, and English-language markets. Its partner-facing Trade-In API powers embedded trade-in flows covering device catalogs, condition questions, offers, payments, and shipping. Valyuu is a Techstars portfolio company; as of mid-2026 valyuu.com redirects to prioont.com, whose storefront is currently unreachable.

providers.name: GreenFi
providers.description: GreenFi is a climate-focused consumer financial technology company — the rebranded continuation of Aspiration's consumer banking arm. It offers a combined checking and savings account, high-yield savings with goal-based "Savings Pods", a debit card, a GreenFi Plus subscription tier, investing through its Redwood fund, and a cash-back Marketplace of sustainable brands, alongside impact programs such as Plant Your Change, tree planting and carbon offsetting. GreenFi is a financial technology company, not a bank; banking services and the debit card are provided by Coastal Community Bank, Member FDIC. Aspiration spun its consumer unit out in 2024 to Mission Financial Partners, LLC, which rebranded it GreenFi in April 2025; Coastal Financial Corporation acquired the GreenFi brand in January 2026. It is a separate company from Aspiration Partners, Inc., the enterprise carbon business that entered Chapter 11. GreenFi ships iOS, Android and web applications to end users and publishes no public developer program, API reference, or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: LevelTen Energy
providers.description: LevelTen Energy operates a two-sided digital marketplace and transaction platform for carbon-free energy, describing itself as the transaction infrastructure for the energy transition. Clean energy buyers, advisors, project developers, utilities and financiers use the LevelTen Energy Marketplace to compare thousands of power purchase agreement (PPA) offers, run NPV and settlement cashflow analysis, evaluate risk scenarios and track a Development Maturity Score across projects in North America and Europe. The platform also covers granular certificates, hybrid and storage PPAs, and performance monitoring, alongside market intelligence products including MarketPulse, the LevelTen PPA Price Index and Market Transparency Reports. The marketplace is served by an authenticated API at api.levelten.energy, which is gated behind marketplace login and publishes no public developer documentation, SDKs or machine-readable specification at this time.

providers.name: Cloover
providers.description: Cloover is a climate-fintech company building an all-in-one, "Shopify of energy" platform for the residential renewable-energy transition. It connects the stakeholders of home energy - installers, homeowners (prosumers), manufacturers, energy providers and investors - so small and mid-sized installation firms can sell, quote, finance and manage solar panels, home batteries, heat pumps and EV charging in a single package. The platform pairs installer sales and operations software with embedded financing and energy management, and offers homeowners flexible subscription and financing options. Founded in 2023 and operating primarily in Germany, Austria and wider Europe, Cloover has raised sizeable seed and Series A equity plus a large debt facility and is backed by QED Investors, MMC Ventures, Lowercarbon Capital and others.

providers.name: Descartes Labs
providers.description: Descartes Labs was a Santa Fe, New Mexico geospatial intelligence company founded in 2014 as a spin-out from Los Alamos National Laboratory. The company built the Descartes Labs Platform, a cloud-native geospatial data refinery and analytics environment combining a petabyte-scale satellite imagery archive (Landsat, Sentinel-1/2, MODIS, NAIP, PlanetScope, SkySat, commercial radar, NEXRAD weather radar, plus client-uploaded data) with a Python client library, JupyterHub-based workbench, and distributed compute for training and running deep learning and remote-sensing models at scale. Customers in agriculture, mining, energy, defense, insurance, and the U.S. government used the platform to build production geospatial machine learning pipelines covering crop forecasting, mineral exploration, infrastructure monitoring, methane detection, wildfire response, and ESG reporting. The Platform exposed a Catalog (imagery, bands, products, blobs, events), a Compute service (containerised functions, jobs, schedules), a Vector service (tabular and geospatial features), Dynamic Compute (lazy raster algebra and tiling), Auth, and a `descarteslabs` CLI. In October 2024, EarthDaily Analytics — backed by Antarctica Capital — acquired Descartes Labs and the Descartes Labs Government, Inc. subsidiary, folding the team, customers, and platform into the EarthDaily Constellation programme. The product was rebranded EarthOne in 2025; the `descarteslabs` Python package has been formally discontinued in favour of `earthdaily-earthone` (v5.x), the github.com/descarteslabs organisation has been renamed to `dlarchives`, www.descarteslabs.com is now a parked domain, and the docs.descarteslabs.com developer portal has been retired in favour of EarthDaily-hosted EarthOne documentation. This catalog entry preserves the historical Descartes Labs Platform surface as an archive — see the EarthDaily / EarthOne profile for the active product.

providers.name: Arkema
providers.description: Arkema S.A. is a French specialty materials company headquartered in La Defense, Paris and listed on Euronext Paris under ticker AKE. The group is organized around three Specialty Materials segments — Adhesive Solutions (anchored by the Bostik brand), Advanced Materials (high-performance polymers including Kynar PVDF, Rilsan polyamides, Pebax elastomers, Sartomer photocurable resins) and Coating Solutions (acrylic monomers, waterborne and solvent-borne resins, additives) — plus a smaller Intermediates business. Arkema employs roughly 21,000 people across 55 countries with about 154 production plants and 17 R&D centers, generating around EUR 9.1 billion in 2025 revenue. Strategy is anchored in materials science, decarbonization and a validated 1.5 degree SBTi pathway toward Net-Zero by 2050. Arkema does not publish a public developer portal or REST API; customer integrations and product data are exchanged through commercial sales channels, the Product Finder web UI and Safety Data Sheet downloads.

providers.name: Farmers Business Network
providers.description: Farmers Business Network (FBN) is a direct-to-farmer ag platform combining a member network, e-commerce for crop inputs (seed, chemistry, animal health), agronomy and precision analytics, financing and crop insurance, and a sustainability / Scope-3 program (Gradable). FBN Analytics ingests precision data from 60+ monitor types and integrates with John Deere Operations Center and CNH AFS Connect to pull machine, planting, application, and harvest data into the FBN platform. FBN is a Field to Market Qualified Data Management Partner via the Fieldprint API. FBN does not publish a public developer portal; partner integrations are arranged directly.

providers.name: Makersite
providers.description: Makersite is an AI-powered Product Lifecycle Intelligence platform that helps manufacturers manage product sustainability, cost, and compliance by connecting products to deep-tier supply chain, material, and chemical data. The platform automates lifecycle assessments (LCA) and product carbon footprint (PCF) calculations, supports eco-design and cost optimization, and produces regulatory reporting such as EU Taxonomy and CBAM. It integrates with enterprise CAD, ERP, and PLM systems (PTC Windchill, Siemens Teamcenter, Autodesk, ANSYS). Makersite is a portfolio company of Partech. As of this enrichment pass it publishes no public developer API or developer portal.

providers.name: RatedPower
providers.description: RatedPower, part of Enverus (ENVERUS RATEDPOWER S.L.U., Madrid, Spain), is a cloud software platform for the design and engineering of utility-scale renewable energy projects. Its pvDesign product automates solar photovoltaic (PV) plant layout, energy-yield simulation, battery energy storage system (BESS) and hybrid plant design, substation and grid-connection engineering, earthwork estimating, and bankable proposal documentation. The platform is delivered as a browser-based SaaS application (login at ratedpower.enverus.com) and reports 64,000+ projects designed and 5.1 TW of simulated capacity. No public developer API, OpenAPI definition, SDK, or developer portal is published; enterprise automation access exists only behind the authenticated application. This profile was seeded as a Techstars portfolio lead and has been run through the API Evangelist enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Sweep
providers.description: Sweep is an enterprise carbon and ESG data management platform helping large organizations measure, manage, report, and reduce their carbon emissions and broader sustainability performance across Scope 1, 2, and 3 following the GHG Protocol. Its platform centralizes sustainability data across an organization and its value chain to produce audit-ready data from a single source, covering carbon accounting, ESG disclosure, value-chain engagement with supplier portals and automated data collection, audit and assurance trails, and business intelligence with dashboards and scenario modeling. Sweep supports compliance with the CSRD, ISSB, GRI, CDP, SFDR, TCFD, UK SRS, the GHG Protocol, and US state regulation including California SB 253 and SB 261, with vertical solutions for asset managers, asset owners, private markets, banks, healthcare, manufacturing, retail, energy, and consumer goods. Sweep was named a Leader in the IDC MarketScape 2026 for Carbon Management and recognized in the Verdantix 2026 Green Quadrant. The platform exposes data ingestion via API and SFTP and integrates with ERP, procurement, and HRMS systems, but Sweep does not publish a public developer portal, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or open-source repos — API access is delivered through customer engagements rather than a self-serve developer surface.

providers.name: Vistra Corp
providers.description: Vistra Corp (NYSE: VST) is an Irving, Texas integrated retail electricity and power generation company and the largest competitive power generator in the United States, operating roughly 41,000-44,000 MW of natural gas, nuclear, coal, solar and battery storage capacity alongside a retail business serving nearly 5 million residential, commercial and industrial customers across 16 states and the District of Columbia through TXU Energy, Dynegy, Ambit Energy, Energy Harbor, Homefield Energy and U.S. Gas & Electric. Its home market is the United States, where it sits on both sides of the competitive value chain, a merchant generator selling into ERCOT, PJM, ISO-NE, NYISO, MISO and CAISO, and a retail electricity provider (REP) reselling that power to end customers. Its API posture is honestly none. No developer portal, no API subdomain and no machine-readable contract of any kind was found: developer., developers., docs., api. and data. on vistracorp.com do not resolve; /developers, /api, /docs, /data, /openapi.json, /swagger.json and /.well-known/openid-configuration all return 404; and TXU Energy's 758-URL sitemap contains no developer or API page. The United States has no consumer energy data mandate. Green Button is an NAESB/NIST ESPI standard adopted voluntarily, and TXU Energy appears on the US Department of Energy's list of "Utilities Committed to Implementing Green Button", a 2012-era commitment list and not evidence of a live endpoint. The only customer-data surface found is Download-My-Data-style export behind the TXU Energy MyAccount login, whose interval readings are themselves sourced from Smart Meter Texas, the shared ERCOT meter-data platform operated by the transmission and distribution utilities (Oncor, CenterPoint, AEP Texas, TNMP) rather than by Vistra. Because Vistra is a retailer and generator and not a wires company, the third-party interval-data API in its home Texas market belongs to Smart Meter Texas and not to Vistra. Vistra likewise publishes no open market or grid data of its own; ERCOT, the other ISOs/RTOs and the EIA publish the market data about Vistra's fleet. Both sides are therefore closed at the company boundary. Not to be confused with Vistra Limited (vistra.com), the unrelated corporate-services and fund-administration firm that does run a real API developer portal at devportal.vistra.com.

providers.name: Archive
providers.description: Archive is a brand-owned resale and recommerce technology platform, founded in 2021, that lets forward-thinking global brands launch and scale profitable, sustainable resale businesses. Its circularity platform spans branded recommerce storefronts, peer-to-peer marketplaces, trade-in (online and in-store), take-back, warranty and repair, a resale warehouse management system (WMS), a unified product catalog, a dynamic pricing engine, and analytics — reclaiming supply through returns, past-season inventory, consumer listings, and in-store trade-ins. Archive serves 50+ brands across 10+ countries, including The North Face, lululemon, Peloton, New Balance, Dr. Martens, Fjällräven, Oscar de la Renta, Hanna Andersson, and Faherty. The company is backed by Bain Capital Ventures and Lightspeed Venture Partners (with Energize Capital leading its $30M Series B), and has raised $54M to date.

providers.name: Aunt Flow
providers.description: Aunt Flow is a woman-owned company on a mission to end period poverty by making menstrual products freely accessible in public restrooms the same way toilet paper is. It manufactures and sells free-vend period product dispensers (models P, E, R, and O), organic cotton tampons and pads, touch-free disposal systems, and retail display boxes, serving schools, universities, offices, airports, stadiums, ski resorts, restaurants, health systems, amusement parks, and coworking spaces. Since 2021 the company has donated over 6 million period products to people in need. Aunt Flow is a physical-products and e-commerce business (Techstars-backed) with no public developer API surface; this profile captures its identity, commercial links, and domain-security posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Clarity AI
providers.description: Clarity AI is a sustainability technology and fintech company that provides AI-powered extra-financial intelligence for financial decision-making. Its platform delivers ESG risk ratings, climate and physical-risk analytics, regulatory-compliance reporting (EU Taxonomy, SFDR, MiFID II, ESMA fund naming, Pillar 3), impact and UN SDG alignment, and retail-banking climate engagement tools. Clarity AI reports coverage of 300K+ listed and private companies, 450K+ funds, and 400+ sovereigns, and serves asset managers, asset owners, banks, wealth managers, and corporates. The company exposes its data through a web application, data feeds, APIs, and emerging AI agent / MCP integrations, though its developer surface is gated behind an enterprise platform login rather than a public developer portal. Clarity AI is a portfolio company of the SoftBank Vision Fund. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Mainspring Energy
providers.description: Mainspring Energy is a Menlo Park, California power-infrastructure company that designs, manufactures, and deploys the Linear Generator, a modular, fuel-flexible onsite power generation system. Its technology delivers firm, dispatchable, and low-emission electricity for data centers, utilities, and industrial and enterprise facilities, running today on natural gas and biogas with a seamless transition to zero-carbon fuels such as hydrogen and ammonia. Backed by Khosla Ventures and other investors, Mainspring has more than one gigawatt of Linear Generator capacity in late-stage development and operation. Mainspring is a hardware and power-systems company and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile captures its corporate, security, and compliance surface.

providers.name: Tracera
providers.description: Tracera (formerly ESG Flo) is an AI-powered corporate sustainability and ESG data platform that automates the collection, verification, auditing, and reporting of sustainability data with finance-grade accuracy and traceability. The platform extracts audit-ready metrics from raw data across PDFs, spreadsheets, and ERP systems for 900+ metrics, supports reporting frameworks including CSRD, SEC, GRI, and CDP, and serves Fortune 2000 enterprises across manufacturing, real estate, construction, retail, technology, and healthcare (customers include EnerSys, La-Z-Boy, Sauder Woodworking, and Putzmeister). Founded in 2022 and based in New York, Tracera raised a $12M Series A in April 2025 led by Foundry with Rho Ignition, Tola Capital, and Contour Venture Partners ($17.25M total). Enrichment probing found no public developer API, developer portal, SDKs, or event surface; the website is bot-gated by a SiteGround captcha.

providers.name: Amperecloud
providers.description: Amperecloud (Amperecloud GmbH) is a German renewable-energy management software company whose cloud platform provides an operating system for monitoring, operating, and commercially managing solar, wind, and other renewable-energy assets at scale. The platform brings asset performance monitoring, maintenance and ticket management, commercial and technical asset management, and virtual power plant (VPP) capabilities into a single system, supported by migration, consulting, and custom-integration services. It is used by more than 300 customers worldwide managing over 8,000 installations and 10+ GWp of capacity. Added to the API Evangelist network as a point-nine portfolio company; no public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer portal is currently published, so this profile captures verified company identity and a domain-security probe pending any future public API surface.

providers.name: Clean Harbors
providers.description: Clean Harbors is the largest provider of environmental and industrial services in North America, delivering hazardous and non-hazardous waste management, emergency response, industrial cleaning, environmental remediation, and used-oil and solvent recycling through its Safety-Kleen subsidiary. Clean Harbors does not publish a public developer portal or general-purpose REST API surface; programmatic interfaces are limited to the authenticated customer portal at clhsaas.cleanharbors.com (CLH SaaS) for service requests, manifests, and reporting, and partner-mediated EDI feeds. Customers also use the EPA e-Manifest system for federally regulated hazardous-waste manifest tracking.

providers.name: Matthews International
providers.description: Matthews International Corporation (NASDAQ: MATW) is a Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania diversified manufacturer founded in 1850 and reporting in three segments. Memorialization covers bronze and granite memorials, caskets, cremation-related products and cremation and incineration equipment for the cemetery and funeral home industries, sold through Matthews Aurora Funeral Solutions and Matthews Environmental Solutions. Industrial Technologies covers product identification — the Matthews Marking Systems marking and coding business and its MPERIA controller platform — plus the design, manufacture and service of custom energy storage solutions including dry-battery-electrode coating and converting lines. Brand Solutions is now a 40% ownership interest in Propelis Group, the entity formed on 1 May 2025 when Matthews contributed the majority of its SGK brand business; the company sold its warehouse automation business (Matthews Automation Solutions — Pyramid, Compass and Lightning Pick) to Duravant on 31 December 2025. Matthews is a manufacturer rather than a software vendor: it operates no public developer program and publishes no API documentation, SDK, package, CLI, MCP server, agent card or machine-readable specification. The MPERIA controller sold with its marking and coding equipment markets a "common API" for ERP, WMS, MES and PLC integration, but that is an on-premises XML or command-line protocol carried over Ethernet or RS-232 and documented only in sales collateral — not a public web API.

providers.name: Tem
providers.description: Tem (Tem-Energy Limited) is a UK-based energy technology company building AI-native transaction infrastructure for a modern energy market. Its RED platform is a modern utility that removes wholesale market markups to cut business electricity costs by up to 30%, provides transparent line-by-line billing from half-hourly meter data, and gives generators fairer earnings with renewable-energy traceability across 6,000+ sites. Backed by a February 2026 GBP 55M Series B led by Lightspeed Venture Partners. The customer-facing platform runs at app.tem.energy behind an OIDC login; the platform API at api.tem.energy is a private AWS API Gateway with no publicly documented developer surface at the time of profiling.

providers.name: Brandback
providers.description: Brandback is a Berlin-based embedded resale infrastructure company (legal entity Arbor Technologies GmbH) that lets online retailers and fashion brands integrate resale directly into their baskets, product listings, and checkouts. Shoppers see an item's future resale value before they buy, resell it later in a single click, and receive store credit, while Brandback's AI handles pricing recommendations, condition checks, customer service, shipping, disputes, and payouts. Retailers can launch a white-label resale marketplace with no upfront cost and integrate with any e-commerce platform. Founded in 2023 and backed by $7.4M in pre-seed and seed funding led by Earlybird VC, Brandback reports a 9.5% average conversion-rate lift with customers including Replay Jeans and Sandqvist.

providers.name: CHAOSS
providers.description: CHAOSS (Community Health Analytics in Open Source Software) is a Linux Foundation project that develops metrics, methodologies, software, and practitioner guides for measuring and improving open source community health and sustainability. It produces a metrics catalog organized into focus areas (Common, DEI, Risk, Value, Evolution) and metrics models, along with open source software (Augur, 8Knot, GrimoireLab) that ingests data from Git, GitHub, GitLab, mailing lists, and other community platforms to compute the metrics. CHAOSS-aligned SaaS services such as OSS Compass and Bitergia Analytics also expose the metrics for adopters who do not want to host the software themselves.

providers.name: Remoov
providers.description: Remoov is a San Francisco-based full-service removal, resale, donation, and recycling company that helps households and businesses declutter by picking up unwanted furniture and goods, then reselling them on consignment (via reperch.com), donating them to charities, or recycling them responsibly. Customers schedule a pickup, receive a quote, and earn a share of resale proceeds. Remoov also serves realtors, stagers, property managers, and living communities as partners. Backed by 500 Global. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead; Remoov publishes a consumer web app and help desk but no public developer API.

providers.name: Resourcify
providers.description: Resourcify (Resourcify GmbH) is a Hamburg, Germany based digital platform for waste management and circular-economy operations, describing itself as "the operating system for a circular future." Its cloud software helps enterprises digitize and optimize their waste streams end to end - automating waste and recycling operations, optimizing cost, CO2 and recycling rates, tracking compliance, and running take-back systems - across manufacturing, construction, retail, healthcare, and airports. The platform connects waste producers with a network of recyclers and haulers, captures waste data and documentation, and reports on sustainability and material recovery. Resourcify is backed by Speedinvest. As of this profile the company exposes no public developer API, API documentation, or developer portal; integrations are delivered as managed connections rather than a self-serve API.

providers.name: Sighten
providers.description: Sighten was a San Francisco software company, backed by Obvious Ventures, that built a cloud platform for the residential and commercial solar industry — covering system design, proposal generation, sales, and financing workflows used by solar installers, dealers, and finance providers. The Sighten business was acquired (by GoodLeap) and folded into EverBright; the original sighten.io domain now redirects to goeverbright.com. EverBright operates as a residential solar and home-battery financing platform, connecting homeowners with local installers through lease and Power Purchase Agreement (PPA) products and the MyEverBright monitoring portal. No public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation is published for the Sighten or EverBright brand; a partner-facing platform (engine.goeverbright.com) and a protected API host (api.goeverbright.com, HTTP 401) exist but are not publicly documented. This profile records the company's current, honest public surface after enrichment.

providers.name: Agreena
providers.description: Agreena is a Copenhagen-based agtech and climate finance company, founded in 2021, that helps farmers transition to regenerative agriculture and monetize the resulting soil-carbon outcomes. Its AgreenaCarbon platform combines farmer enrollment, a satellite-, AI-, and soil-sampling-based digital measurement, reporting and verification (dMRV) engine, and Verra-certified carbon credit issuance. Agreena also offers standalone remote-sensing products such as a field-boundary-detection API for agrifood supply-chain monitoring. The platform spans roughly 5 million hectares and 2,500+ farmers across ~20 European countries. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Anthemis and HV Capital and is being enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; Agreena publishes no public developer portal or OpenAPI surface at this time.

providers.name: Certa
providers.description: Certa (operated by Opinr, Inc. d/b/a Certa) is an AI-native third-party risk management (TPRM) and compliance platform that unifies the full third-party lifecycle — onboarding, due diligence, contract management, continuous compliance monitoring, and offboarding — in a single no-code system. Founded by Jag Lamba and headquartered in Saratoga, CA, Certa serves Fortune 500 companies (Honeywell, Uber, Mars, Box, Quantcast) across 120+ countries and 17 languages. The platform covers all risk domains — operational and resilience, infosec and cyber, compliance and legal, financial and credit, reputational, geopolitical, and ESG and ethical risk — via its Studio no-code process designer, Certa Connect (130+ native integrations), and embedded AI agents. Certa was named a Leader in the inaugural 2026 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Third-Party Risk Management Tools. External integration is available through an enterprise external API surfaced from the platform; no public OpenAPI or developer portal is published as of this profile.

providers.name: Goodr
providers.description: Goodr is an Atlanta-based sustainable surplus food management and hunger-relief logistics company founded in 2016 by Jasmine Crowe-Houston. Goodr helps businesses divert edible and inedible food waste from landfills by scheduling pickups, donating surplus edible food to local nonprofits, and providing donors with the tax deductions and impact reporting tied to those donations. Alongside its food-waste solutions, Goodr runs hunger-relief programs including pop-up grocery markets, meal delivery, student snackpacks, and community grocery stores. The company reports more than 30 million meals served and 4 million pounds of food diverted from landfills for enterprise partners such as Amazon, Google, NASA, and Fulton County. Goodr operates through a partner portal rather than a public developer API; this profile tracks its public web properties in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Cladwell
providers.description: Cladwell is a smart-closet and outfit-planning consumer application that helps people build capsule wardrobes and get more wear out of the clothes they already own. The service digitizes a user's closet, then uses AI styling ("Ask Cladwell") together with weather and personal preferences to recommend daily outfits, reduce over-buying, and encourage sustainable, intentional dressing. With more than one million app downloads, Cladwell is delivered primarily as iOS/Android and web apps (app.cladwell.com) with a subscription model; it currently exposes no public developer API. Founded and led by CEO Erin Flynn, it was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment tracking.

providers.name: METYCLE
providers.description: METYCLE is a Cologne, Germany-based digital B2B marketplace and AI-powered trading platform for the international secondary (scrap) metal industry, connecting suppliers and buyers of recycled metals - copper, aluminum, zinc, nickel, lead and magnesium - across borders. Operated by METYCLE GmbH and led by managing directors Rafael Suchan and Sebastian Brenner, the company raised a 14.1M euro Series A round to expand its platform for transparent, sustainable global metal trade and to advance circular-economy sourcing of secondary metals. Its customer platform supports biddable listings, product discovery and trade execution. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a company/provider record; METYCLE currently exposes no public developer API.

providers.name: Rondo Energy
providers.description: Rondo Energy is an Alameda, California industrial decarbonization company led by CEO John O'Donnell that builds the Rondo Heat Battery (RHB), a thermal energy storage system that converts intermittent wind and solar electricity into heat stored in thousands of tons of refractory brick at temperatures up to 1,500C and returns it as continuous steam, thermal oil, superheated air, or combined heat and power at rated outputs from 2MWth to over 100MWth. The RHB is sold as a drop-in replacement for a fossil-fuel boiler, via capital purchase, lease, or heat purchase agreement, into cement, food and beverage, chemicals, fuels and ethanol, textiles, pulp and paper, mining, pharmaceuticals, and direct air capture. Rondo operates the world's largest industrial heat battery and has announced a 90GWh factory plan with Siam Cement Group, backed by Breakthrough Energy Ventures and Catalyst, Energy Impact Partners, Microsoft's Climate Innovation Fund, Rio Tinto, SABIC, Aramco Ventures, and the European Investment Bank. Rondo sells hardware and delivered heat, not software: it publishes no developer portal, API reference, or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Sunairio
providers.description: Sunairio is a grid forecasting company that provides integrated weather, climate, and energy insights for power markets. Its flagship platform, Sunairio ONE, generates 1,000-member ensemble forecasts across horizons from hourly to decadal, capturing extreme-weather and grid-stress scenarios that traditional forecasts miss. The company also publishes SHED (Sunairio High-resolution Earth Data), a proprietary historical weather dataset for the Continental US from 1950 to present at roughly 100x the resolution of ERA5, with asset-level wind and solar variability. Customers such as energy traders, grid operators, utility-scale asset developers, and demand-response aggregators access forecasts and data through a web UI, an API, and (on higher tiers) direct Snowflake data delivery. Founded in 2020 by Rob Cirincione, the company has been recognized by the National Science Foundation, American Clean Power, and EPRI.

providers.name: Booster Fuels
providers.description: Booster (Booster Fuels, Inc.) is a mobile energy delivery company that brings gasoline, diesel, diesel exhaust fluid (DEF), and renewable fuel alternatives directly to vehicles, fleets, and on-site fuel tanks using a fleet of Smart Tankers, removing the need for drivers to visit gas stations. The company serves enterprise fleets and local businesses across the United States, pairing on-demand fueling with a proprietary technology platform (BoosterOS / the Fleet dashboard at fleet.trybooster.com) for real-time fleet management, fuel-usage reporting, invoicing automation, fraud prevention, and emissions reduction. Booster offers custom enterprise integrations (ERP, CRM, and telematics such as Geotab and Samsara) but does not publish a public developer API portal, OpenAPI definition, or SDKs. This profile is a company/lead entry in the API Evangelist network; no public API surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Gireve
providers.description: Gireve is a B2B digital platform for electric-vehicle charging and new-mobility services, connecting charge point operators (CPOs), e-mobility service providers (eMSPs), and EV drivers across Europe. Its interoperability hub powers EV charging roaming, clearing and transaction settlement, Plug & Charge, smart charging, and mobility data services, spanning 680,000+ connected charging points and roughly one million monthly roaming transactions across 13,000+ signed agreements. Technical integration is delivered to connected operators over an OCPI-based hub through the Connect Place B2B platform; Gireve does not publish a public self-serve developer portal or OpenAPI specification.

providers.name: Go To-U
providers.description: GO TO-U is an operating system for electric-vehicle charging management, built for Charge Point Operators (CPOs) and businesses that run charging infrastructure. The platform is hardware-agnostic, integrating with 50+ charger manufacturers (ABB, Wallbox, Siemens, EVBox and others), and bundles charge-point management, AI-powered analytics and load optimization, a driver-facing mobile app (iOS and Android), roaming, white-label options, and integrated payment processing. Its Advanced Reservation Technology (ART) lets drivers book charging slots in advance to reduce wait times. GO TO-U is a Techstars portfolio company. This profile was enriched from the company's public website; no public developer/API documentation, SDKs, or machine-readable API specifications were discoverable at the time of enrichment.

providers.name: Plans
providers.description: Plans (plans.app, formerly lun.energy) is a climate-technology company focused on decarbonising the built world. It removes the friction that stands in the way of transitioning homes to low-carbon energy faster, letting professionals capture building data on a mobile device, analyze it, and produce retrofit / energy plans — "capture, analyze, plan, all in your pocket." A web platform (platform.plans.app) and a Chrome extension support the workflow, and the product is offered across English, Danish, and French markets. Plans is backed by Partech. No public developer API has been identified during enrichment; the platform is a login-gated single-page application and the site exposes no OpenAPI, SDKs, docs, or developer portal.

providers.name: Replenysh
providers.description: Replenysh is an enterprise circularity platform that runs circular supply chains for brands and recovery facilities. It routes, recovers, verifies, and optimizes material recovery flows across a network of 5,000+ partners, giving enterprises a single control layer for reverse logistics with audit-ready chain-of-custody, pricing, settlement, and compliance documentation. Customers include PepsiCo, Disney, Marriott, and Live Nation. Backed by Kindred Ventures and M13. Surfaced as a portfolio-lead stub and enriched via the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: Aclima
providers.description: Aclima is a San Francisco-based environmental intelligence company that maps and analyzes air pollution and greenhouse gas emissions at hyperlocal, block-by-block resolution. Using a network of roving (vehicle-mounted) and stationary sensors, Aclima measures multiple pollutants and climate gases simultaneously at up to 100,000x greater resolution than traditional monitoring, then translates billions of scientific measurements into environmental intelligence for governments, companies, and communities. Its professional analytics software, Aclima Pro, delivers visualization and automated analytics for emissions reduction and public-health programs, while its free air.health app maps address-level air and climate insights for the communities Aclima serves. Co-founded by CEO Davida Herzl, Aclima is backed by DCVC and is added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment.

providers.name: trawa
providers.description: trawa (operated by Future Energy Services GmbH) is a Berlin-based energy management company that helps mid-sized businesses procure and manage electricity. It pairs AI-optimized green-electricity sourcing on the wholesale market with cloud energy-management software that gives customers real-time visibility into consumption, costs, and CO2 emissions, alongside battery storage and smart control of energy-consuming assets such as CHP plants and charging stations. Founded in 2022, trawa is backed by Balderton Capital and Speedinvest. The platform is delivered through a customer web portal and a trust center; no public developer API was found as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Last Energy
providers.description: Last Energy is an American developer and operator of micro-modular nuclear power plants, founded in 2019 in Washington, D.C. by Bret Kugelmass as a commercial spinout of the Energy Impact Center. Its flagship PWR-20 is a 20 MWe pressurized water reactor assembled from a few dozen factory-made, steel-encased modules that ship to site and are installed rather than constructed in place. Last Energy sells power rather than reactors: it designs, finances, owns and operates plants under long-term power purchase agreements for energy-intensive customers including data centers, metals, chemicals, cement, pulp and paper, and food and beverage. The company has announced projects in Texas, South Wales, Poland and Romania, entered nuclear site licensing in the United Kingdom, partnered with Texas A&M and DP World, and raised roughly $164M across a $40M Series B and a $100M Series C. Last Energy publishes a marketing site and a gated customer/whitepaper portal, but no public developer program, API, or machine-readable interface.

providers.name: Lightship
providers.description: Lightship is an American manufacturer of all-electric travel trailers, co-founded by former Tesla leaders Toby Kraus and Ben Parker, with design and manufacturing in Colorado and offices in San Francisco. Its flagship product, the AE.1, is marketed as the first mass-produced all-electric travel trailer, offering up to 77 kWh of battery capacity, 1.8 kW of integrated solar, and named technologies including TrekDrive self-propulsion, CampQuiet silent operation, and Aero-Electric Design. Owners control the trailer through an onboard Atlas tablet and companion mobile app. Lightship sells direct to consumer and states that more than 85% of its supply chain is in the United States. Enrichment probes on 2026-07-19 found no public API, developer portal, SDK, or /.well-known/ discovery surface; this is a company record in the API Evangelist network rather than an API listing.

providers.name: Ecovadis
providers.description: Ecovadis is a global leader in providing sustainability ratings and performance improvement tools for companies looking to assess and improve their environmental and social practices. Their platform helps organizations evaluate the sustainability performance of their suppliers, partners, and vendors, enabling them to make more informed decisions when it comes to selecting business partners.

providers.name: Arbor
providers.description: Arbor is a consumer energy savings service operating in deregulated electricity markets across 13 states in the U.S. Northeast, Midwest, and Texas. The Arbor app analyzes a household's current electricity supply rate, matches the customer with vetted alternative suppliers, and automatically switches them to a lower-cost plan when one becomes available, all without changing the utility provider, interrupting service, or charging the customer. Arbor earns revenue through referral fees from energy suppliers rather than from consumers. Founded in 2022 by Andrew Meyer (previously co-founder of Swell Energy), Arbor is backed by First Round Capital, Obvious Ventures, Spring Tide Capital, and Blisce. Arbor is a consumer-facing application and does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, or technical documentation.

providers.name: Astronergy
providers.description: Astronergy (Chint New Energy Technology Co., Ltd.) is the photovoltaic cell and module manufacturing arm of China's CHINT Group. Founded in 2006, it is one of the earliest private Chinese enterprises in the PV sector and is ranked among the world's largest module suppliers. It designs, manufactures and sells high-efficiency crystalline-silicon PV cells and modules — notably the n-type TOPCon ASTRO N series in bifacial and monofacial form — for utility-scale power stations, commercial and industrial rooftops, and residential systems. Astronergy sells into more than 140 countries and regions and operates manufacturing bases and sales centers in markets including Germany, Spain, the USA, Brazil and Turkey. Its public web surface is a marketing and product-download site: datasheets, installation manuals, warranty and certification PDFs, a module-authenticity checker and a PV Planner yield calculator. It publishes no developer program, API documentation or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Enurgen
providers.description: Enurgen is a solar energy software company whose DUET platform uses 3D physics-based modeling to optimize photovoltaic assets across their entire lifecycle. The platform spans three products - Design, Construction, and Operations - helping large-scale solar developers, independent power producers, EPC engineers, and asset managers improve energy yield estimates, validate construction against expected performance, and monitor plants in production to close the gap between forecasted (P50) and actual field output. Enurgen is a Techstars-backed company; customers include Scatec, Potentia, Lightsource, Eni, and Kiewit. The company operates a customer web application at app.enurgen.com but does not currently publish a public developer API, documentation, or SDKs. This API Evangelist profile is an enrichment pass that captures the company's public web properties and domain security posture.

providers.name: Fuse
providers.description: Fuse Energy is a UK retail energy supplier providing gas and electricity to homes and businesses, alongside EV charging, solar and battery storage tracking with grid export, and smart home energy management. The company emphasises savings against the UK price cap, a fast (~3 minute) online sign-up, automated supplier switching, and 24/7 customer support including an AI assistant called "Plugs". Fuse was surfaced as a portfolio company of Accel and Speedinvest and added to the API Evangelist network. It operates a consumer/business energy web and mobile experience and does not publish a public developer API program at this time.

providers.name: Fuse Energy
providers.description: Fuse Energy (Fuse Energy Supply Limited) is a UK-based residential and business energy supplier providing gas and electricity on variable, fixed, and multi-rate tariffs, alongside EV charging, solar and battery export tracking, multi-property account management, and an in-app AI energy assistant called Plugs. The company positions itself around beating the UK energy price cap, sign-up in under three minutes, and 24-hour customer support. It operates a consumer- and business-facing web and mobile app experience and publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDKs at this time.

providers.name: Invesdor
providers.description: Invesdor is a pan-European crowdinvesting and digital investment platform that connects private and professional investors with companies raising capital through equity, subordinated loans, and bonds, with minimum tickets starting around EUR 250. Founded in Finland in 2012 and expanded through mergers with Finnest, Kapilendo, and Oneplanetcrowd, Invesdor now serves more than 180,000 investors across Europe and has channeled over EUR 600 million into more than 1,000 renewable-energy, scale-up, and SME financing rounds. It operates as a regulated investment firm under the EU Crowdfunding Service Provider (ECSP) regime. Invesdor does not currently publish a public developer API or developer portal; this profile tracks its public web, investor, and legal surface in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Orbio
providers.description: Orbio Earth is a climate-tech company (founded 2021; Dover, Delaware, USA and Cologne, Germany) that turns open satellite data into industrial methane intelligence for the energy sector. Its platform detects, quantifies, and tracks methane emissions from oil-and-gas infrastructure globally at asset level with a roughly 5-day revisit rate, using multispectral imagery (Sentinel-2, Landsat 8/9, EMIT) and machine learning, plus Bayesian uncertainty estimation. Customers — oil-and-gas operators and private-equity firms — use it for super-emitter identification, historical trend and root-cause analysis, and compliance with emerging methane regulation. Platform access is offered via the web application or a sales-gated data API integration; there is no public self-serve developer portal, OpenAPI, or SDK. Orbio also publishes the open-source Project Eucalyptus methane-detection pipelines on GitHub for research use.

providers.name: Overstory
providers.description: Overstory provides AI-powered vegetation intelligence for electric utilities and grid operators. The platform fuses high-resolution satellite and aerial imagery with machine learning to detect vegetation encroachment, hazard trees, and wildfire risk along power line corridors, helping utilities prioritize trimming, optimize vegetation management spend, and improve grid reliability (SAIDI). Overstory was founded as 20tree.ai and surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a Techstars portfolio company. As of this profile the company delivers its intelligence through a customer platform and services rather than a public developer API; no public API documentation, OpenAPI, or developer portal was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Runwise
providers.description: Runwise provides wireless smart-control systems that automate heating, cooling, water, and gas infrastructure in multifamily and commercial buildings. Its retrofit hardware and cloud platform replace legacy boiler, steam, and HVAC controls, cutting heating, cooling, and water bills by roughly 23% with same-day installation. Runwise reports more than 10,300 buildings under management and over $175 million in cumulative utility savings for customers. The company is backed by Fifth Wall, Initialized Capital, and Menlo Ventures. This API Evangelist profile tracks Runwise's public web presence; as of this pass no public API, developer portal, or programmatic integration surface has been identified.

providers.name: Epsor
providers.description: Epsor is a French fintech, founded in 2017, that manages employee savings and retirement plans (épargne salariale et retraite) for companies and helps them turn that benefit into an HR lever. A certified B Corp and mission-driven company, Epsor ranks among the top 10 employee-savings and retirement providers in France and serves more than 2,500 corporate clients. It targets HR, Compensation & Benefits, and Finance teams at mid-size and large French firms, combining a pedagogical, personalized saver experience, an open-architecture fund range (40+ funds from 15+ asset managers, with a strong ESG/SRI focus), and year-round support to run and promote the plan. Epsor is neither an asset manager nor a bank: it is the single point of contact for companies and their employees, and delegates account-keeping to Société Générale Securities Services (SGSS). Products span PEE, PER Collectif (PERECO), PER Obligatoire, intéressement, participation, abondement, and employee share ownership. Epsor exposes no public developer API; this profile captures its public identity and security posture for the API Evangelist network.
