This API Evangelist profile tracks Aalo Atomics as a company in the network; the company does not currently publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Advano
providers.description: Advano is a New Orleans, Louisiana battery-materials company that develops silicon-based anode materials for lithium-ion batteries. Spun out of Tulane University in 2016 and backed by 25+ patents, its flagship REALSi silicon-carbon composite is engineered as a drop-in replacement for graphite anodes, delivering up to 9x the energy density of graphite for electric vehicles, consumer electronics, defense, and grid energy storage. Advano's process avoids hazardous silane gas, uses abundant metallurgical-grade silicon, and runs on existing manufacturing equipment. The company operates a pilot plant in New Orleans East and is scaling toward 3,000 tons of REALSi in 2026 and 20,000 tons by 2030. This is a physical deep-tech manufacturer with no public API or developer platform; it is catalogued in the API Evangelist network as a VC portfolio company profile.

providers.name: Aiko Solar
providers.description: Aiko Solar (Zhejiang Aiko Solar Energy Co.) is a solar photovoltaic manufacturer specializing in high-efficiency solar cells and modules, best known for its ABC (All Back Contact) module technology for residential, commercial, industrial, and utility-scale applications. A BloombergNEF Tier 1 manufacturer, the company reports 200 GW+ accumulative cell and module shipments and mass-production cell efficiency around 25%. This is a hardware manufacturer with no public developer or API surface; the profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record.

providers.name: Amogy
providers.description: Amogy is an energy-technology company decarbonizing hard-to-electrify sectors by converting energy-dense ammonia into dispatchable, zero-carbon electricity. Its AMMDrive power systems crack ammonia into hydrogen and nitrogen and convert the hydrogen to power for data centers, industrial facilities, microgrids, and maritime vessels, and it develops proprietary low-temperature ammonia-cracking catalysts. Backed by DCVC and other investors, Amogy has demonstrated the world's first carbon-free ammonia-powered maritime vessel and partners with firms such as Samsung Heavy Industries and Mitsubishi. This is a company profile in the API Evangelist network; Amogy publishes no public developer API surface at this time, so this record captures its corporate identity and public web properties rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: Bloom Energy
providers.description: Bloom Energy Corporation (NYSE: BE) is a San Jose, California hardtech company that designs and manufactures solid-oxide fuel cell "Energy Server" platforms which generate electricity on-site from natural gas, biogas, or hydrogen through an electrochemical process rather than combustion. Its modular systems deliver resilient, always-on power for data centers, manufacturing, healthcare, utilities, and critical infrastructure, can be deployed in roughly 90 days, and scale from single units to hundreds of megawatts. Bloom also builds high-temperature solid-oxide electrolyzers for low-cost hydrogen production. The company is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a hardtech portfolio company; it publishes no public developer API surface at this time.

providers.name: Bolt.Earth
providers.description: Bolt.Earth operates what it describes as India's largest EV charging network, with more than 100,000 charging points deployed across 2,100+ cities. The company sells EV charging hardware (3.3kW smart sockets for 2/3/4-wheelers, AC chargers from 7.4kW to 22kW, and DC fast chargers from 30kW to 240kW) alongside a Charging Management System (CMS) for operators and a consumer mobile app for locating, booking, and paying for charging sessions. Services span site assessment, installation, KYC onboarding, charger activation, remote firmware updates, and 24/7 support for individuals, RWAs, enterprises, fleet operators, hospitality venues, highways, and government agencies. Bolt.Earth is backed by Version One Ventures and is tracked in the API Evangelist network as an energy-sector company profile. No public developer API portal or OpenAPI definition was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Capstone Turbine
providers.description: Capstone Turbine Corporation, now operating as Capstone Green Energy (and its operating entity Capstone Energy+), is a California-based manufacturer of low-emission microturbine energy systems founded in 1988. The company designs and builds oil-free, air-bearing microturbines ranging from 65 kW to multi-megawatt configurations for on-site and on-demand power, combined heat and power (CHP), and combined cooling, heat and power (CCHP). Its systems power data centers, microgrids, ports, EV charging, oil and gas operations, critical power, and renewable energy applications. Capstone was surfaced as a portfolio company of Canaan Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. It is an industrial energy manufacturer with no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile captures company identity and public web properties only.

providers.name: Ceibo
providers.description: Ceibo is a Chilean copper technology company accelerating access to copper supply through a proprietary leaching process that recovers copper from primary sulfide ores. Backed by Khosla Ventures and BHP Ventures, the company positions its on-site technology as faster than bioleaching, using less water than concentration and a fraction of the capital expenditure of concentrators, aiming to close the global copper supply-demand gap needed for the energy transition. Headquartered in Santiago, Chile, Ceibo was named a 2026 Fast Company World Changing Ideas winner. This is a company profile in the API Evangelist network; Ceibo publishes no public developer/API surface at this time.

providers.name: E-Peas
providers.description: e-peas is a Belgian fabless semiconductor company founded in 2014 in Louvain-la-Neuve that designs power management integrated circuits (PMICs) for energy harvesting, enabling battery-free and battery-assisted IoT devices to power themselves from ambient energy. Its flagship Ambient Energy Manager (AEM) family harvests from photovoltaic (light), thermal, vibration/piezoelectric, radio-frequency, and hybrid multi-source inputs, and the company also develops ultra-low-power microcontrollers for autonomous data acquisition. e-peas positions itself as a pioneer of the "Ambient IoT" concept serving smart buildings, industrial IoT, consumer electronics, and wearables, with an ecosystem of 30+ partners including Panasonic, TDK, Vishay, and Silicon Labs. This is a hardware/silicon company that does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or API documentation.

providers.name: Eastman Chemical
providers.description: Driven by more than 100 years of continuous innovation, Eastman is a global Fortune 500 specialty materials company that produces a broad range of advanced materials, chemicals, and fibers used in everyday products. Eastman operates a customer-facing Customer Center for orders, documents, and Safety Data Sheets, but no public developer portal or REST API has been documented.

providers.name: Enter
providers.description: Enter is a Berlin-based residential energy-efficiency company that positions itself as Germany's largest energy advisor, combining on-site building analysis with installation of heat pumps, photovoltaic (solar) systems, battery storage, EV wallboxes, and home energy-management systems. It guides homeowners through energy consulting, subsidy (Foerderung) applications, and financing, and reports 37,000+ completed projects and 150M+ EUR in secured subsidies. Enter is a B2C service provider with no public developer API, documentation portal, or SDKs; it was surfaced as a VC-portfolio lead and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment.

providers.name: Explomar
providers.description: ExploMar (Changshu, China) designs and manufactures high-power fully-electric outboard propulsion systems for boats, ranging from 70HP to 1200HP. Its product line spans lightweight axial-flux electric outboard motors, high-density marine batteries for long-range and wide-temperature operation, the Smart Captain integrated control system with 200+ diagnostic capabilities, and 5S energy/charging stations (7kW portable through 120kW dual-gun). ExploMar markets an eco-friendly, high-performance alternative to combustion marine propulsion and exhibits at international yachting festivals (Cannes, Monaco, Interboot, Polboat). Backed by DCM Ventures; surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company. Note: ExploMar is a marine hardware manufacturer and publishes no public developer API, documentation, or SDKs at this time — this profile carries identity and web-property signals only.

providers.name: Fazla Gida
providers.description: Fazla (formerly Fazla Gida / Whole Surplus) is a Turkish technology-driven waste management and circular-economy company founded in 2017 in Istanbul. Its digital, decision-support platform helps B2B clients across the supply chain — manufacturers, retailers, e-commerce, distributors, HoReCa, food banks and municipalities — prevent waste at the source and recover value from surplus inventory through a food-recovery hierarchy of secondary-sales marketplace, donation, animal-feed conversion and recycling modules, backed by logistics support, a smart-scale IoT inventory system and an AI analysis tool that reports financial, CO2 and social impact. The company operates the Fazla Iyi surprise-box consumer app, is the first B Corp-certified waste-management organization in Turkey, and is backed by 500 Global among other investors.

providers.name: Forum Mobility
providers.description: Forum Mobility develops, owns, and operates zero-emission heavy-duty trucking infrastructure, bundling electric Class 8 truck leases with charging subscriptions for a single monthly price so freight carriers of every size can electrify without upfront capital. The company builds and runs a network of charging depots — anchored by its flagship FM Harbor site at the Port of Long Beach (44 ports, 360KW fast chargers, 9MW capacity) — with additional depots in development across California and Nevada. Forum Mobility was surfaced as a portfolio company of obvious-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network. It is a physical-infrastructure operator with no public developer/API surface at this time; this profile captures its identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Mazama Energy
providers.description: Mazama Energy is a geothermal energy company reinventing power generation with enhanced geothermal systems (EGS) that tap superhot rock to deliver universal, scalable, clean, and affordable electricity. Its Thermal Lattice sequential-stimulation technology improves connectivity between injectors and producers in super hot reservoirs (SHR). The company is developing the Newberry project in Oregon and runs the Mazama EMPOWER program, and is backed by Khosla Ventures. Headquartered in Frisco, Texas.

providers.name: Mesodyne
providers.description: Mesodyne is an MIT-founded engineering and manufacturing company (established 2018) that builds the LightCell, a patented thermophotovoltaic power generator which converts liquid and gaseous fuels — gasoline, diesel, propane, jet fuel, and hydrogen — directly into silent electricity with more than ten times the energy density of batteries. Designed for military, tactical, drone, and off-grid use, it operates day or night across extreme environments with low heat and emissions signatures and no routine maintenance. Mesodyne publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface; this profile captures the company identity and its domain-security posture.

providers.name: Reach
providers.description: Reach Power (Reach Labs) is a Y Combinator-backed (S2015) wireless power company building long-range wireless energy distribution networks, aiming to "do for power what Wi-Fi did for data." Its patented, AI-driven power-beaming systems use adaptive metamaterial antennas to steer electromagnetic waves and deliver electricity through the air to multiple devices simultaneously, scaling from microwatts to kilowatts across both mobile and stationary transmitters. Reach serves defense and intelligence, manufacturing and logistics, and public safety markets, powering autonomous vehicles, industrial robotics, sensors, and drones. Partners and customers include the U.S. Department of Defense, NASA, DARPA, the U.S. Army and Air Force, Aisin/Toyota, and Panasonic. The company is headquartered in San Francisco. As of this profile, Reach publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this is a hardware and energy-infrastructure company rather than an API platform.

providers.name: SOLS Energy
providers.description: SOLS Energy is Malaysia's leading residential and commercial solar energy company, on a mission to make green energy a basic human right. It has completed more than 8,900 solar installations across Malaysia spanning residential (Green Homes), commercial (Green Business), and off-grid indigenous community projects (Green Impact), and also offers EV charging (ChargeSingh) and a Solar Academy apprenticeship program. The company is a portfolio company of 500 Global. As of this enrichment pass SOLS Energy publishes a consumer marketing website (blog, FAQ, contact, privacy and terms pages) but no public developer platform, API, or developer documentation.

providers.name: Swift Charge
providers.description: Swift Charge is an electric vehicle charging company that provides turn-key, fully managed EV charging infrastructure to property owners across the hospitality, education, and multi-family residential sectors, pairing installed charging hardware with a payment application that lets EV drivers locate and pay for charging sessions. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass Swift Charge publishes a public marketing and charger-map website but exposes no public developer API, documentation, SDKs, or developer portal, so this profile is limited to company identity plus a domain-security probe of its website host.

providers.name: Tiger New Energy
providers.description: Tiger New Energy is a Bangladesh-based clean-energy company building a battery-swapping network for electric vehicles, primarily electric rickshaws and motorcycles. Drivers swap depleted lithium batteries for fully charged ones at Tiger swapping stations in seconds instead of waiting to recharge, and a "battery passport" tracks each pack's health and lifecycle. The company operates consumer and partner mobile apps (Tiger Driver, Tiger Partner, Tiger Dealer) on iOS and Android. Tiger New Energy is a portfolio company of 500 Global. As of this enrichment pass the company exposes no public developer portal, API documentation, SDKs, or machine-readable specifications; its mobile apps are backed by private, undocumented services.

providers.name: Zeitview
providers.description: Zeitview (formerly DroneBase) is an AI-powered aerial inspection and asset intelligence platform. It combines a managed network of drone and aircraft pilots with computer-vision analytics and lifecycle asset-management software to deliver inspection imagery, condition assessments, and actionable intelligence for wind energy, solar, utilities, oil & gas, construction, commercial real estate, and property management. As of this profile the company operates a customer web platform, support center, and blog but does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, or SDK; data access is arranged through direct customer engagement.

providers.name: 24M
providers.description: 24M Technologies is a battery technology company founded in 2010 out of MIT laboratories and headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts. Rather than manufacturing cells at scale itself, 24M licenses its battery materials, cell architecture and SemiSolid manufacturing platform to energy-storage system integrators, EV battery manufacturers and OEMs worldwide. Its product portfolio spans the Eternalyte electrolyte (ultra-fast charging and low-temperature performance), the Impervio separator (thermal-runaway prevention), the LiForever electrode, the 24M ETOP electrode-to-pack architecture, and 24M production equipment. Partners and corporate investors have included Volkswagen Group, Kyocera, Itochu and FREYR Battery. 24M is a hardware, materials and manufacturing company; it publishes no public developer API, SDK or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Antora Energy
providers.description: Antora Energy is a San Jose, California clean-energy hardware company founded by Justin Briggs, Andrew Ponec and David Bierman that designs, manufactures and deploys factory-built thermal batteries for heavy industry, data centers and the grid. Antora's system resistively heats blocks of solid carbon to temperatures up to 2,400C when electricity is cheapest, stores that energy for multiple days in a compact modular unit, and discharges it around the clock as radiant heat delivered directly to industrial processes or paired with off-the-shelf steam turbine equipment for firm power; the company also develops thermophotovoltaic (TPV) heat-to-power cells at what it describes as the world's largest TPV manufacturing line. Its HeatCore product delivers heat up to 375C at 300 kW-thermal per module, and its power block is rated at 50 MW-electric. Antora's first giga-scale deployment, Project Big Stone, is a 5 GWh system of more than 200 thermal batteries at POET's bioprocessing plant in Big Stone City, South Dakota, built from empty lot to energy delivery in under twelve months. The company closed a $550 million Series C in 2026. Antora sells energy hardware and long-term energy offtake rather than software: it publishes no developer program, no public API, no SDK and no machine-readable API contract, and its only public software surface is Insight, an authenticated steam and power optimization dashboard for named project stakeholders.

providers.name: Apiday
providers.description: Apiday is an ESG (Environmental, Social, and Governance) software platform built for private markets. It combines AI-powered automation with expert guidance so investors, fund managers, and portfolio companies can streamline sustainability reporting, comply with regulatory frameworks (SFDR, EU Taxonomy, EDCI, PRI, ILPA), automate ESG questionnaires and due-diligence requests, calculate GHG emissions against 3,000+ benchmarks, and turn ESG obligations into measurable value creation. The company reports that over 500 investors and 5,000 companies use the platform across private equity, venture capital, private credit, institutional LP, and infrastructure asset classes. Backed by Speedinvest. Apiday does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or developer portal; this profile captures the company's identity and public web surface.

providers.name: CF Industries Holdings
providers.description: CF Industries Holdings is a Fortune 500 American manufacturer and distributor of nitrogen-based fertilizers (ammonia, urea, ammonium nitrate, UAN) and clean-energy products serving agricultural and industrial customers worldwide. CF operates one of the largest global ammonia production networks and is scaling clean (blue and green) ammonia for low-carbon energy. CF does not publish a public developer API program; programmatic data access is limited to investor-relations SEC filings feeds, press/news RSS, and partner EDI/B2B integrations with agricultural distributors, rail, terminal, and industrial customers.

providers.name: Electric Hydrogen
providers.description: Electric Hydrogen (EH2) is a Massachusetts-based clean-energy company that designs, manufactures, and commissions the world's most powerful PEM electrolyzers, packaged into a fully-integrated 100MW HYPRPlant that turns water and renewable electricity into the lowest-cost green hydrogen. The complete plant solution bundles power conversion, gas processing, water treatment, and thermal management so heavy industry can decarbonize ammonia, e-fuels, steel, and refining at gigawatt scale. Founded in 2020 and led by CEO Raffi Garabedian, EH2 operates a 1.2GW gigafactory in Devens, Massachusetts, became green hydrogen's first unicorn with a $380M Series C, and is backed by Fifth Wall, Fortescue, Energy Impact Partners, bp Ventures, Temasek, and Microsoft's Climate Innovation Fund. This profile enriches the API Evangelist network stub with the company's real public web surface.

providers.name: Niron Magnetics
providers.description: Niron Magnetics is a U.S. advanced-manufacturing company commercializing high-performance permanent magnets made from Iron Nitride rather than rare-earth elements. Spun out of University of Minnesota and U.S. Department of Energy ARPA-E research and founded in 2013, the company holds 150+ patents around its Clean Earth Magnet technology and is building the first full-scale Iron Nitride magnet plant in Sartell, Minnesota, alongside its Minneapolis headquarters and a Washington, D.C. policy office. Its magnets target electric-motor, automotive, consumer-audio, industrial and defense applications, with announced collaborations including Stellantis, Moog, Aspina, FaitalPRO, MATTER and Bimotal. Niron Magnetics is a materials and hardware manufacturer: it publishes no developer program, no public API, and no machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Volter
providers.description: Volter (Get Volter Ltd) is a London-based energy platform that connects UK businesses with renewable generators to procure cheaper, greener electricity, and helps commercial real estate owners and generators deploy, optimize, and monetize rooftop solar and other onsite renewable assets. The platform spans renewable energy matching, solar optimization, and a forthcoming energy management suite with analytics, anomaly detection, flexible asset control, and battery storage. Backed by Transition and Seedcamp with a $3.2M pre-seed round in 2024. Volter does not currently publish a public API or developer documentation.

providers.name: Zanskar
providers.description: Zanskar (Zanskar Geothermal & Minerals, Inc.) is a Salt Lake City-based geothermal energy company founded in 2021 by Carl Hoiland and Joel Edwards. It uses custom artificial intelligence, machine learning, and subsurface geoscience to discover and develop conventional geothermal resources, with a mission to make geothermal the most affordable form of widely-deployable, 24/7 carbon-free power. The company raised a $115M Series C and is backed by Obvious Ventures and Union Square Ventures. Zanskar publishes public geothermal datasets on the Snowflake Marketplace; it does not currently expose a public developer API.

providers.name: Senken
providers.description: Senken (Senken GmbH, Berlin) is a carbon credit procurement marketplace and advisory for European enterprises. It curates high-integrity carbon credits by scoring climate projects across 600+ data points with its Sustainability Integrity Index (SII), aligned to the Oxford Offsetting Principles and ICVCM Core Carbon Principles, rejecting roughly 95% of available credits. Products span advisory (CSRD, SBTi, CDP compliance), vetted procurement, audit-ready documentation (Champion's Kit), the SBTi 2035 Reserve carbon-removal supply, an OER portfolio, and free self-serve tools at tools.senken.io (checkout, portfolio calculator, OER calculator, EU greenwashing auditor). Clients include Vodafone, Deutsche Telekom, DZ Bank, and Union Investment. No public developer API is published as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Understory
providers.description: Understory is an insurtech company headquartered in Madison, Wisconsin (founded 2012) that combines its own network of ground-truth Dot weather sensors with a proprietary weather risk model to underwrite parametric insurance against severe weather, including hail coverage for automotive dealership open lots and agricultural weather risk. Its UnderstoryOS platform covers broker management, pricing and quoting, and automated weather-triggered claims. Understory publishes no public API or developer portal; the platform is offered to insurance partners rather than as a self-service developer product.

providers.name: AptDeco
providers.description: AptDeco is a full-service online marketplace for buying and selling used, new, and vintage furniture. Founded in 2014 in New York City by Reham Fagiri and Kalam Dennis, the company handles the entire resale transaction end to end: pickup, disassembly and assembly, delivery, payment, scheduling, and logistics are all carried out by its own trained delivery teams. AptDeco serves the New York City metro, New Jersey, Connecticut, Philadelphia, Delaware, and the San Francisco Bay Area, and has expanded to additional US metros with national shipping. Backed by Y Combinator and Initialized Capital. AptDeco does not publish a public developer API; this profile captures its public web, support, legal, and developer surfaces for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: LF Energy
providers.description: LF Energy is a Linux Foundation project building open source technology solutions for the power grid and energy sector. Launched in 2018, it accelerates the energy transition through open source collaboration and hosts projects for grid modernization, flexibility, and decarbonization.

providers.name: Alcoa
providers.description: Alcoa Corporation is a global industry leader in bauxite, alumina, and aluminum production. Founded in 1888, Alcoa operates mines, refineries, and smelters across Australia, Brazil, Canada, Iceland, Norway, Saudi Arabia, and the United States. The company is a Fortune 500 member and one of the world's largest aluminum producers, supplying lightweight, high-strength materials to automotive, aerospace, packaging, construction, and industrial markets. Alcoa is committed to sustainability through low-carbon aluminum production, responsible bauxite mining, and advancing aluminum recycling.

providers.name: CEEZER
providers.description: CEEZER (CEEZER Software GmbH) is a Berlin-based climate-tech enterprise platform for the procurement and portfolio management of carbon credits, Energy Attribute Certificates (EACs), and Sustainable Aviation Fuel Certificates (SAFc). The platform gives corporate sustainability teams access to a marketplace of more than 10,000 global carbon projects with transparent pricing and volume data, a proprietary risk-assessment engine ("Prism") that evaluates hundreds of validated data points per project, and audit-ready reporting for net-zero and decarbonization commitments. CEEZER combines expert climate advisory with enterprise-grade technology to help buyers plan, procure, and manage climate performance assets. Surfaced as a portfolio company of HV Capital and added to the API Evangelist network; the company operates a customer-facing web application but does not publish a public developer API or documentation at this time.

providers.name: ecoplanet
providers.description: ecoplanet provides cloud-based, integrated energy management software for German mid-market companies. The platform combines three core functions: real-time consumption monitoring through meter integration with AI-powered anomaly detection and automated load-shifting on price signals; strategic energy procurement using algorithmic purchasing across spot markets, tranches, and power purchase agreements (PPAs); and automated ISO 50001 compliance documentation. The company reports customers achieve up to 15% consumption savings and ~13.9% average price advantages on energy purchases. Backed by EQT Ventures and HV Capital. No public developer/API surface was found at the time of profiling.

providers.name: Enertiv
providers.description: Enertiv is a commercial real estate sustainability and decarbonization technology company serving owners and operators of large CRE portfolios. Its platform combines portfolio-scale utility data collection and ESG reporting (Report), asset-specific carbon planning that pairs AI recommendations with on-site equipment surveys (Decarbonize), and real-time monitoring with fault detection and operational optimization (Optimize). Additional workflow tools cover automated tenant utility billing and maintenance/work-order management, with integrations into property management systems such as Yardi and MRI. The company guarantees 100% utility data coverage — including tenant-controlled utilities — and has worked with 100+ large portfolios over more than fifteen years.

providers.name: Enpal
providers.description: Enpal is a Berlin-based residential clean-energy company and one of Germany's market leaders in home solar. It sells and finances complete home energy systems — rooftop solar PV, battery storage, air-to-water heat pumps, EV wallbox chargers, and a dynamic electricity tariff — orchestrated by its Enpal.One+ smart energy-management platform, with flexible purchase and zero-down financing options. Enpal serves over 130,000 German households and operates business (business.enpal.de) and installer partner (enpal.pro) channels alongside its consumer offering. Backed by HV Capital and the SoftBank Vision Fund. This API Evangelist profile was created from a VC-portfolio lead; Enpal publishes a consumer website and customer portal but no public developer API surface at the time of enrichment.

providers.name: Green Fusion
providers.description: Green Fusion GmbH is a Berlin-based climate-energy software company that provides an intelligent 360-degree energy management platform for the residential real estate sector (Wohnungswirtschaft). Its software digitizes and optimizes building heating systems: "Der Energiespar-Pilot" delivers digital boiler-room management and optimized operation of conventional heat sources (gas, oil, district heating, CHP/BHKW), while its AI platform for sector coupling (Sektorkopplung) integrates heat pumps, PV systems, storage, and grid connectivity for intelligent monitoring and control. The platform is TUV-certified under GEG section 71a. Green Fusion is backed by HV Capital and surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a climate-energy provider; it operates a customer control platform (control.green-fusion.de) but publishes no public developer API at this time.

providers.name: Manus Bio
providers.description: Manus Bio Inc. (trading as "Manus", the BioAlternatives Company) is a Cambridge, Massachusetts industrial biotechnology company founded in 2011 out of MIT by Dr. Aji Parayil and Dr. Greg Stephanopoulos. Manus engineers microbial cell factories and precision-fermentation processes so that complex molecules normally obtained through petrochemical synthesis, agricultural extraction, or animal husbandry can be produced by fermentation instead - what the company calls bioalternatives. Its commercialized products include the first U.S. commercial-scale monk fruit sweetener (produced at its Augusta, Georgia BioFacility), the Yume M stevia Reb M sweetener co-developed with Tate & Lyle, citrus-derived aroma ingredients (Nootkatone 70, Valencene 80, BioNootkatone) for Givaudan, and an artemisinin antimalarial program funded by HHS/ASPR. It sells scale-up services through its BioAccelerator and BioManufacturing programs (protein engineering, strain development, bioprocess development from 250 ml to 3,000 L, pilot-scale and biomanufacturing). In April 2025 Manus merged with genome-engineering company Inscripta, adding whole-genome editing technology and the MAD7 CRISPR nuclease licensing program; inscripta.com is now a redirect notice. Manus is a manufacturer of physical ingredients and a contract development and manufacturing organization - it sells molecules and services, not software. It publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, webhook surface, or machine-readable specification of any kind, and its computational and AI-driven enzyme-engineering tools are internal capabilities that support its services rather than a customer-facing platform.

providers.name: Matsmart
providers.description: Matsmart (operating internationally as Motatos) is a Swedish e-commerce company that fights food waste by selling surplus, short-dated, and overstocked groceries and household goods at a discount, with average savings of up to 50%. Its catalog spans pantry staples, beverages, snacks, candy, baby food, health and beauty, cleaning supplies, pet food, and non-food surplus, sourced from manufacturers and retailers and shipped across Sweden and other European markets via partners including Bring, Airmee, and PostNord. The company runs a consumer web storefront and iOS/Android apps. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Northzone and added to the API Evangelist network; it publishes no public developer API or documentation, so this profile captures its public web, security, and identity surface.

providers.name: Swell Energy
providers.description: Swell Energy is a residential clean-energy company that designs, finances, installs, and operates home solar, battery storage, and virtual power plant (VPP) systems for homeowners, businesses, and utilities. Its Swell Compass platform connects to home energy devices to monitor, report, and optimize energy use, and coordinates aggregated distributed batteries into grid services (GridRevenue programs) in partnership with utilities. Backed by SoftBank Vision Fund, the company operates a consumer web and mobile experience (Compass) rather than a public developer API; no developer portal, OpenAPI, SDKs, or documented public API surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Volteum
providers.description: Volteum provides fleet electrification and EV fleet management software that helps companies plan, execute, and operate the transition of their vehicle fleets to electric. The platform covers electrification planning, charging optimisation, and live fleet management, connecting directly to vehicles through OEM APIs across 30+ brands with no hardware installation to track mileage, fault codes, charging sessions, maintenance intervals, and costs across electric, diesel, petrol, and hybrid fleets. Volteum is a Techstars portfolio company and publishes no public developer portal; its telematics and fleet-system API integrations are offered to customers directly.

providers.name: Cake
providers.description: Cake (stylized CAKE) is a Stockholm, Sweden based maker of premium, lightweight, high-performance electric motorcycles and mopeds, built around a mission to accelerate the shift to a zero-emission society by combining excitement with responsibility. Its clean-mobility lineup spans commuter models (Makka, Osa), off-road bikes (Kalk, Bukk) and work-focused utility variants. Founded by Stefan Ytterborn and backed by Creandum, CAKE filed for bankruptcy in early 2024 and its brand and IP were acquired by Norway's Brages Holding AS, which relaunched the company. Cake sells direct to consumers and through dealers at ridecake.com. Its bikes ship with the CAKE Connect module, and CAKE markets a "CAKE API" on its own :work and delivery pages that lets fleet owners pull vehicle data, telemetry and controls into their own fleet software — but that API has no public developer portal, no reference and no machine-readable specification; access runs through the contact and partner forms.

providers.name: Calysta
providers.description: Calysta, Inc. is a cellular agriculture company founded in 2012 and headquartered in San Mateo, California, with operations in Memphis, Tennessee (NouriTech), Wilton/Teesside in the United Kingdom (Calysta UK Ltd.) and Singapore (Calysta Asia Pte Ltd.). It produces protein ingredients through a patented gas-fermentation platform in which a naturally-occurring microorganism converts carbon and energy into a non-GMO single-cell protein, using no arable land and no plant or animal inputs. Its product family includes FeedKind for aquaculture and livestock, FeedKind Pet, FeedKind Net Zero and Positive Protein for human food ingredients; FeedKind Aqua is sold globally through Calysseo, a 50/50 joint venture with Adisseo whose first production plant in China manufactures thousands of tonnes per year. Calysta sells physical protein ingredients to feed and food manufacturers — its fermentation platform is industrial process technology, not commercial software — and it publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Checkerspot
providers.description: Checkerspot is an Alameda, California biotechnology company, founded in 2016 and incorporated as a Public Benefit Corporation, that designs and produces functional fats and oils through precision fermentation of microalgae. Its biology-driven molecule licensing platform pairs algal strain development, an advanced analytical platform, bioinformatics, high-throughput screening, fermentation scale-up and downstream oil refining, built around the proprietary microbe Prototheca moriformis, which the company reports reaches over 80% oil content by dry cell weight. The commercial molecule portfolio includes a high sn-2 palmitate algal oil that mimics the triglyceride structure of human milk fat for infant nutrition, an Omega-7 (palmitoleic acid) algal oil, a designer high-oleic tropical-fat alternative to palm oil, and Algolein tG C18/80 for cosmetic formulation; earlier work commercialized algae-derived urethane composites through the WNDR Alpine outdoor brand. Checkerspot works through ingredient and manufacturing partners including AAK, Huvepharma and La Fabrique Vegetale, and closed a USD 55 million Series C led by ArrowMark Partners with participation from Cox Enterprises. It is a business-to-business ingredient and molecule licensing company rather than a software vendor: it operates a WordPress marketing site, publishes no developer portal, no API documentation, no SDK and no machine-readable API contract, and has no GitHub organization.

providers.name: Epic CleanTec
providers.description: Epic Cleantec is a San Francisco based water technology company that designs, builds and operates onsite water reuse systems for buildings. Its OneWater and OneWater Rain systems collect, treat and recycle a building's greywater, blackwater, rainwater and condensate onsite — recovering up to 95% of wastewater for non-potable uses such as toilet flushing, irrigation, cooling towers and laundry — alongside wastewater heat recovery and a soil amendment product line. The technology grew out of work on the Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation Reinvent the Toilet Challenge and is deployed in multifamily, commercial office, hospitality, stadium, data center, higher education and community-scale developments across North America. Systems ship with PLC/SCADA control and a cloud-connected Eco-Insights reporting dashboard for remote monitoring, alarms and utility savings reporting, but Epic Cleantec publishes no public developer program, API documentation or machine-readable API contract; the data surface is delivered to building owners and operators as a hosted dashboard rather than as a public API.

providers.name: Gradiant
providers.description: Gradiant is a global water and wastewater infrastructure company founded in 2013 out of MIT and headquartered in Boston, Massachusetts, that designs, builds and operates end-to-end industrial water systems from intake to discharge. It positions itself as "the Water Layer of the AI Economy", supplying ultrapure water, process water, wastewater recycling, minimal- and zero-liquid-discharge and resource-recovery systems to semiconductor fabs, AI data centers, energy producers and applied industries including pharmaceuticals, mining, food and beverage, refining and chemicals, textiles and renewables. Its proprietary technology portfolio includes Counterflow Reverse Osmosis (CFRO), Semi-Batch Reverse Osmosis (SBRO), Carrier Gas Extraction (CGE), Selective Contaminant Extraction (SCE), Free Radical Oxidation (FRO), Bio Infinity, the ForeverGone PFAS destruction process, the HyperSolved data-center cooling-water platform, the CURE Chemicals specialty-chemicals line and SmartOps AI, a machine-learning platform for optimizing and predicting plant operations. Gradiant raised a Series E at a $2 billion valuation in May 2026. It is an industrial equipment, chemicals and build-own-operate services company: it publishes no public developer portal, no developer API, no SDK and no machine-readable API contract, and SmartOps AI is delivered as a customer-facing operations platform rather than as a public API.

providers.name: LanzaJet
providers.description: LanzaJet is a sustainable fuels technology company, headquartered at 520 Lake Cook Road, Deerfield, Illinois, that produces and licenses sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) and renewable diesel. Founded in 2020 as a spin-out of LanzaTech with Suncor and Mitsui, and later backed by Shell, British Airways, Southwest Airlines, Microsoft's Climate Innovation Fund, Breakthrough Energy, Groupe ADP, MUFG and All Nippon Airways, the company commercializes a patented Alcohol-to-Jet (ATJ) process that converts ethanol into synthetic paraffinic kerosene through a continuous catalytic reaction, reaching roughly 90% hydrocarbon selectivity to jet fuel and converting about 98% of the ethanol carbon into salable product. The ATJ pathway was approved by ASTM International in 2018. LanzaJet Freedom Pines Fuels in Soperton, Georgia — opened in 2024 — is the world's first commercial ethanol-to-jet SAF plant, producing roughly 10 million gallons of SAF and renewable diesel a year, and the company is developing Project Speedbird in the UK alongside a CirculAir joint solution with LanzaTech that widens the feedstock base to municipal solid waste, agricultural residues and industrial off-gases via gas fermentation. LanzaJet sells technology licenses, project development and engineering services and fuel offtake rather than software: as of this profiling pass it publishes no public developer portal, no API reference, no SDKs, and no machine-readable API contract of any kind, and every /.well-known/ discovery probe against its web host returned 404.

providers.name: LARQ
providers.description: LARQ is a direct-to-consumer water technology company that designs self-cleaning and filtering drinkware and home water products. Its flagship Bottle PureVis uses UV-C light to neutralize up to 99.9999% of harmful, odor-causing bacteria in the bottle and on the water surface, and the range extends to filtered bottles, filtered pitchers, an under-sink water filter, and the cuva beverage flavor line. The company positions itself around sustainable hydration — reducing single-use plastic bottle consumption — and funds environmental nonprofits from a portion of each purchase. LARQ is a consumer hardware and e-commerce business: as of this enrichment pass it publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable specification, and no /.well-known/ discovery documents. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of dcm-ventures. Sector: consumer.

providers.name: Modern Meadow
providers.description: Modern Meadow is a bio-design and materials-science company founded in 2011 in Brooklyn by Andras Forgacs, Francoise Marga, Gabor Forgacs and Karoly Jakab, now headquartered in Nutley / Pine Brook, New Jersey, where it operates an innovation lab opened in 2017. The company applies synthetic biology and protein engineering to build animal-free, bio-fabricated alternatives to leather and other petrochemical-derived materials, through the Bio-Alloy technology platform (an alloy of engineered proteins and bio-based polymers), the BIO-VERA material launched in 2023, and its current flagship INNOVERA, a next-generation leather alternative made from plant proteins, biopolymers and recycled rubber with more than 80% renewable carbon content. It sells into interiors, fashion and accessories, footwear, and automotive, and has partnered with BASF, tannery HELLER-LEDER (a 2026 European joint venture) and Allbirds (the Terralux footwear line). Modern Meadow has raised roughly $236M. It is a materials manufacturer, not a software vendor: profiling on 2026-08-01 found no public API, no developer portal, no documentation, no OpenAPI/GraphQL/MCP surface, no /.well-known/ documents, and no GitHub organization. Its corporate site (modernmeadow.com, Craft CMS) largely redirects to the product site innovera-world.com.

providers.name: SkenarioLabs
providers.description: SkenarioLabs is a Helsinki-based real estate finance data intelligence company (founded 2015) that turns fragmented building data into auditable, asset-level intelligence for European banks and financial institutions. From a single address it reconstructs complete building profiles covering automated valuation, climate and transition risk, energy performance, technical condition, and renovation potential — aligned with CRREM, EU Taxonomy, ECB, EBA, CRR3, MEPS, and SFDR frameworks. It serves 200+ institutional clients monitoring over 60 billion euros of collateral and scores more than one million assets monthly. SkenarioLabs delivers its intelligence ad hoc into loan origination, portfolio audit, and continuous risk-monitoring workflows rather than through a public self-serve developer API.

providers.name: The Modern Milkman
providers.description: The Modern Milkman is a UK doorstep delivery service that brings farm-fresh milk, groceries and household essentials to customers in returnable and reusable glass bottles or recyclable packaging, with flexible ordering and early-morning delivery. Founded to modernise the traditional milkround, the company focuses on reducing food waste and single-use plastic through a return-and-reuse model, local sourcing, and a subscription-style ordering experience delivered through its website and mobile apps. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Insight Partners and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. The company publishes no public developer API, but does maintain an llms.txt for AI agents, a customer help centre, and a blog. Sector: consumer / direct-to-consumer grocery delivery.

providers.name: World View
providers.description: World View (World View Enterprises) is a Tucson, Arizona-based stratospheric balloon company focused on remote sensing and persistent intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance (ISR). Its uncrewed high-altitude balloons carry EO/FMV, IR, SAR, and hyperspectral sensors for defense, government, and commercial missions. Acquired by Ondas Holdings in 2026, it now operates as part of the Ondas Sentinel multi-domain intelligence platform, with partnerships including Palantir and Sierra Nevada Corporation. World View publishes no public developer program or API.

providers.name: Wunder
providers.description: Wunder (formerly Wunder Capital, wewunder.com, now wunderpower.com) is a commercial clean-energy company that deploys solar, battery storage, and EV charging infrastructure across real estate portfolios with no-CapEx energy solutions, managing projects from design through operations in 40+ US states. Backed by Techstars and a $650M partnership with Blackstone, Wunder runs its project development on Astra, a proprietary internal platform for energy data analysis, forecasting, and automation. Wunder publishes no public API or developer program.

providers.name: Anthro Energy
providers.description: Anthro Energy is a battery materials company based in Alameda, California, developing next-generation electrolyte technology for lithium-ion and next-gen battery cells. Its flagship Proteus platform is a drop-in electrolyte that increases energy density, improves safety, and adds mechanical integrity without requiring changes to existing gigafactory manufacturing infrastructure, and is compatible with a wide range of anodes, separators, and cathodes. Spun out of research at Stanford, Anthro Energy is a portfolio company of Union Square Ventures and Ultratech Capital. It is a physical-materials company with no public API surface; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network for company and market discovery.

providers.name: Apeel
providers.description: Apeel (Apeel Sciences) is a food technology company founded in 2012 and headquartered in Goleta, California. It produces a plant-derived, edible coating, made from lipids and glycerolipids found in the peels, seeds and pulp of produce, that is applied to fresh fruit and vegetables at packing houses to slow water loss and oxidation, extending shelf life and reducing food waste across the supply chain. Apeel-treated produce is sold through grocery retailers in multiple countries. In 2021 Apeel acquired ImpactVision and added hyperspectral imaging to its supplier installations to grade interior quality, ripeness and freshness. Apeel is a materials-science and supply-chain operator: as of this profile it publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, machine-readable API contract, or self-serve developer sign-up.

providers.name: Gravity
providers.description: Gravity (Gravity Technologies) builds and deploys ultra-fast DC electric-vehicle charging infrastructure for dense urban environments. Its Distributed Energy Access Points (DEAPs) deliver up to five-minute charges from compact, modular hardware that requires minimal real estate and no dedicated utility upgrade, letting operators place high-power charging in garages, curbside, and fleet depots. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of GV and Redpoint Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; it publishes no public developer portal, API, or SDKs at this time, so this profile captures company identity and the domain security surface rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: Hula Earth
providers.description: Hula Earth is a Munich-based environmental technology company providing real-time biodiversity monitoring. It combines solar-powered, maintenance-free Hula BioT IoT sensors with AI-powered species detection, satellite-based Earth Observation, and the Hula Platform dashboard so organizations can monitor, manage, and report on biodiversity at landscape scale. Hula Earth serves renewables (solar and wind), agriculture, nature conservation, and urban development, turning environmental uncertainty into operational confidence and compliance-ready reporting.

providers.name: HumanCo
providers.description: HumanCo is a mission-driven consumer packaged goods and wellness holding company that builds and acquires better-for-you food, beverage, and lifestyle brands made with real, clean ingredients and free of seed oils and highly processed inputs. Its portfolio spans brands and concepts such as Against the Grain (gluten-free foods), True Food Kitchen (health-focused restaurants), and Grove Collaborative (sustainable home and personal care). Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. HumanCo operates a marketing and e-commerce web presence but publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or technical developer platform at this time.

providers.name: SunPower
providers.description: SunPower is a residential solar energy company (Nasdaq: SPWR) that designs, installs, and finances solar systems and battery storage for homeowners. The original SunPower Corporation filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in August 2024; its assets were acquired by Complete Solaria in September 2024, which rebranded as SunPower Inc. in April 2025. SunPower maintains the GitHub org github.com/SunPower, hosting open-source solar modeling tools including pvfactors (view-factor model for bifacial PV modeling), PVMismatch (mismatch loss calculations), and SolarUtils. These Python libraries are used by solar energy professionals and researchers for photovoltaic system modeling and simulation.

providers.name: Green Software Foundation
providers.description: The Green Software Foundation is a Linux Foundation project founded by Accenture, GitHub, Microsoft, and ThoughtWorks to build standards, tools, and best practices for reducing the carbon emissions of software. It developed the Software Carbon Intensity specification and provides patterns for building green software.

providers.name: Unspun
providers.description: Unspun is a fashion-technology company building Vega, the world's first 3D weaving machines, which transform yarn directly into finished woven garments in about twenty minutes for automated, localized, on-demand apparel manufacturing. Founded by Beth Esponnette, Walden Lam, and Kevin Martin and operating from Oakland, California and Hong Kong, the company pairs its weaving hardware with software for custom-fit patternmaking and design automation, working with manufacturers and brands to eliminate overproduction, with a mission of reducing global human carbon emissions by one percent. Unspun is backed by DCVC and does not currently publish a public API or developer program.

providers.name: Blau Corp
providers.description: Blau (Blau Corp) is a waste-management operating system for haulers (gestores), final-destination facilities, and government regulators across Mexico, Colombia, and Spain. The SaaS platform delivers AI-assisted route optimization, route-level profitability analysis, automated RP and RPBI hazardous- and biological-infectious-waste manifests, online collection booking, and end-to-end traceability, plus the Blau Driver mobile app for field crews. Founded in Guadalajara, Mexico in 2021 and backed by 500 Global (LatAm B17 batch), Blau integrates with SAT/CFDI, SEMARNAT, SAP/ERP, QuickBooks, WhatsApp, fleet GPS, and Power BI. Blau does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or API documentation.

providers.name: David Energy
providers.description: David Energy is a clean-energy technology company and licensed electricity retailer that installs free plug-in smart batteries for homes and businesses. Its software charges batteries when grid power is cheap and discharges them during peak-price periods to lower customers' monthly utility bills, alongside bill-monitoring and thermostat-management advisory tools. Backed by Union Square Ventures, David Energy operates in the New York City market with a stated mission of powering the grid on 100% clean energy and shifting the balance of energy control from institutions toward consumers.

providers.name: Essity
providers.description: Essity is a Swedish-headquartered global hygiene and health company operating across four business areas: Health & Medical, Personal Care, Consumer Tissue, and Professional Hygiene. The company is listed on Nasdaq Stockholm (ESSITY) and owns roughly 40 brands including TENA (incontinence care), Tork (professional hygiene), Libero (baby diapers), Libresse / Bodyform / Nana / Saba / Nuvenia / Libra (feminine care), Modibodi and Knix (period underwear), JOBST (compression hosiery), Leukoplast (adhesive bandages), Cutimed, Sorbact, Hydrofera and Actimove (wound care, sports medicine, orthopedic supports), Delta-Cast (casting), and consumer tissue brands Lotus, Zewa, Tempo, Cushelle, Plenty, Velvet, Regio, Sorbent and Purex. No public developer-facing APIs or developer portal have been identified for Essity; this repository tracks corporate, brand, sustainability, investor, and integration surfaces for ongoing API discovery. The company's Tork brand ships a connected washroom data platform — Tork Vision Cleaning — which is the closest thing to a public data surface in the portfolio.

providers.name: Exowatt
providers.description: Exowatt is a clean-energy technology company redefining power generation for the AI era. Its flagship Exowatt P3 is a modular, dispatchable solar-thermal energy platform that captures solar energy with proprietary Fresnel lenses and heat exchangers, stores it in a high-efficiency heat battery, and dispatches electricity on demand via a proprietary heat engine, delivering up to 24 hours of dispatchable baseload power. The systems are factory-built in the USA from abundant, low-cost materials without rare-earth minerals, and are aimed at energy-intensive customers such as AI data centers and utilities. Backed by a16z and Felicis, Exowatt is added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile; it currently publishes no public developer API or documentation surface.

providers.name: General Matter
providers.description: General Matter is a domestic nuclear-fuel company founded in 2024 and based in California, building United States uranium enrichment capacity to produce low-enriched uranium (LEU) and high-assay low-enriched uranium (HALEU) for advanced commercial and government nuclear reactors. Co-founded by Scott Nolan and Lee Robinson and backed by Founders Fund, the company was awarded a $900M Department of Energy IDIQ contract and plans a $1.5B commercial enrichment facility at the former Paducah Gaseous Diffusion Plant in Kentucky, plus a lease on the Hanford Fuels and Materials Examination Facility in Washington. Its mission is to reduce American reliance on foreign nuclear fuel and strengthen energy independence. General Matter is an industrial energy manufacturer with no public developer API; this profile captures its identity, website properties, and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Heron Power
providers.description: Heron Power is an industrial power-electronics company modernizing the electrical grid with solid-state transformers and integrated power conversion systems. Founded by former Tesla executive Drew Baglino, the company builds Heron Link products that combine a solid-state transformer with a power supply or inverter for two markets: data centers (AI and hyperscale power delivery, including 800 VDC datacenter architectures) and solar-and-storage renewable energy systems. Heron Power targets the grid infrastructure bottlenecks of the clean-energy transition, replacing century-old passive transformer technology with dense, controllable, software-defined power hardware. The company is backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and Breakthrough Energy. Heron Power is a hardware and infrastructure company and does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, or SDKs; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network for company intelligence.

providers.name: HyperStrong
providers.description: HyperStrong (Beijing HyperStrong Technology Co., Ltd. / 北京海博思创科技股份有限公司, SSE: 688411) is a leading Chinese provider of battery energy storage systems (BESS) and integrated energy solutions. Founded in 2011 and headquartered in Beijing, the company designs and manufactures modular liquid-cooled storage systems (HyperBlock and HyperCube series), integrated solar-plus-storage and charging-storage units, and the core control stack of battery management systems (BMS), energy management systems (EMS), and power conversion systems (PCS), alongside its HyperCloud AI cloud platform for fleet monitoring and optimization. HyperStrong serves generation-side, grid-side, and user-side (commercial, industrial, and residential) storage markets, ranking among the top domestic and global players by cumulative installed capacity with 60+ GWh deployed across 400+ projects. It is backed by IDG Capital and Qiming Venture Partners. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network; HyperStrong is a hardware and energy-platform company and does not publish a public developer API surface at this time.

providers.name: Marvel Fusion
providers.description: Marvel Fusion is a Munich-based deep-tech company founded in 2019 that is developing laser-based inertial confinement fusion energy. It combines a proprietary fast-ignition approach with innovations across lasers, fuel targets, and power-plant design to make commercial fusion power viable, building on the National Ignition Facility 2022 ignition breakthrough. The company operates in Germany and the United States, with a demonstration facility in Fort Collins, Colorado, and has raised over $400M from venture capital, industrial partners, and public funding. As a physics and energy-infrastructure company it publishes no public developer API, SDK, or MCP surface; this profile captures its corporate identity and web/domain security posture.

providers.name: Proxima Fusion
providers.description: Proxima Fusion is a Munich-based fusion energy company building the first generation of commercial fusion power plants using quasi-isodynamic (QI) stellarators. Spun out of the Max Planck Institute for Plasma Physics, the company is developing Stellaris, a stellarator power plant concept, with milestones that include a Stellarator Model Coil and an Alpha demonstration stellarator on the path to grid-scale fusion energy. Proxima Fusion is a privately held deep-tech startup and does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable API surface; this profile captures its identity and public web properties for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: rabot.energy
providers.description: rabot.energy (RABOT Energy DE GmbH) is a Hamburg-based German electricity supplier offering dynamic and fixed-rate power tariffs where consumers pay hourly rates that track the wholesale electricity market. The company provides 100% renewable energy certified by TÜV NORD, smart meter installation and management, EV charging optimization (Autostrom), and home battery storage (Rabot Flow), all managed through a consumer mobile app for consumption monitoring. It is a consumer-facing energy retailer; no public developer portal or API is currently published. Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of HV Capital.

providers.name: Recyda
providers.description: Recyda is a German software company offering an all-in-one platform for packaging sustainability and regulatory compliance. The platform centralizes packaging data, automates Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) fee calculation and declaration across 20+ countries, and assesses packaging recyclability against standards such as the ZSVR Minimum Standard and EN 18120. It supports EU Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation (PPWR) compliance, portfolio-wide assessments, and submission-ready reporting, turning weeks of manual compliance work into minutes. Recyda is trusted by global brands and is backed by venture firm Speedinvest.

providers.name: SXD
providers.description: SXD is a New York-based design-technology company founded in 2022 that uses patented artificial intelligence to generate zero-waste apparel patterns for the fashion industry. Its SXD AI platform transforms a sketch or design concept into production-ready patterns that eliminate fabric waste before the first cut, and the company reports up to 69% material savings across more than 35 brand and manufacturing partners. SXD has been recognized with the Global Change Award and a top prize at the SXSW Pitch competition, and is backed by Initialized Capital. SXD does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Bright
providers.description: Bright is Mexico's leading residential and commercial solar energy provider, founded in 2014 (Y Combinator W15) by Jonah Greenberger. Often described as "Sunrun for the developing world," Bright combines financing and software to let homeowners and businesses adopt rooftop solar and battery energy storage (BESS) at no upfront cost. The company operates a marketplace connecting a network of local installers, distributors, and retail promoters with customers, and offers financing models such as solar PPAs and leasing schemes. Bright's public web presence is a Wix-hosted marketing site (thinkbright.mx) covering its industrial, commercial, and home solutions, success cases, and 24/7 energy monitoring technology. It exposes an agent-facing surface via an llms.txt and a hosted Wix Site MCP endpoint, but publishes no first-party developer/REST API.

providers.name: Koobz
providers.description: Koobz is a Ventura, California additive-manufacturing company rebuilding the footwear supply chain around on-demand 3D printing. Its "gigafactory" prints circular-ready, mono-material foamed-TPU shoes to order, so brands carry zero inventory and face no minimum order quantities: a consumer buys on the brand's own storefront, the order and personalization specs sync to the Koobz factory, the shoe is printed in Ventura and dropshipped direct to the customer in days. The company markets 10x faster concept-to-market cycles (4-6 weeks, no tooling), custom cushioning and foot-scanning personalization, and a KoobzWeave toolpath-as-textile upper pattern engine. Its mono-material architecture is positioned for Extended Producer Responsibility regimes such as California SB 707, since a single-polymer shoe yields premium TPU on take-back rather than mixed waste. Koobz has raised $7.2M and is backed by Uncork Capital. It describes its factory as API-driven and its order intake as an API sync from brand storefronts, but as of this profile it publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API definition; integration appears to run through its partner ("Partner With Us") channel.

providers.name: PwC (PricewaterhouseCoopers)
providers.description: PricewaterhouseCoopers (PwC) is one of the Big Four professional services firms, with approximately 370,000 staff across a global network of member firms coordinated by PricewaterhouseCoopers International Limited (PwCIL). PwC organizes delivery across three primary service lines — Assurance (audit), Tax (tax compliance, planning, and reporting), and Advisory (consulting, deals, and risk). The firm operates proprietary technology platforms including PwC Halo (a suite of data analytics tools used to support audit engagements), the Trusted AI initiative (PwC's responsible-AI governance and assurance framework), and ProEdge (a workforce upskilling platform). In April 2024 PwC announced a multi-year alliance with OpenAI positioning the firm as both OpenAI's largest customer and its first reseller of ChatGPT Enterprise, supporting PwC's broader generative-AI consulting practice. PwC's research and insights surface — pwc.com/insights, the annual Global CEO Survey, the Global Workforce Hopes and Fears Survey, the Money Tree report, and regional industry outlooks — is the firm's primary public-facing knowledge product. PwC does not publish a public developer portal, OpenAPI specifications, partner API documentation, or a GitHub organization at the corporate level. The github.com/pwc handle is held by an unrelated individual user (Patrick Clearwater). Any technical integrations with PwC platforms are arranged through engagement contracts and the PwC Technology Consulting practice rather than through self-service developer credentials. PwC's content distribution is reader-facing (newsletter subscriptions, the PwC US Newsroom, LinkedIn, YouTube) with no documented public RSS feed endpoint exposing news, press releases, or insights as a syndication contract.

providers.name: CohnReznick
providers.description: CohnReznick is a top-25 US accounting, tax, and advisory firm formed in 2012 by the merger of J.H. Cohn LLP and Reznick Group, P.C. The firm serves clients across more than 30 industries from offices throughout the United States and four offshore subsidiaries, with its global reach extended through membership in the Nexia International network (operating in more than 128 countries). In May 2024 CohnReznick became the first US accounting firm of its scale to receive a strategic growth investment from a private equity sponsor when funds advised by Apax Partners acquired a majority stake. As part of that transaction the firm operates under an alternative-practice structure: audit and attest services are delivered by CohnReznick LLP (a licensed CPA firm) while tax and advisory services are delivered through CohnReznick Advisory LLC. Largest practice areas include Real Estate, Renewable Energy, Government Contracting, Asset Management (private equity, hedge funds, private credit, REITs), Financial Services, Healthcare, Life Sciences, Consumer & Industrial, Technology & Media, Public Sector, and Private Clients (family offices, high net worth individuals, professional sports). CohnReznick does not publish a public software developer API; this repository documents the firm's organizational profile, practice taxonomy, and linked-data context for API catalog purposes.

providers.name: EcoPlant
providers.description: EcoPlant provides an intelligent air compressor control and monitoring platform for industrial facilities. The Ecoplant 360 solution uses IoT sensors, AI-powered dynamic controls, and predictive analytics to optimize compressed-air systems in real time, preventing downtime, improving reliability, and reducing compressed-air energy costs by up to 50 percent. It installs in under a week with no installation fees and is compatible with most compressor brands and existing plant technology.

providers.name: Electra
providers.description: Electra (legal name Electrasteel, Inc.) is a Boulder, Colorado clean-industrial company founded in 2020 that is reinventing ironmaking. Instead of smelting iron ore with fossil fuels in a blast furnace, Electra uses an electrochemical process — an acidic leach plus electrowinning driven by renewable electricity — to dissolve a broad range of iron ores, including low-grade and previously uncommercialized ores, and plate out 99% pure iron at roughly 60°C while recovering high-value co-minerals and emitting oxygen. The modular design lets units be added as building blocks for rapid scaling and lets the process follow intermittent renewable power. Electra has raised over $200M from Rio Tinto, BHP Ventures, POSCO, Breakthrough Energy Ventures, Amazon's Climate Pledge Fund, Capricorn and Lowercarbon Capital, runs a pilot plant in Boulder, and is building a demonstration plant in Colorado. It is an industrial manufacturer with no public developer program: as of this profile it publishes no API, developer portal, documentation, machine-readable specification, or /.well-known discovery surface.

providers.name: Indian Energy Exchange
providers.description: Indian Energy Exchange (IEX) is India's largest electricity trading platform, operating a nationwide automated exchange for the physical delivery of electricity, renewable energy, and certificates. IEX runs Day-Ahead, Real-Time, Term-Ahead, Renewable Energy Certificate and Energy Saving Certificate market segments, matching buy and sell bids across a member network of distribution utilities, industrial and commercial consumers, and power generators. For members with sophisticated trading needs IEX offers a members-only trading API (currently for the iDAM and RTM segments) supporting order placement, trade-data retrieval and real-time monitoring for automated and high-frequency trading; access is provisioned to registered members rather than published as a public developer portal. Surfaced as a portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment.

providers.name: Inertia
providers.description: Inertia is a commercial fusion energy company pursuing laser-driven inertial confinement fusion to deliver safe, affordable, grid-scale clean power. Building on the December 2022 ignition milestone at the National Ignition Facility (NIF) in Livermore, Inertia is developing a modular laser system composed of roughly a thousand smaller, more efficient lasers, mass-manufacturing 4.5mm fusion fuel targets for under a dollar each, and firing them ten times per second to power a 1.5 gigawatt baseload, dispatchable power plant. The company is a deep-tech venture tracked in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub; it operates a corporate/marketing web presence and publishes no public developer or API surface at this time.

providers.name: Nanotech Energy
providers.description: Nanotech Energy is an advanced materials manufacturer that develops and produces graphene-based super materials and the energy-storage products built from them. Its catalog spans graphene powders, graphene oxide pastes, dispersions, conductive inks and conductive adhesives, silver nanowires, and non-flammable lithium-ion battery cells and packs aimed at home and grid energy storage, marine, household and electric-vehicle applications. The company also offers customer-facing testing, analysis and product development services to help customers scale a graphene formulation from concept to full production. It is a physical-goods manufacturer: it publishes a marketing and product website but no developer program, public API, SDK or machine-readable specification of any kind.

providers.name: Assembly OSM
providers.description: Assembly OSM is a New York City off-site manufacturing company founded in 2019 by SHoP Architects co-founders Bill and Chris Sharples to industrialise the construction of high-rise urban housing. The company calls its method "post-modular": rather than trucking finished volumetric boxes from a single factory, Assembly designs a kit-of-parts chassis and distributes fabrication across a network of specialist suppliers — an aerospace and automotive supply-chain model applied to buildings — then stacks the resulting units on site, claiming delivery of market-competitive high-rise residential architecture in roughly 60% of conventional schedule. Its buildings are all-electric and passive-design led, targeting 55-70% energy-efficiency improvement and 35% less embodied carbon today, net-zero operational carbon by 2027 and climate-positive buildings by 2040. Completed and in-progress work includes Prototype Alpha, 147 St. Felix Street and 247 East 117th Street in New York, plus an AOSM Canada operation. The company has raised more than $60 million, including a $38 million Series A in 2022, and draws engineering staff from SpaceX, Tesla and Boeing. Assembly runs a digital-twin engineering platform — a heavily scripted CATIA environment carrying each module from design through fabrication to installation — but that platform is an internal manufacturing tool, not a product: Assembly OSM sells buildings, and publishes no developer program, no public API, no SDK and no machine-readable API contract of any kind.

providers.name: SolarCycle
providers.description: SolarCycle is a technology-driven solar recycling company founded in 2022 that provides certified end-of-life management for solar energy systems. It recovers up to 97% of panel materials (silver, copper, gold, aluminum, glass), recycles power electronics such as inverters and transformers, and handles logistics and field operations for large-scale solar projects, achieving 100% landfill diversion. SolarCycle operates seven facilities across Georgia, Illinois, Texas, Nevada, and Arizona and is building a domestic recycled-solar-glass manufacturing plant, serving major solar companies including Q Cells, AES, Orsted, and Sunrun. It is a portfolio company of Fifth Wall. This is a physical circular-economy operations business with no public developer or API surface.

providers.name: zincfive
providers.description: ZincFive is a power solutions company that manufactures nickel-zinc (NiZn) battery technology for mission-critical and backup power applications, including data center UPS systems, AI dynamic power, and grid storage. Its product line covers BC Series UPS battery cabinets, NiZn retrofit kits, monobloc batteries, and cylindrical cells, positioned as non-flammable, high-power-density, and highly recyclable alternatives to lead-acid batteries. ZincFive publishes technical documents, papers, and industry insights reports, but does not expose a public developer API or SDK surface.

providers.name: AgFunder
providers.description: AgFunder is a global agrifood-tech venture capital firm investing in deeptech and foundational technologies across AI, biology, robotics, and climate to advance food, agriculture, and human and planetary health. Founded roughly a decade ago by Michael Dean and Rob Leclerc and headquartered in Silicon Valley with offices in London and Singapore, the firm manages over $300M in assets and has backed more than 100 portfolio companies across four continents. AgFunder also operates AgFunderNews (AFN), the leading agtech and foodtech news and research publication, and publishes market research for the agrifoodtech ecosystem. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-company lead and enriched with the firm's public identity and site properties; AgFunder publishes no public developer API surface.

providers.name: Apeel
providers.description: Apeel Sciences is a food technology company headquartered in Santa Barbara, California that develops plant-based protective coatings which extend the shelf life of fresh fruits and vegetables. The company uses food-grade ingredients derived from the peels, pulp, and seeds of plants to create a thin, edible layer that reinforces produce's natural peel, slowing water loss and oxidation. This extends peak taste, juiciness, and nutrient retention while reducing reliance on refrigeration, waxes, pesticides, and plastic packaging across the fresh-produce supply chain. Apeel positions itself as a sustainability and food-waste leader, reporting that since 2021 its technology has prevented millions of pieces of fruit from spoiling, avoided tens of thousands of metric tons of CO2-equivalent emissions, and conserved billions of liters of water. Its products have undergone regulatory review in the United States, European Union, and other markets. Apeel is a portfolio company of Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and was added to the API Evangelist network as a venture-portfolio lead. It publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or machine-readable API specification as of this profile.

providers.name: Charm Industrial
providers.description: Charm Industrial is a carbon removal technology company that permanently sequesters atmospheric CO2 by converting waste biomass (agricultural residues and other plant matter) into a stable, carbon-rich liquid called bio-oil through fast pyrolysis, then injecting that bio-oil into EPA-regulated underground wells where it solidifies and remains stored for millennia. Charm sells verified carbon dioxide removal (CDR) credits to enterprise buyers and publishes a public ledger of delivered tonnage. The company received a $53M advance market commitment from Frontier and is backed by investors including General Catalyst and Lowercarbon Capital. This API Evangelist profile tracks Charm Industrial as a company; the provider publishes a marketing and carbon-purchasing website but no public developer API surface as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Cycle
providers.description: CYCLE (operated by CM Invest B.V., Amsterdam) is a European electric-mobility subscription service that provides e-bikes and cargo bikes to professional delivery riders, couriers, and businesses. Its all-inclusive monthly subscriptions bundle maintenance, on-site repairs, bike swaps, GPS tracking, theft protection, and remote motor control across 100+ cities in Germany, Austria, the Netherlands, Belgium, Poland, Italy, and the UK. CYCLE was added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile; the provider publishes a consumer/business marketing and operations site but exposes no public developer API, SDKs, or developer portal at this time.

providers.name: Cylib
