Backed by SOSV/IndieBio and a USD 34 million Series B closed in March 2022, and now led by co-founder and CEO Brandon Chen with co-founder Brian Wyrwas as CSO, Finless Foods is a food-biotechnology and consumer-products business rather than a software vendor: it operates a single-page Squarespace marketing site with a Squarespace Commerce cart, publishes no developer portal, no API documentation and no machine-readable API contract, and its 2017-era GitHub organization holds one dormant static-HTML repository.

providers.name: BrightSource Energy
providers.description: BrightSource Energy is a renewable energy technology company founded in 2006, historically known as a pioneer of utility-scale Concentrated Solar Power (CSP) — it designed, developed and built the 377 MW Ivanpah Solar Electric Generating System in California along with CSP projects in Israel, Dubai and South Africa. In 2022 the company transformed into a software business and now commercializes OASES, a cloud-based, AI-powered Energy Management System (EMS) that forecasts, optimizes and dispatches portfolios of photovoltaics, battery energy storage (BESS), wind, microgrids and EV charging. OASES combines physics-based digital twins, big-data analytics and sensor fusion with an on-site SCADA edge controller ("OASES Gateway + IoT") to run asset management, energy-market bidding and arbitrage, PPA management, grid services and frequency regulation. Engineering is based in Jerusalem, Israel, with a UK office in London. BrightSource does not publish a public developer program, API documentation or machine-readable API contract as of August 2026.

providers.name: Byanat
providers.description: Byanat is an Oman-based, award-winning AI company offering a unified platform for optimizing digital infrastructure across telecommunications networks and data centers. The platform pairs system-wide visibility with custom-tailored automation to scale operations, ensure compliance, and promote sustainability, an approach the company frames as "Infrastructure 4.0." Its product families span mobile network solutions (site management, degradation detection, auto-discovery, performance analytics), data centre solutions (predictive analytics, capacity forecasting, energy management, infrastructure monitoring), and an API and integration layer for cross-platform connectivity and AI-powered workflow automation. Byanat is a portfolio company of 500 Global and was added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. The company does not currently publish a public developer portal, OpenAPI specification, or API reference; its API and integration capability is delivered as a managed product.

providers.name: Carnot Innovations
providers.description: Carnot Innovations is a Hong Kong-based building energy management company that applies AI, machine learning, and advanced data analytics to optimize HVAC systems and reduce energy consumption across commercial buildings, data centers, hospitals, railways, and sewage treatment facilities in the Asia-Pacific region. Its platform delivers AI-driven energy optimization, predictive maintenance and fault detection for chillers, pumps, cooling towers, and air handling units, analytics dashboards for facility managers, and continuous commissioning insights, reporting outcomes such as 15% energy cost reductions, 90% hidden-fault detection, and 15 million kWh per year of energy savings across its deployment portfolio. It is a portfolio company of 500 Global. Carnot Innovations does not currently publish a public developer program or API; this profile exists in the API Evangelist network for discovery and enrichment.

providers.name: Gyre Energy
providers.description: Gyre Energy is a UK-based climate-tech company that reduces cooling costs for operators of cold storage facilities, data centers, and building portfolios by combining artificial intelligence with thermal energy storage. Its platform pairs Gyre AI, a digital twin that learns a facility's thermal behavior and shifts cooling cycles to run when grid energy is cheapest and greenest, with an integrated thermal energy storage "cold battery" and a real-time monitoring and controls layer that tracks temperature, energy use, and door-open events. The company reports up to 50% lower cooling expenses, 38% verified energy cost savings at its first commercial cold storage deployment, a 91% reduction in temperature excursions, and a payback period of under 1.5 years. Gyre Energy is a portfolio company of Speedinvest and, as of July 2026, secured $1.3m in funding to support a major blue-chip deployment and global scaling. It currently exposes no public developer API, documentation, or developer portal; this profile captures its identity and public web surface for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Nitricity
providers.description: Nitricity is a climate-tech and agricultural-technology company that produces nitrogen fertilizer on-farm from only air, water, and renewable electricity. Founded in 2018 by Stanford graduate researchers Nicolas Pinkowski and Joshua McEnaney, the company uses a solar-powered plasma / electrochemical process to fix atmospheric nitrogen and produce nitric acid and calcium nitrate fertilizers on-site and on-demand, eliminating the fossil-fuel-intensive Haber-Bosch process and long-distance transportation that make conventional fertilizer responsible for roughly 5% of global greenhouse gas emissions. Backed by Khosla Ventures, Fine Structure Ventures, Lowercarbon Capital, and strategic investor Chipotle, Nitricity is a hardware and physical-product company; it publishes a corporate website, blog, and field-trial program but exposes no public API, developer portal, or technical integration surface.

providers.name: Petra Power
providers.description: Petra Power is an on-site power generation company based in Solon, Ohio, and backed by Techstars, building rapidly deployable, high-efficiency generation systems positioned as "the next 100GW of on-site power." Its technology runs on natural gas, diesel, or hydrogen, claims up to 3x fuel savings versus conventional generators and turbines, and operates silently and odorlessly for use in populated areas. Target applications include data centers, critical backup power, heavy industry, and utility-scale deployment. Petra Power is a hardware/energy company with no public developer or API surface; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record.

providers.name: Photon Crystal Energy
providers.description: Photon Crystal Energy Technology Ltd. (广东光晶能源科技有限公司) is a China-based perovskite photovoltaic module manufacturer, founded May 2022 and headquartered in Foshan, Guangdong. The company commercializes full wet-process, full-printed perovskite PV modules for building-integrated photovoltaics (BIPV), photovoltaic curtain walls, rooftop distributed solar, carports and architectural solar applications. Product families include standard, semi-transparent, textured, architectural color and solar tile modules, and the firm operates a 100 MW full-printed perovskite pilot line with IEC 61215 / IEC 61730 certification milestones. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming and added to the API Evangelist network; it publishes a marketing/corporate website but no public API, SDK, or developer surface.

providers.name: Pivot Bio
providers.description: Pivot Bio is an agricultural biotechnology company headquartered in Berkeley, California with additional operations in St. Louis, Missouri. The company engineers naturally occurring soil microbes to fix atmospheric nitrogen on crop root systems, providing a biological alternative to synthetic nitrogen fertilizer that reduces nitrous-oxide emissions, nitrate runoff, and exposure to volatile fertilizer prices. Pivot Bio's product line includes PROVEN 40 and PROVEN G3 (corn and corn silage), RETURN (wheat and small grains), CERT-N (cotton), and RETAIN (sorghum). The company also operates N-OVATOR, an outcomes-based program that pays farmers for verified emissions reductions; the program reports having paid out more than $6M to growers since 2022 and contributing to over 1,050,000 metric tons of CO2e avoided. Pivot Bio was founded by Karsten Temme (CEO) and Alvin Tamsir. Investors include Breakthrough Energy Ventures, Temasek, DCVC, Generation Investment Management, Pavilion Capital, G2 Venture Partners, Bond, and others. Pivot Bio's product is the microbe, not an API; the company operates a farmer-facing Salesforce-based portal but does not publish a public developer API or SDK.

providers.name: Ampaire
providers.description: Ampaire is a Long Beach, California electric aviation company that develops hybrid-electric propulsion systems for aircraft. Its AmpDrive powertrain retrofits and powers regional aircraft, and the company reports more than 30,000 flight miles with a stated goal of cutting fuel consumption, maintenance costs, and noise. Ampaire is backed by Techstars and has worked with partners including NASA and ARPA-E. The company currently exposes no public API, developer portal, or documentation surface; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record awaiting any future developer program.

providers.name: Exide Technologies
providers.description: Exide Technologies is a global producer and recycler of lead-acid batteries used in transportation and industrial applications, serving automotive, motive power, network power, and other markets. Headquartered in Milton, Georgia, the company operates manufacturing and recycling facilities worldwide. No public developer APIs have been identified; ordering and product data are provided through B2B portals and distributor channels.

providers.name: Living Carbon
providers.description: Living Carbon is a reforestation and carbon removal company that restores abandoned mineland and degraded agricultural land in the United States, generating income for landowners while producing high-quality carbon removal credits with true additionality, limited leakage, and unique co-benefits. It develops fast-growing poplar trees for permanent land restoration and for custom biomass feedstock sited near processing facilities. Backed by Homebrew and surfaced through the API Evangelist network as a climate-sector company profile; the company publishes no public developer, API, or technical surface at this time.

providers.name: Neocarbon
providers.description: NeoCarbon GmbH is a Berlin-based climate-technology company building integrated cooling and carbon-capture systems for data centers. Its patented Hollow Fiber platform converts low-grade waste heat (30-55C) simultaneously into efficient cooling, captured CO2 for industrial reuse, and recovered water, deployed as a retrofit without redesigning existing infrastructure. Backed by Speedinvest, the company operates as an industrial hardware and climate-infrastructure business and does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or an API developer portal.

providers.name: Project Eaden
providers.description: Project Eaden (PROJECT EADEN GmbH) is a Berlin-based food-technology company building fiber-spinning technology to power the next generation of whole-cut plant-based protein. Its platform reconstructs the fibrous structure of animal muscle from plant ingredients to create alternatives such as plant-based fish and meat, and it collaborates on consumer brands including LEKKA. Backed by Creandum and co-funded through EIT Food and the European Union, the company operates as a consumer food-tech producer and currently publishes no public developer API surface.

providers.name: Radia
providers.description: Radia is a dual-use aerospace company founded in 2016 by MIT-trained aerospace engineer Mark Lundstrom, headquartered in Boulder, Colorado with a second operating base in Italy led by Giuseppe Giordo. After roughly seven years in stealth the company emerged in March 2024 with WindRunner, an aircraft it describes as the largest ever built: roughly ten times the cargo volume of a Boeing 777, sized to carry onshore wind turbine blades of up to about 105 metres, and designed to land on semi-prepared packed-dirt or gravel strips so that oversized cargo can be flown directly to a wind farm, a forward operating site or a disaster zone rather than trucked over highways it cannot fit on. Radia frames WindRunner as a deliberately low-novelty airframe assembled from existing certified technologies to shorten the certification path, targeting entry into service in the early 2030s across three markets: energy (delivering the very large blades that make low-wind onshore sites economic), defense (outsized-volume strategic airlift), and commercial supply-chain logistics. It has assembled an industrial ecosystem of more than twenty suppliers and technology partners including Aernnova, Leonardo, AFuzion, Atitech, Latecoere, Stirling Dynamics, Collier Aerospace and Maximus Air, and has raised roughly USD 128 million from investors including ConocoPhillips, Lauder Partners, LS Power Development and HCVC. Radia is an aircraft manufacturer and logistics operator rather than a software vendor: as of August 2026 it publishes no developer portal, no API documentation, no SDK and no machine-readable API contract of any kind. Its only machine-readable public surface is the Strapi headless-CMS backend at radia.com/strapi that renders its own marketing site, whose content API is permission-locked and undocumented.

providers.name: Samsara Eco
providers.description: Samsara Eco is an Australian climate-technology company pioneering enzymatic recycling, a process that uses engineered enzymes to break plastics and synthetic textiles down into their molecular building blocks so they can be infinitely remade into new materials with no loss of quality. Spun out of the Australian National University, the company recovers nylon and polyester from mixed and coloured textile and plastic waste and partners with global brands to build a circular materials supply chain. It is a materials-science and biotech company rather than an API provider, and has no public developer, API, or technical integration surface at this time.

providers.name: Sortera Technologies
providers.description: Sortera Technologies (formerly Sortera Alloys) is an AI-driven metals recycling company founded in 2020 and headquartered in Markle / Fort Wayne, Indiana. It combines sensor fusion (XRF plus optical), machine-learning image and data analytics, and an advanced high-throughput scrap feeder to sort end-of-life scrap by metal type and alloy composition, upgrading feedstock streams and removing contaminants at industrial scale. From a 200,000 square foot sortation facility opened in 2023 the company produces specification aluminum scrap across cast, extrusion and sheet fractions - including 380, 356, 319 and wrought grades such as 3105 - and sells it back into domestic manufacturing. Its stated vision is 100% reuse of metals recovered from end-of-life products. The artificial intelligence runs inside Sortera's own sorting lines as an in-house platform; the product sold is recycled metal, not software, and the company publishes no public API, SDK, developer portal or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: SuperCircle
providers.description: SuperCircle (operated by MASC Inc.) is a technology and reverse-logistics platform that helps retail and fashion brands run circular-economy programs for textiles. It provides turnkey trade-in and resale programs that let consumers send worn clothing back to brands for store credit, manages excess and overstock inventory through a warehouse pickup and logistics network, and delivers real-time performance tracking and customizable impact reporting on recycling and diversion outcomes. Brand partners include Reformation, tentree, Parachute, A.L.C., and Subset. No public developer API, documentation, or SDK surface was found at the time of enrichment; this profile is a company lead in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Equator Principles
providers.description: The Equator Principles is a risk management framework adopted by financial institutions for determining, assessing, and managing environmental and social risk in project finance transactions. It provides a minimum standard for due diligence and monitoring to support responsible risk decision-making and is primarily intended to provide a minimum standard for due diligence and monitoring in project finance and related advisory activities.

providers.name: Polestar
providers.description: Polestar is a Swedish premium electric performance car brand, originally spun out of Volvo Cars' Polestar Performance racing arm and now jointly owned by Volvo Cars and Zhejiang Geely Holding Group. Headquartered in Gothenburg, Sweden and publicly listed on Nasdaq (ticker PSNY) since 2022, Polestar designs and sells a lineup of battery-electric vehicles — Polestar 1 (discontinued hybrid GT), Polestar 2 (fastback), Polestar 3 (SUV manufactured in South Carolina and Chengdu), Polestar 4 (SUV coupe), and the upcoming Polestar 5 GT. The vehicles run a Google Automotive Services–based infotainment platform with Google built-in (Maps, Assistant, Play Store), and support NACS-compatible DC fast charging in North America. Polestar emphasizes sustainability through the Polestar 0 project (climate-neutral car by 2030) and partnerships with Circulor for battery traceability. Polestar does not currently publish or document a public developer API, SDK, OEM connected-car API, or partner integration programme; all known third-party Polestar integrations (Home Assistant, community Python clients) rely on reverse-engineering the unauthenticated customer app endpoints and are explicitly unsupported by Polestar.

providers.name: Purpose Green
providers.description: Purpose Green is a Berlin-based sustainability consulting firm and 360-degree provider for sustainable real estate development, serving property owners and investors who manage multi-unit residential and commercial buildings. The company combines energy auditing (its Energy Light Report tool), ESG reporting, subsidy and grant consultation, renovation project management, and a web-based portfolio management portal (Green+ Portal) to help reduce a building's final energy demand by up to 80%. It is backed by Speedinvest and was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead; the company publishes web tools and a customer portal but no public developer API or documentation at this time.

providers.name: Libra Robotics
providers.description: Libra Robotics is a Silicon Valley robotics startup building autonomous robots that install solar panels in the field, targeting projects from 1 MW upward across utility-scale, commercial and industrial, community solar, and agrivoltaic applications. The company's field system — marketed as Libra 001 — combines purpose-built end-effectors, suction-based panel handling and transport, vision and positioning systems that align each module with the tracker structure, and fastener workflows compatible with multiple commercial racking systems, operating across day and night shifts. Libra Robotics was founded by Yaojing Huang and Jermaine Zhao, is part of the Y Combinator Summer 2026 batch, and operates out of Newark, California. As of this profile the company publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable specifications; its web presence is a six-page marketing site covering solutions, technology, safety, company, and contact.

providers.name: Newcleo
providers.description: Newcleo is a nuclear energy company founded in September 2021 by Stefano Buono, Luciano Cinotti and Elisabeth Rizzotti, headquartered in Paris with operations across France, Italy, the United Kingdom, Switzerland, Belgium and Slovakia. It designs small modular lead-cooled fast reactors (LFR) fuelled with mixed oxide (MOX) fuel made from reprocessed spent nuclear fuel, with the aim of closing the nuclear fuel cycle and reducing long-lived waste. The group employs roughly 1,000 people, has raised over EUR 780 million, and has grown by acquisition (Hydromine Nuclear Energy, SRS-Fucina, Rutschi Group). Newcleo publishes no public developer API or developer program; its only public machine-consumable software is a small set of open-source scientific Python libraries released through its newcleo-dev-team GitHub organisation.

providers.name: Rainbow
providers.description: Rainbow — formerly Riverse, whose riverse.io domain now 301s to rainbowstandard.io — is a carbon crediting programme and registry that certifies and issues Rainbow Carbon Credits (RCCs) from engineered carbon removal and greenhouse-gas reduction projects across biochar, BiCRS/BioCCS, enhanced rock weathering, ex-situ mineralization, biogas from anaerobic digestion, biobased construction materials, battery second life and electronics refurbishment. The programme is ICVCM Core-Carbon-Principles approved, ICROA endorsed, approved as a Frontier credit issuer, and runs EU CRCF-compliant plus CORSIA and Paris Agreement Article 6 crediting tracks. It operates two platforms: Arc (arc.rainbowstandard.io), the project-developer certification and MRV platform launched October 2025, and the public Rainbow Registry (registry.rainbowstandard.io) where every project, credit block, serial number and retirement is published. Its public surface is a 163-page GitBook documentation hub of standard rules, procedures, methodologies, fees and governance policies, served with a real llms.txt and a Content-Signal AI-usage declaration. No OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, GraphQL SDL, SDK, MCP server or A2A agent card is served on any Rainbow host; the only public acknowledgement that an API exists at all is a single line in the published fee schedule confirming that API connections carry no additional cost.

providers.name: Shepherd
providers.description: Shepherd is a technology-driven commercial insurance provider offering coverage for the builders and operators shaping the physical world. It underwrites Primary Casualty, Excess Casualty, and Builder's Risk lines for the construction and renewable-energy sectors, using data and an in-house AI underwriting engine (Nova) to deliver faster indications and modernized risk assessment. Shepherd sells through insurance brokers rather than exposing a public developer platform; it has issued 1,500+ policies across $400B+ in insured volume. This API Evangelist profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Costanoa Ventures and enriched by the pipeline; no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable specification was found.

providers.name: Shepherd 3
providers.description: Shepherd is a Y Combinator-backed (W21) insurtech modernizing commercial insurance for the construction and renewable energy sectors. Using technology and data-driven underwriting, it delivers faster decisions and clearer risk insights across Primary Casualty, Excess Casualty, and Builder's Risk coverage for middle-market to enterprise builders and operators. As of this enrichment pass Shepherd does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, MCP server, or a developer portal — this profile captures the company identity and public web properties only.

providers.name: Sonoco Products
providers.description: Sonoco Products Company is a global leader in sustainable metal and fiber consumer and industrial packaging, operating 285 facilities across 40 countries with 23,000+ employees. Products include metal packaging (aerosol cans, steel food cans, closures), rigid paper packaging (paper containers, fiber cartridges), industrial paper packaging (tubes, cores, recycled paperboard), and industrial specialty packaging (plastic components, reels, spools). Serves food and beverage, pet care, household products, beauty, automotive, and industrial markets. A Fortune 500 company (NYSE: SON).

providers.name: Valar Atomics
providers.description: Valar Atomics is a nuclear energy company developing high-temperature gas reactors (HTGR) with TRISO fuel, graphite moderators, and helium coolant, deployed as grid-independent gigasites of many small reactors that power heavy industry - hydrogen production via the sulfur-iodine cycle, AI data center power, industrial process heat, and clean synthetic hydrocarbon fuels via Fischer-Tropsch synthesis with captured CO2. Its Ward 250 test reactor is a partnership with the U.S. Department of Energy, the San Rafael Energy Research Center, and the State of Utah. Founded by Isaiah Taylor and backed by Initialized Capital, the company publishes no public API or developer surface as of July 2026.

providers.name: XING Mobility
providers.description: XING Mobility (行競科技) is a Taiwan-based battery technology company building immersion-cooled lithium battery systems under the IMMERSIO brand, including cell-to-pack (CTP) battery platforms, battery backup units (BBU) for AI data centers, and the automotive-grade XBE energy storage series, serving electric mobility, energy storage (ESS), marine, and data center markets from its Taoyuan City headquarters. A 500 Global portfolio company, XING Mobility publishes no public developer API or API documentation as of July 2026.

providers.name: AltoTech Global
providers.description: AltoTech Global is a Bangkok-based energy-management technology company building an AI and IoT (AIoT) platform that optimizes energy consumption and reduces carbon emissions across smart buildings. Its Alto CERO air-side and water-side products autonomously tune HVAC, VRF, and chiller-plant systems based on real-time occupancy and conditions, while Alto Digital Twin, Alto Multi-Property, and AltoACE deliver spatial building intelligence, centralized multi-site energy tracking, and AI-assisted facility engineering. Backed by 500 Global, AltoTech serves offices, malls, hotels, banks, and government facilities across Southeast Asia to help accelerate the net-zero economy.

providers.name: Alva Energy
providers.description: Alva Energy is a nuclear technology company rewriting the economics of nuclear deployment to deliver gigawatts of clean power in years, not decades. Rather than building new reactors, Alva productizes capacity upgrades ("uprates") for the existing U.S. reactor fleet: the Alva Uprate combines advanced steam generators with improved heat transfer, a second turbine plant (2TGP) sited outside the protected area, and the DUO-SYNC digital control system, adding roughly 250-300 MWe per reactor as a fixed-price, turnkey project deployable in under two years and targeting 10 GWe across the fleet. The company launched in February 2026 with $33 million in funding led by Playground Global to meet surging power demand from AI and industrial load. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of playground-global and added to the API Evangelist network; Alva Energy publishes a marketing and news presence but no public developer, API, or SDK surface at this time.

providers.name: Ateios
providers.description: Ateios Systems is an Indianapolis-based advanced battery manufacturer that produces high-energy, recyclable, PFA-free battery electrodes for global battery makers. Its proprietary RaiCure platform is a solvent-free, cure-on-command coating process using energy-curable polymers instead of solvent-based thermal drying, enabling thicker electrodes (>10 mAh/cm2), higher energy density, and roughly 5x faster coating throughput at lower cost and emissions. Ateios targets medical device, IoT, mobility, and defense markets. Founded in 2017 and backed by Techstars, TitletownTech, Good Growth Capital and others, the company is a materials/hardware manufacturer and publishes no developer API, SDK, or programmatic developer platform.

providers.name: Borqs
providers.description: Borqs Technologies Inc. is a global Internet of Things (IoT) platform solution provider delivering customizable, differentiated and scalable smart-connected IoT software, hardware and cloud-service platforms. Founded in 2007, Borqs is a Google-licensed Android and Android Wear partner with R&D centers in the U.S., India and China, and debuted publicly on Nasdaq (BRQS) in August 2017. Its BorqsWare platform powers smartphones, tablets, wearables, in-vehicle infotainment (IVI), M2M and smart-appliance solutions, and in 2021 it expanded into solar and energy storage systems (ESS) via its Holu Hou Energy acquisition. Borqs is now a Sasken Group company. No public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer portal is published; this profile carries company identity and a live domain-security probe.

providers.name: Element Zero
providers.description: Element Zero is a green-materials technology company decarbonizing the production of iron and other critical metals. Its patented non-aqueous electrochemical process converts any grade of metal ore (iron, nickel, titanium, lithium) into high-purity metal with zero carbon emissions, using 30-40% less energy than conventional smelting and operating at low temperatures so it can run on intermittent renewable energy (wind, solar, hydro). Based in Perth and northern Western Australia near the world's largest iron-ore ports, the company is scaling a modular platform aimed at the roughly 8% of global CO2 emissions from iron and steelmaking, including its Pilbara Iron Super Hub at Port Hedland. Backed by a US$10M seed round led by Playground Global. This is an industrial deep-tech company with no public API or developer platform; the profile carries identity and domain-security signals only.

providers.name: Gokin
providers.description: Gokin Solar Co., Ltd. (高景太阳能股份有限公司) is a Chinese photovoltaic manufacturer founded in 2019 and headquartered in Jiangsu, China. The company produces monocrystalline silicon ingots and wafers (N-type and P-type) and high-efficiency solar modules (GOKIN BC and FLAMINGO series), operating four major production bases with roughly 100 GW of wafer and 16 GW of module annual capacity. Ranked among the top three global silicon-wafer shippers, Gokin employs 6,000+ people, holds 500+ patents, and serves utility, commercial, and residential solar projects across 30+ countries. Backed by IDG Capital, Gokin is a solar-hardware manufacturer with a corporate marketing website and no public developer or API surface.

providers.name: Green Canopy NODE
providers.description: Green Canopy NODE is a Seattle- and Portland-based sustainable real estate development and construction technology company that designs and builds all-electric, low-carbon homes. The business operates across three lines: prefabricated "Building Kits" (including mass-timber panelized systems), full development services for multi-unit and infill housing projects, and impact investment funds that finance green housing. The company reports 300+ all-electric homes built, five real estate investment funds, and roughly 35K metric tons of greenhouse-gas emissions mitigated since inception. Green Canopy NODE was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. It publishes a marketing and investor website but no public developer program, API, or machine-readable API surface at this time.

providers.name: InRisk
providers.description: InRisk Labs is a climate insurtech company building parametric insurance products for climate and disaster risk financing. Its platform pairs an AI-driven pricing engine, real-time geospatial and weather monitoring, and blockchain smart contracts to deliver rapid, data-triggered payouts across 15+ parametric products spanning agriculture (crop, livestock, agri-input), renewable energy (solar, wind), logistics, tourism, energy demand, infrastructure protection, and wage and business-interruption cover. Risk models incorporate global climate drivers such as ENSO and IOD and range from India to global coverage. InRisk exposes an "API on-demand" so insurance partners can integrate customized products, dynamic pricing, and real-time analytics into their own infrastructure. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Bessemer Venture Partners.

providers.name: Solestial
providers.description: Solestial is a space solar energy company developing space-stable silicon photovoltaics — radiation-hardened, ultrathin flexible silicon heterojunction solar cells and modules for spacecraft. Its products are the only solar products on the market that self-cure radiation damage at operating temperatures, offering competitive performance at lower cost than III-V multijunction solar. Solestial has flight heritage across multiple spacecraft and works with customers including NASA, Boeing, and the U.S. Space Force. This is a hardware and manufacturing company with no public developer API surface.

providers.name: Tibo Energy
providers.description: Tibo Energy is an Eindhoven-based energy software company building an AI-driven Energy Management System (EMS) for commercial and industrial customers. Its SaaS platform simulates, monitors, and autonomously controls on-site energy hubs and smart grids, coordinating distributed assets such as heat pumps, EV charging stations, and battery storage to cut energy costs and emissions and to unlock additional capacity from existing infrastructure without waiting for grid upgrades. Tibo connects hardware through standard protocols such as MODBUS and OCPP via the Tibo Gateway and exchanges data with BMS, SCADA, and ERP systems through open APIs. Since launching in late 2023 it has deployed its EMS across more than 30 industrial sites and is backed by KOMPAS VC, Hitachi Ventures, SET Ventures, WEPA Ventures, and Speedinvest.

providers.name: Wikifarmer
providers.description: Wikifarmer is a global agricultural platform that connects producers with buyers through a B2B marketplace for agricultural products and educates farmers through expert-reviewed content. It provides practical agricultural knowledge, market access, and price insights for farmers, agribusinesses, traders, and food companies worldwide, with a multilingual educational library covering crop cultivation, livestock, sustainability, soil management, irrigation, pest control, and post-harvest handling, alongside a global marketplace connecting suppliers and buyers and a price-insights service for agricultural commodities.

providers.name: Coreshell
providers.description: Coreshell (Coreshell Technologies, Inc.) is a San Leandro, California battery technology company founded in 2017 that develops silicon-anode lithium-ion battery cells built on low-cost, domestically sourced metallurgical-grade silicon instead of graphite or refined polysilicon. A proprietary nanolayer surface coating stabilizes the silicon anode, and the company has unveiled commercial-scale 60 Ah cells aimed at electric vehicles, defense platforms and stationary energy storage. Coreshell is a materials and cell manufacturer, not a software vendor: its public web presence is a Webflow marketing site with no developer portal, API reference, machine-readable specification, SDK, or public code repository.

providers.name: I Flow
providers.description: iFlow Inc. is an energy and water solutions provider headquartered in Santa Ana, California, offering products and services for the sustainable use of vital resources including water metering and leak detection, wastewater management, gas measurement and control, thermal energy/BTU metering, and data connectivity solutions. No public developer APIs are documented at this time.

providers.name: IKEA U.S.
providers.description: IKEA U.S. is the United States retail operation of IKEA, run by Ingka Group, the largest IKEA franchisee. The U.S. business operates ~50+ full-service stores, ~40+ Plan & Order Points, and ~80+ pick-up locations across the country, alongside the ikea.com/us e-commerce site and the IKEA mobile app. Inter IKEA Systems B.V. separately owns the IKEA Concept and brand. IKEA U.S. offers home furnishings, kitchens, appliances, lighting, the IKEA Family loyalty program, the IKEA Business Network for B2B customers, home delivery and Click & Collect, design and planning services, the Buy Back & Resell program, and IKEA Home smart products controlled via the IKEA Home smart and IKEA Home smart 1 apps. IKEA U.S. does not publish a public developer API; supplier and trading-partner integrations are handled through IKEA's vendor systems and Ingka Group's internal digital platforms.

providers.name: Helion Energy
providers.description: Helion Energy is an Everett, Washington fusion power company building commercial fusion electricity generators using a pulsed, magneto-inertial field-reversed configuration (FRC) approach burning deuterium and helium-3. Helion forms two FRC plasmas at opposite ends of its machine, accelerates them toward each other, merges them, and uses pulsed magnetic compression to drive them to fusion conditions; the expanding plasma pushes against the confining magnetic field and induces current directly back into the machine's capacitor bank via Faraday's Law, recapturing electricity without a steam cycle. Founded in 2013 by David Kirtley, John Slough, Chris Pihl, and George Votroubek, Helion is chaired by Sam Altman and has progressed through seven generations of prototypes (IPA, Venti, Trenta, and most recently Polaris) on its way to commercial generators. Polaris, brought online in late 2024, is the company's seventh-generation machine and the first privately developed fusion device to demonstrate measurable deuterium-tritium fusion, reaching 150 million degrees Celsius in February 2026. In May 2023, Helion signed the world's first commercial fusion power purchase agreement, committing to deliver 50 MWe to Microsoft starting in 2028, with the Orion plant planned for the Malaga, Washington area; a subsequent agreement with Nucor targets a 500-MWe facility. Helion is funded by Sam Altman, SoftBank Vision Fund 2, Nucor, Lightspeed Venture Partners, and others, with a reported $5.4B valuation as of early 2025. The company's revenue model is fusion electricity sales under long-term PPAs; Helion has no public developer API, SDK, or open-source software product, and its public GitHub organization (Helion-Energy) contains only forks of plasma-physics simulation tools (WarpX, FerroX, pyamrex, maestrowf).

providers.name: TerraPower
providers.description: TerraPower is a Bellevue, Washington-based advanced nuclear innovation company founded in 2006 with Bill Gates as founder and chair. Its flagship product is the Natrium reactor, a 345 MWe sodium-cooled fast reactor co-developed with GE Vernova Hitachi Nuclear Energy and paired with an integrated molten salt energy storage system that can boost output to 500 MWe for up to five-plus hours to follow renewable grid load. TerraPower broke ground in 2024 on the first commercial Natrium demonstration plant in Kemmerer, Wyoming under the U.S. Department of Energy's Advanced Reactor Demonstration Program (ARDP), a 50/50 cost-share with up to $2 billion in federal funding. The company's second business line, TerraPower Isotopes (TPI), produces research-grade actinium-225 — an alpha-emitting radionuclide used in targeted alpha therapy for cancer — from DOE thorium-229 stockpiles in partnership with Isotek, with a lab in Everett WA and a cGMP manufacturing facility under construction in Philadelphia's Bellwether District. TerraPower has no commercial developer API, SDK, or public partner integration platform; its revenue model is reactor sales, plant operation, and isotope supply contracts with pharmaceutical partners including Aktis Oncology, Advanced Accelerator Applications, Cardinal Health, and Point Biopharma. The company does maintain a meaningful open-source nuclear engineering footprint on GitHub — most notably ARMI (Advanced Reactor Modeling Interface), an Apache 2.0 Python framework for nuclear reactor design and analysis automation used internally to design Natrium and made available to the wider reactor engineering community.

providers.name: Treecard
providers.description: Treecard was a Seedcamp-backed "walk to plant" climate consumer company that funded reforestation from everyday activity, originally through a wooden debit card and later a step-tracking mobile app. The company has shut down, and treecard.org now serves a closing notice thanking members and reporting 10,037,912 trees funded and 2,931,070 lifetime tons of carbon, pointing former users to Ecosia and Treekly while its planting projects live on at impact.veritree.com/treecard. Treecard published no public API, developer program, or machine-readable API artifacts.

providers.name: vestiairecollective
providers.description: Vestiaire Collective is a global online marketplace for pre-owned luxury and designer fashion, founded in Paris in 2009. The platform lets members buy and sell authenticated second-hand clothing, bags, shoes, watches, and accessories, with in-house physical authentication and quality control on higher-value items and a mission centered on circular fashion and sustainable consumption. It operates a consumer marketplace across web and mobile apps in dozens of countries. It is backed by Balderton Capital among other investors. This API Evangelist profile was added as a VC-portfolio lead; enrichment probes found no public developer/API program, but did verify the company's published security disclosure surface and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Wildtype
providers.description: Wildtype is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of crv, spark-capital and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: food. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Aquafortus
providers.description: Aquafortus Technologies is a New Zealand-based deep-tech water treatment company that develops patented non-thermal, zero-liquid-discharge (ZLD) desalination technology for high-salinity industrial brines. Its ABX system uses a solvent-extraction and membrane-filtration process at ambient temperatures to turn up to 98% of high-salinity brine into fresh water while using significantly less energy than thermal alternatives, and can expose, isolate and extract valuable metals and minerals (lithium, copper, magnesium salts and others) from the treated brine. The company targets cooling towers, mining, oil and gas, inland desalination, flue-gas desulphurisation and other high-volume, high-salinity industrial processes. Aquafortus is backed by deep tech venture firm DCVC and Novo Holdings, and was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub; it publishes no public API or developer surface.

providers.name: Duane Morris
providers.description: Duane Morris LLP is a Philadelphia-headquartered, full-service U.S. and international law firm founded in 1904 by Russell Duane, Steven Heckscher, and Roland S. Morris. Chaired by Matthew A. Taylor, the firm describes itself as "a law firm with more than 900 attorneys in offices across the United States and internationally" — with a U.S. footprint spanning the East Coast, Texas, the Mountain West, and California, plus international offices in London, Singapore, Vietnam (Hanoi, Ho Chi Minh City), Shanghai, Myanmar, and joint ventures/alliances reaching Mexico and Latin America. An Am Law 100 firm since 2001, Duane Morris is known for depth in intellectual property (including patent prosecution and PTAB practice), trial and appellate litigation, real estate, corporate transactions, employment, healthcare, cannabis, and life sciences. The firm publishes an extensive LexBlog-powered thought-leadership network of more than 50 practice-area blogs, all of which expose RSS 2.0 feeds via the standard WordPress /feed/ convention. Duane Morris does not expose any public developer API, SDK, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI spec, GraphQL endpoint, webhooks, status page, or developer portal; the GitHub organization github.com/duanemorris exists but has no public repositories. The firm's only machine-readable surfaces are the RSS feeds of its blog network.

providers.name: GeoGrid
providers.description: Geogrid Co., Ltd. is a South Korean smart-building water technology company behind BLOS ("Building Oasis"), an integrated building-level water purification and monitoring system. BLOS delivers drinkable water from every tap using chemical-free ionization to eliminate rust, scale, and biofilm, and pairs it with real-time monitoring of water quality, usage, carbon emissions, and consumption plus predictive analytics for pipe condition, contamination risk, and filter replacement. Geogrid targets schools, hotels and resorts, public institutions, and healthcare facilities, and offers a BLOS Care membership service. The company is based at Seoul Startup Hub Seongsu, holds 21 registered patents, and has been recognized with venture certification, ESG awards, and selection as a Korean representative for WSA 2026. This profile was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio lead and enriched from the company's public website.

providers.name: GreenQ
providers.description: GreenQ is an Israeli smart waste-management technology company (founded 2015, Jerusalem) promoting the "Internet of Garbage" — turning ordinary garbage trucks into smart trucks. Its GreenTrack device installs on any collection vehicle to weigh incoming waste and track route, mileage, capacity, time and per-bin (single-can-level) pickup data without requiring sensors on the bins, using a patent-pending visual-recognition algorithm. A recommendations engine then suggests route-optimization and scheduling improvements, surfaced through the GreenQ dashboard of reports and analytics. Collected data can be integrated with a municipality's local-authority systems through a private integration API; the company publishes no public developer portal, API reference, SDKs, or specification. GreenQ was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global (also backed by URBAN-X) and added to the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Heart Aerospace
providers.description: Heart Aerospace is a hybrid-electric aircraft manufacturer founded in 2019 and headquartered in Torrance / Los Angeles, California, working to decarbonize and lower the cost of regional air travel. The company is developing the X1, a full-scale hybrid-electric technology demonstrator, and the ES-30, a 30-seat regional production aircraft, backed by strategic airline partners including United Airlines and Air Canada and investors such as Breakthrough Energy Ventures, Lowercarbon Capital, EQT Ventures, and Y Combinator. Heart Aerospace publishes no public developer or API surface; this profile tracks the company as an API Evangelist network entry in the sustainable-transport sector.

providers.name: Hydroleap
providers.description: Hydroleap is a Singapore-based greentech company revolutionizing industrial water and wastewater treatment through proprietary electrochemical technology. Its chemical-free, modularized systems - electro-coagulation (HL-EC), electro-oxidation (HL-EO), and electro-oxidation for cooling towers (HL-EO-CT) - replace conventional chemical-intensive processes with automated, energy-efficient alternatives. Hydroleap serves data centers, palm oil mills, food and beverage production, pharmaceuticals manufacturing, and municipal wastewater operators, helping businesses cut operating costs, improve regulatory compliance, and reduce environmental impact. Backed by 500 Global, the company is profiled in the API Evangelist network; it publishes a product and marketing website but no public API or developer platform.

providers.name: Kadeya
providers.description: Kadeya is a Chicago-based, female-founded climate technology company operating a closed-loop, waste-free beverage vending system for workplaces. Its autonomous stations dispense filtered water and flavored, carbonated, and branded drinks into reusable stainless steel "Infinite Bottles," filling a cold beverage on demand in under seven seconds. Used bottles are returned to any station where they are autonomously cleaned, sanitized, and refilled for reuse, eliminating single-use plastic on site. Kadeya owns and operates the stations and sells hydration-as-a-service, charging workplaces per drink so beverages are free for employees. It serves industrial and manufacturing sites, fulfillment centers, offices, universities, and fitness centers, and reports up to a 75% carbon reduction versus PET plastic bottles. Kadeya was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. No public API, developer portal, or OpenAPI has been found.

providers.name: MBA Polymers
providers.description: MBA Polymers is a global plastics recycling company founded in 1997 that transforms waste plastics recovered from end-of-life durable goods such as computers, electronics, appliances, and automobiles into high-quality post-consumer recycled polymer granulates. Grades include ABS, impact-modified PS, PC/ABS, PP copolymer, and HDPE, produced through a three-step separate, clean, and finish process across operations in several countries. The company publishes no developer API, SDK, or technical developer surface; it was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-company profile of balderton-capital.

providers.name: Movopack
providers.description: Movopack is a Milan-based sustainability startup, founded in 2021 and backed by Techstars, 360 Capital, and Greiner Innoventures, that provides reusable, customizable packaging for e-commerce, retail, and B2B logistics. Its circular system pairs branded reusable mailers with pre-paid return labels and QR-code drop-off points, then handles quality checks, cleaning, and redistribution — cutting packaging waste by up to 98% and CO2 emissions by 84% after repeated reuse cycles. Movopack is a physical-product and reverse-logistics company and does not currently publish a public developer API; this profile captures its identity and domain-security posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Plant Cartridge
providers.description: Plant Cartridge is a Malaysian ag-tech company modernizing sustainable agriculture with modular growing systems for indoor and vertical farming. It designs and builds growing environments, supplies growing systems, and offers managed services to cultivate leafy vegetables, herbs, and fruiting vegetables with a faster growth rate while saving water, nutrients, and growing media. Headquartered in Petaling Jaya, Selangor with operations at Technology Park Malaysia in Kuala Lumpur, the company empowers farmers in the ag-tech transformation to help secure the food future. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global, Plant Cartridge publishes a marketing and news website but no public developer or API surface at this time.

providers.name: Qarbotech
providers.description: Qarbotech (Qarbotech Sdn Bhd) is a Malaysian agritech and nanotechnology company that develops biocompatible organic compounds to optimize plant photosynthesis and raise agricultural productivity. Its flagship product, QarboGrow, is a photosynthesis-enhancing treatment marketed to boost photosynthetic efficiency and lift crop yields by roughly 20-30% while improving plant health, disease resistance, and crop quality, alongside the Harvast and Harvast+ product lines. Headquartered in Puchong, Selangor with additional offices in Bukit Mertajam, Penang and Jakarta, Indonesia, the company was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global. Qarbotech is a physical-product agritech business and publishes no public developer, API, or documentation surface as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: RecommerceX
providers.description: RecommerceX is an engineering-driven manufacturing company applying circular-economy practices to transform industrial waste into advanced engineering materials. It operates three flagship brands: RexSteel (seamless and ERW stainless steel pipes, tubes, forgings, flanges and heat-exchanger tubes), RexPol (HDPE and DWC polymer pipes, polymer compounds and engineering plastics), and RexTherm (critical infrastructure including liquid cooling, heat exchangers, power components and acoustics). It serves oil & gas, chemical, pharmaceutical, infrastructure, automotive, water, power and industrial manufacturing sectors. Surfaced as a portfolio company of accel and added to the API Evangelist network; the public site publishes no API, SDK, developer portal, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Seppure
providers.description: SepPure Technologies (Seppure) is a deep-tech company building advanced organic solvent nanofiltration (OSN) membrane systems that make industrial chemical separation dramatically more sustainable, claiming processes up to 580x less energy intensive than conventional thermal separation. Its product line includes GreenMem organic solvent nanofiltration membranes, RE(SOLV) solvent recovery systems, and DE(SOLV) oil-refinery equipment, serving edible-oil refining, pharmaceutical filtration, semiconductor processing, and specialty chemicals across offices in Singapore and Calgary, Canada. It is a 500 Global portfolio company. Seppure sells membranes online at seppure.shop and publishes no public API, developer documentation, or GitHub organization at this time.

providers.name: Apollo Atomics Inc
providers.description: Apollo Atomics is a Y Combinator-backed (Spring 2026 / P26) nuclear technology company building compact, power-dense pressurized water reactors for electricity generation, industrial process heat, and data-center power. Founded by Assil Halimi and Drew Walker and based in Cambridge, Massachusetts, the company modifies the steam generator of proven pressurized water reactor technology to shrink the plant by roughly an order of magnitude without sacrificing power output, turning a decade-long construction project into a factory-built machine that can ship on a truck. Apollo has announced a research collaboration with MIT's Department of Nuclear Science and Engineering to validate its reactor design and has submitted a regulatory engagement plan to the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission, targeting a construction permit application in 2028. This is a hardware/energy company with no public developer or API surface at this time.

providers.name: Ideal Power Converters
providers.description: Ideal Power Inc. (NASDAQ: IPWR), formerly Ideal Power Converters, is an Austin, Texas power semiconductor company developing bidirectional bipolar junction transistor (B-TRAN) technology for ultra-low conduction losses, bidirectional current flow, and fast fault protection and switching. Its product portfolio includes B-TRAN power switches, SymCool power modules, and B-TRAN Known Good Die, targeting data centers, energy storage systems, power grids, solid-state circuit breakers, and EV charging infrastructure. Surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a Battery Ventures portfolio company; the company publishes a corporate and investor web presence but no public developer API or programmatic surface at this time.

providers.name: Inviscid AI
providers.description: Inviscid AI is a San Francisco-based startup (Y Combinator W2026) building physics-informed AI for real-time cooling and airflow simulation of buildings and industrial facilities. Its platform combines computational fluid dynamics (CFD) with physics-informed neural networks to run thermal digital twins up to 1000x faster than traditional CFD, ingesting live data from building management systems, meters, and IoT sensors to autonomously recommend HVAC setpoints and optimize airflow. Target facilities include data centers, offices, hospitals, and cold storage, where the company claims 30%+ energy savings and sub-90-day ROI. As of mid-2026 Inviscid AI is a pre-product-launch company with no public developer portal, API, SDKs, or OpenAPI surface; this profile tracks it as an API Evangelist network lead pending an external API.

providers.name: LINSOL Co.,Ltd.
providers.description: LINSOL Co.,Ltd. (린솔) is a safety-technology company headquartered in Daejeon, South Korea, founded as an in-house venture spun out of Hanwha Aerospace. LINSOL adapts acoustic detection techniques originally developed for defense landmine applications into commercial real-time hazard, accident, and environmental detection. Its product line includes Karang F (driving-environment detection), Karang S (precision acoustic signal transmission), SkyShield (fall detection), BR, Acoustic Eye (aerial security), and Safety Nova (smart integrated safety platform), sold into industrial safety, ESG, and defense security use cases. The company operates a Daejeon headquarters and research center plus a Goheung branch. LINSOL ships hardware and integrated platforms; as of a 2026-07-19 probe it publishes no public developer API, portal, SDK, or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Sense
providers.description: Sense is a Cambridge, Massachusetts energy-intelligence company that builds a residential energy monitor and machine-learning platform for real-time whole-home electricity disaggregation. The Sense Monitor installs in a home electrical panel, samples voltage and current at one million times per second, and uses signature-based machine-learning models to identify individual appliances and loads behind a single point of measurement. The Sense iOS, Android, and web apps surface device-level usage, always-on load, solar production, time-of-use cost, and goal tracking to homeowners. For utilities and grid operators, Sense embeds its disaggregation software into next-generation AMI 2.0 smart meters through partnerships with meter manufacturers such as Landis+Gyr, providing grid-edge visibility, fault detection, load-management, demand-response, and virtual-power-plant enablement. Sense also runs a partner program for smart-device integration with thermostats, EV chargers, heat pumps, and home-service providers. Sense has not released an official public developer API; community developers maintain reverse-engineered, unofficial clients in Python, Node.js, and Home Assistant against an undocumented and unsupported endpoint. Sense's revenue model is hardware sales of the consumer monitor and licensing of its disaggregation software to utilities and meter OEMs.

providers.name: Soma Energy
providers.description: Soma Energy is an AI-powered energy intelligence platform that optimizes how power is produced, stored, and consumed. Founded by former Amazon and technology leaders, it coordinates power generation, battery storage, and large energy consumers such as data centers. Its Intelligence Platform combines three products: AI Trader, which automates energy procurement, hedging, and dispatch for independent power producers (IPPs); BESS Dispatcher, which manages battery energy storage systems; and Load Optimizer, which coordinates data-center workloads with grid conditions to cut energy costs and turn facilities into flexible grid assets. Soma Energy is an early-stage company backed by Uncork Capital. As of this profile the company exposes no public API, developer platform, or documentation.

providers.name: Spruce Finance *
providers.description: Spruce Power operates sprucepower.com as a customer portal ("CustomerPortal") for its residential solar and home energy services, giving homeowners a dashboard to monitor their solar energy systems and production, manage their service agreement, and get in touch with support (public routes include /dashboard, /monitoring, /pro, and /get-in-touch). Surfaced as a GV portfolio company (sector: frontier-tech) and added to the API Evangelist network. Enrichment found no public developer API, developer portal, OpenAPI specification, or working /.well-known/ discovery surface — all /.well-known/ paths return the customer-portal single-page-app shell rather than real documents, and no api./developer./docs. host resolves.

providers.name: EnergyBank
providers.description: EnergyBank is a New Zealand deep-tech energy company developing next-generation energy storage for the offshore wind market. Its core approach firms floating offshore wind generation at the turbine so that compute modules can be co-located with the generation itself — taking "data to the power rather than electricity to the data" — which removes the need for a grid connection, enables consentless high-seas deployment, and allows direct ocean cooling of the co-located compute. The company was founded by CEO Tim Hawkey and CTO Alex Szczepaniak, and its team combines applied mathematicians, electronics engineers, and business development staff with advisors drawn from subsea turbomachinery. EnergyBank is venture backed by Version One Ventures, Blackbird, Icehouse Ventures, Outset Ventures, Promus Ventures, Nuance Capital, and Boost VC. As of this enrichment pass EnergyBank publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable specification — it is a hardware and energy-infrastructure company rather than an API provider.

providers.name: First Solar
providers.description: First Solar is a leading global provider of comprehensive photovoltaic (PV) solar energy solutions, designing and manufacturing thin-film solar modules. No public developer portal or open APIs have been identified at this time.

providers.name: Hexing Electrical Co., Ltd.
providers.description: Hexing Electrical Co., Ltd. (海兴电力 / Hexing) is a Chinese energy-technology company focused on smart power distribution and utilization, new energy, smart water and gas, water treatment and clean water, and marine electrification. Beyond hardware, Hexing delivers integrated solutions and project delivery spanning metering devices, communication networks (RF, PLC, cellular, NB-IoT), MDC / MDM / AMI platforms, billing systems, distribution automation, energy storage (BESS), EV charging, water metering, seawater desalination and electric marine propulsion. The company reports 34 years of industry experience, operations across 110+ countries and 17 global manufacturing hubs. Surfaced as a portfolio company of qiming and profiled in the API Evangelist network; Hexing publishes no public developer/API surface today, so this profile captures corporate identity plus the AI knowledge file (llms.txt) the company publishes for AI search / RAG.

providers.name: ICF (ICF International)
providers.description: ICF (NASDAQ: ICFI), formerly ICF International, is a global consulting and digital services firm headquartered in Reston, Virginia, delivering management, technology, and policy consulting to US federal agencies, state and local governments, utilities, and commercial clients. ICF serves markets spanning government, energy, environment, infrastructure, transportation, health, education, social programs, public safety, and disaster management, with approximately 9,000 employees worldwide. The firm has invested in an in-house AI offering branded "ICF Fathom," but no public REST APIs, developer portal, SDKs, or technical documentation have been identified. ICF's work is delivered under contract rather than through a productized developer platform.

providers.name: Ion Mobility
providers.description: ION Mobility is a Singapore-headquartered technology and automotive company that designs and builds affordable, zero-emission smart electric motorcycles for riders across Southeast Asia, with its flagship M1-S model and a companion rider mobile app. The company combines advanced hardware and software with human-centred design, spanning electric two-wheelers and energy charging and storage solutions, with additional offices in Jakarta and Shenzhen and backing from investors including 500 Global. This API Evangelist profile tracks the company's public developer and identity surface; ION Mobility currently publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or OpenAPI specification, operating a consumer waitlist/test-ride site and an internal open-source tooling estate on GitHub.

providers.name: Johnson Controls
providers.description: Johnson Controls is a global diversified technology and multi-industrial leader serving customers in over 150 countries, providing products, services, and solutions for buildings (HVAC, fire, security, building automation), energy storage, and connected building platforms (Metasys, OpenBlue). No public, self-service developer portal or OpenAPI is currently published; partner and customer integrations are typically delivered through the OpenBlue and Metasys product lines.

providers.name: Kairos Power
providers.description: Kairos Power is an Alameda, California-based advanced nuclear fission company developing the KP-FHR (Kairos Power Fluoride salt-cooled High-temperature Reactor), a Generation IV reactor design that uses TRISO (tri-structural isotropic) fuel pebbles cooled by molten fluoride salt (FLiBe) at low pressure and high temperature. Kairos Power is building Hermes, a low-power demonstration reactor at the East Tennessee Technology Park in Oak Ridge, Tennessee, which became the first non-light-water reactor authorized for construction by the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission in over 50 years (construction permit issued December 2023). A second unit, Hermes 2, will pair two reactors with a 28 MWe electricity-generating turbine. In October 2024 Google signed a corporate power purchase agreement with Kairos Power for up to 500 MW of nuclear electricity from multiple small modular reactors, with the first deployment targeted by 2030 and additional capacity through 2035 — the first corporate PPA for new advanced nuclear in the United States. The company's revenue model is reactor sales, electricity PPAs, and federal cost-share partnerships (DOE Advanced Reactor Demonstration Program). Kairos Power is privately held, does not expose a public developer API or SDK, and operates under NRC regulatory oversight as a safety-critical nuclear licensee.

providers.name: Kyten Technologies
providers.description: Kyten Technologies is a Seattle, Washington hardware manufacturing startup building a factory to produce custom aerospace-grade battery packs. The founders spent six years at Starlink, where they put more than 5,000 battery packs into space, and are now bringing rapid development and volume production of aerospace-grade battery packs to the wider industry. The company positions itself against a legacy supply chain that cannot keep up with the 100,000+ drones, submarines, and satellites being built in the United States. Kyten Technologies is a Y Combinator Winter 2026 company, classified under Industrials / Manufacturing and Robotics, and was an early-stage two-person team at the time of profiling. As a hardware manufacturer it publishes no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable API artifacts; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record.

providers.name: Orbital Insight
providers.description: Orbital Insight was a Palo Alto, California geospatial analytics company founded in 2013 by James Crawford (formerly Bell Labs, Google Books, and NASA's Mars rover program). The company applied computer vision and machine learning to satellite imagery, aerial photography, AIS vessel signals, and IoT/mobile location data to produce intelligence on supply chains, global commodities (notably oil storage via its Global Geospatial Crude Index), geopolitical events, demographics, retail foot traffic, disaster damage, and national-security questions. Its flagship product was the GO platform (later rebranded TerraScope), a self-service geospatial intelligence platform layering proprietary models over commercial satellite imagery from partners including DigitalGlobe, Airbus, Planet Labs, and e-GEOS. Orbital Insight raised funding from In-Q-Tel, GV (Google Ventures), Sequoia Capital, CME Ventures, and others, and acquired Boston-based FeatureX in 2018. After a period of financial distress in 2023, Orbital Insight was acquired by Privateer (co-founded by Apple's Steve Wozniak and Alex Fielding) on May 6, 2024. Following the acquisition, the standalone orbitalinsight.com brand was wound down and the TerraScope platform is now offered by Privateer alongside its Wayfinder space-domain-awareness data engine, fused into Privateer's "Elements" all-domain data platform. As of 2026 there is no public self-service Orbital Insight developer API, SDK, or open-source release; the orbitalinsight GitHub organization has only two archived repositories (a region-aggregation reference and a fork of tileserver-gl) and no current developer portal.

providers.name: Pachama
providers.description: Pachama is a San Francisco–based climate technology company founded in 2018 that built a satellite- and machine-learning-powered platform for monitoring, reporting, and verification (MRV) of nature-based carbon projects — including forest conservation, reforestation, afforestation, and improved forest management. Pachama combined satellite imagery, LiDAR, remote sensing, and deep-learning models to measure aboveground biomass, detect deforestation, and track project performance against verified baselines, surfacing that intelligence through an online marketplace where corporate buyers (including Microsoft, Shopify, Salesforce, Flexport.org, Mercado Libre, Boom Supersonic, and Nespresso) could discover and purchase high-integrity carbon credits. In November 2025, Pachama was acquired by Carbon Direct, and its proprietary digital MRV platform and forest-carbon science team were folded into Carbon Direct's science-backed carbon management offering; pachama.com now redirects to carbon-direct.com. Throughout its life as an independent company Pachama operated a buyer marketplace and discussed plans for a partner API to embed project selection and retirement data into third-party products, but never shipped a public, self-service developer API, SDK, or open OpenAPI specification — its GitHub organization contains only forks and archived internal tooling.

providers.name: SINAI Technologies
providers.description: SINAI Technologies is a San Francisco–headquartered enterprise SaaS company providing a Decarbonization Intelligence platform for carbon management, sustainability planning, and ESG compliance. The platform unifies organization-wide emissions accounting, climate transition planning, climate financial planning, and execution management so industrial enterprises can measure, report, and reduce Scope 1, 2, and 3 emissions using science-based methodologies. Core modules include Carbon Accounting & Reporting, the Climate Transition Planner (with marginal abatement cost curves and scenario modeling), the Climate Financial Planner, and Execution & Management for tracking decarbonization projects. SINAI's Decarbonization Intelligence Portal layers Tableau-based dashboards, AI-powered bulk data ingestion, and AI Emissions Match (which maps unstructured emissions data to emission factors) on top of the underlying carbon ledger. The platform is designed around major reporting frameworks including CDP, TCFD, SEC climate disclosure, CSRD, CBAM, California SB 253 / SB 261, Brazil SBCE, and Brazil CVM resolutions 217 and 218, and is SOC 2 compliant with TÜV SÜD ISO 14064 verification. Customers include Siemens Energy, ArcelorMittal, Harley-Davidson, Emirates, Natura &Co, Minerva Foods, Wilson Sons, BRK Ambiental, and Japan's largest bank MUFG. SINAI states publicly that it can connect to enterprise customer systems through APIs to automate roughly 70% of emissions data ingestion, but it does not publish a developer portal, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, public API reference, or a GitHub organization — its API surface is delivered as a private integration capability negotiated with enterprise customers rather than a self-serve developer product.

providers.name: Unigrid
providers.description: UNIGRID Inc. is a San Diego-based sodium-ion battery company founded in 2021 out of UC San Diego Ph.D. research by Dr. Darren H. S. Tan and Dr. Erik A. Wu. Its sodium chromium oxide (NCO) chemistry and alloy anode technology deliver fire-safe, fully passive batteries rated for 30,000+ cycles and -40C to 60C operation, sold as 12V starter batteries (Na+ Fleet), BMS-less rack modules (Na+ Module), residential energy storage (Na+ Casa), and DC rack systems for commercial, industrial, and data center use (Na+ Cleo). Cells are UN38.3 and UL 9540A certified. Backed by Transition VC, Ritz Venture Capital, Union Square Ventures, and Foothill Ventures via an oversubscribed $12M Series A (2024); shipped its first sodium-ion residential batteries in July 2026. UNIGRID publishes no public API or developer program.

providers.name: Voxel Energy
providers.description: Voxel Energy is a Y Combinator Winter 2026 company building energy-independent, off-grid data centers powered by on-site solar generation and second-life EV batteries over a DC microgrid architecture. Founded in 2025 by ex-Tesla engineers Casey Spencer, Max Pfeiffer, and Evan Schmidt, the San Francisco company delivers modular, prefabricated data center power systems that bypass multi-year utility interconnection queues, taking facilities from site selection to commissioning in months. Voxel Energy is an infrastructure hardware company and does not currently publish a public API or developer program.

providers.name: Anda
providers.description: Anda (andaafrica.com) is an Angolan mobility and delivery company that operates ride-hailing and courier services using motorcycles, electric motorcycles, and tuk-tuks, integrating technology, finance, and sustainability to serve people and businesses across Angola. Anda runs a drive-to-own model that empowers drivers to own their vehicles through training (ANDA Academia), insurance, maintenance support, and safe operating hubs, turning informal transport work into stable livelihoods. Moto-taxi rides are fulfilled through the Yango app, alongside green electric-motorcycle options, tuk-tuk transport, and express delivery. The company is based in Talatona, Angola, and is a portfolio company of Speedinvest (invested 2025). Anda does not currently publish any public API or developer documentation; this profile captures the verified company identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Arctus Aerospace
providers.description: Arctus Aerospace is a Bengaluru, India based deep-tech startup building high-altitude, long-endurance autonomous unmanned aircraft (MALE/HALE UAVs) for real-time Earth observation and geospatial intelligence. Its platforms are designed to operate near 45,000 feet for over 24 hours while carrying payloads up to 250 kg, delivering centimeter-level multispectral imagery as a "zero-infrastructure" alternative to satellites. The company positions itself as a data-as-a-service provider, selling subscription-based aerial coverage for energy, infrastructure, climate, defense, and agriculture use cases. Founded in 2024 by Shreepoorna S. Rao, Arctus raised a $2.6M pre-seed round led by Version One Ventures (with South Park Commons, gradCapital, and angels). As of this writing the company is pre-product from an API standpoint and publishes no public developer surface, API, or documentation; this profile was surfaced as a Version One Ventures portfolio lead.

providers.name: Dispatch Goods
providers.description: Dispatch Goods is a reusable-packaging and reverse-logistics company that offers returnable containers and insulated bags as an alternative to single-use and compostable packaging for direct-to-consumer meal kits, grocery delivery, and food-service operations. The company handles the full circular loop — packaging, collection, washing, and redistribution — and markets its reusable system as a cheaper and lower-impact substitute for cardboard, gel packs, and insulation, citing reductions in water use and CO2 equivalent emissions. It was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile; it does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, or technical documentation.

providers.name: Kintep (Jiangsu Kintep Environmental Protection Co., Ltd.)
providers.description: Jiangsu Kintep Environmental Protection Co., Ltd. (江苏康泰环保股份有限公司), founded in 2011 and headquartered in Taizhou, Jiangsu, China, is a national high-tech enterprise that designs, manufactures, sells, and services new-type environmental-protection equipment and complete turnkey solutions. Kintep focuses on solid-liquid separation and intelligent sludge / pollutant collection and treatment. Its KINTEP product line includes multi-disc (stacked-screw) sludge dewatering machines, integrated automatic chemical dosing units, dense-phase belt sludge deep-dewatering machines, high-efficiency fully-automatic filter-press systems, Lamella sedimentation tanks, and screw presses. The company operates seven national customer-service centers (Shenzhen, Wuhan, Chongqing, Xi'an, Tianjin, Shanghai, Yixing) and exports to customers worldwide. Kintep is a physical industrial-equipment manufacturer and does not publish a public web API, developer portal, or developer documentation.

providers.name: MOLG
providers.description: MOLG (molg.ai) is a circular manufacturing company tackling electronic waste. It operates autonomous robotic microfactories that disassemble complex devices like laptops and servers to recover components and materials for reuse, remanufacturing, and recycling. MOLG also partners with manufacturers on design-for-circularity (modular snap/press-fit/latch assembly instead of screws and adhesives) and offers OriginMark, a traceability platform for tracking devices, components, and materials across their lifecycle to calculate embodied carbon and supply-chain transparency. As of this enrichment pass MOLG publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or technical documentation; this profile captures its identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Alsym Energy
providers.description: Alsym Energy is a Malden, Massachusetts battery technology company founded in 2015 by Mukesh Chatter, Rahul Mukherjee, and Kripa Varanasi to develop low-cost, high-performance rechargeable batteries that are free of lithium and cobalt. Its Na-Series is a line of non-flammable, non-toxic sodium-ion batteries aimed at grid and utility-scale energy storage, data-center backup, and industrial applications where safety and supply-chain resilience matter. The company uses a proprietary AI/computational-materials platform to accelerate battery chemistry development, and has raised roughly $111M+ including a $78M round in 2024 led by Tata Limited and General Catalyst. Alsym is a hardware/energy-infrastructure manufacturer and does not currently publish a public developer API; this profile captures its identity and public web surface for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Amprius Technologies
providers.description: Amprius Technologies is a Fremont, California-based developer and manufacturer of high-energy density lithium-ion batteries built on a proprietary 100% silicon anode platform. Its flagship SiCore and SiMaxx cell families are marketed as among the industry's highest gravimetric and volumetric energy density rechargeable cells, enabling longer endurance, faster charging, and higher payload capacity than conventional graphite-anode chemistries. Amprius targets aviation and aerospace (high-altitude pseudo-satellites, unmanned aerial systems, electric vertical takeoff and landing aircraft), defense (US Army soldier-worn power, BAE Systems), light electric vehicles, robotics, and AI hardware. Public references include AALTO's Airbus-derived Zephyr HAPS programs, Prismatic's PHASA-35 stratospheric aircraft, Nokia Drone Networks, and Matternet drone delivery. The company runs pilot manufacturing and R&D in Fremont and is scaling a GWh-scale Brighton, Colorado plant alongside contract manufacturing partnerships in Asia.
