Amprius is publicly traded on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker AMPX. It is certified to ISO 9001:2015 and AS9100:2016. Amprius sells cells, modules, and engineering services to OEMs and defense primes; it does not publish a developer API, SDK, or open-source battery telemetry interface, and has no public GitHub organization.

providers.name: Ballard Spahr
providers.description: Ballard Spahr LLP is a national U.S. law firm founded in 1885 and headquartered in Philadelphia. Following its January 1, 2025 combination with Seattle-based Lane Powell, the firm operates as a "nationally recognized firm of more than 750 lawyers across 18 U.S. offices" with departments in Business and Transactions, Finance, Intellectual Property, Litigation, and Real Estate. The firm has historic depth in consumer financial services, real estate, public finance, and IP, and runs widely read thought-leadership properties including the Consumer Finance Monitor blog (with public RSS feed) and the Business Better podcast. Ballard Spahr does not expose any public developer API, SDK, OpenAPI spec, or developer portal — its only machine-readable surface is the Consumer Finance Monitor RSS feed.

providers.name: Darling Ingredients
providers.description: Darling Ingredients is a global developer and producer of sustainable natural ingredients from edible and inedible bio-nutrients, creating products for the food, pet food, feed, fuel, bioenergy, and fertilizer industries. Darling operates Diamond Green Diesel as a renewable diesel joint venture with Valero, and brands such as Rousselot (gelatin and collagen), Sonac, CTH, and EnviroFlight. Darling does not publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Form Energy
providers.description: Form Energy is a long-duration energy storage company headquartered in Somerville, Massachusetts and Weirton, West Virginia. Its flagship product is an iron-air battery designed to store electricity for up to 100 hours, intended to enable utilities and grid operators to firm renewable generation across multi-day weather events, replace aging fossil-fueled peakers, and defer transmission and distribution upgrades. The company manufactures its battery at Form Factory 1, a 550,000-square-foot facility built on the former Weirton Steel mill site that employs roughly 400 people. Form Energy also publishes Formware, a grid-modeling software suite used by utilities to plan resource portfolios that include multi-day storage. Notable customers and partners include Georgia Power, Xcel Energy, Great River Energy, Dominion Energy, PG&E, New York Power Authority, and Crusoe Energy (a 12 GWh agreement to firm power for AI data centers). Form Energy does not currently publish a public developer API or SDK; engagement is through utility sales, partnership, and policy channels.

providers.name: Helion Energy
providers.description: Helion Energy is a fusion energy company headquartered in Everett, Washington pursuing a pulsed, magneto-inertial field-reversed-configuration (FRC) approach that uses a deuterium-helium-3 fuel cycle and direct electricity recovery rather than steam turbines. The company is on its seventh-generation prototype, Polaris, which achieved first plasma in 2024 and is targeted to demonstrate net electricity production from fusion. Helion's prior machines include Trenta, the sixth-generation prototype that reached fusion-relevant plasma temperatures, and Hercules, an earlier device. Orion is Helion's planned first commercial fusion power plant, with a publicly announced 2028 target for delivering electricity to Microsoft under what the companies describe as the world's first commercial fusion power purchase agreement; a second customer agreement is in place with steelmaker Nucor. Helion is led by co-founder and CEO David Kirtley, CTO Chris Pihl, Chief Scientist George Votroubek, and co-founder Anthony Pancotti. Investors include Sam Altman (chair), Dustin Moskovitz, Reid Hoffman, SoftBank Vision Fund 2, Mithril Capital, Capricorn Investment Group, Peter Thiel, and others. Helion does not publish a public developer API or SDK.

providers.name: Holtec International
providers.description: Holtec International is a privately held American supplier of equipment and systems for the nuclear, solar, geothermal, and fossil power-generation industries. The company is best known for its spent-fuel storage and transport casks (HI-STAR, HI-STORM, HI-STORE CISF), decommissioning services through Holtec Decommissioning International (HDI), and its in-development SMR-300 small modular reactor — a roughly 320 MWe two-loop pressurized water reactor with an 80-year design life. Holtec is currently pursuing the first-ever restart of a permanently shut-down U.S. commercial nuclear power plant at Palisades in Michigan, which is also designated as the first deployment site for the SMR-300. The company runs manufacturing facilities in Camden, NJ, Pittsburgh, PA, and Orrville, OH, and partners with Hyundai Engineering & Construction (HDEC) on SMR-300 detailed design and full-scope plant construction.

providers.name: Moment Energy
providers.description: Moment Energy is a Coquitlam, British Columbia clean-energy company that builds battery energy storage systems (BESS) from repurposed electric-vehicle batteries for commercial and industrial customers. Its Luna BESS is described as the first repurposed-battery system to achieve UL 1973, UL 9540, and UL 9540A certifications, and is applied to demand-charge management, grid backup, EV-charging support, and energy arbitrage across data centers, public institutions, transportation, food & beverage, manufacturing, and forestry. Moment Energy is a hardware and energy-services company and publishes no public developer API surface at this time.

providers.name: NuScale Power
providers.description: NuScale Power is a Portland, Oregon-based small modular reactor (SMR) company developing the NuScale Power Module (NPM), a 77 MWe pressurized light-water reactor that is the first — and to date one of only two — SMR designs to receive design approval from the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission. Originally certified in 2020 at 50 MWe and uprated to 77 MWe under the US460 Standard Design Approval issued by the NRC on May 29, 2025, the NPM is delivered as a factory-fabricated, rail-shippable cylindrical containment vessel using passive natural-circulation safety features. Its commercial offering, the VOYGR SMR power plant, is sold in 4-, 6-, and 12-module configurations (308, 462, and 924 MWe respectively) and is targeted at utilities, data centers, hydrogen production, district heating, desalination, and industrial process heat. NuScale traces its origins to Oregon State University research begun in 2000 and was formally founded in 2007; Fluor Corporation became majority investor in 2011. The company went public on the NYSE in 2022 (ticker SMR) through a SPAC merger with Spring Valley Acquisition Corp., becoming the first publicly traded pure-play SMR vendor. NuScale partners exclusively with ENTRA1 Energy for global commercialization and operates Energy Exploration (E2) Centers — full control-room simulators hosted at Oregon State University, Texas A&M, the University of Idaho, and SNU in South Korea — for operator and regulator training. The high-profile Utah Associated Municipal Power Systems (UAMPS) Carbon Free Power Project at Idaho National Laboratory was terminated in November 2023 after costs rose from $58 to $89/MWh and subscription targets fell short, leaving NuScale without a first-of-a-kind US deployment and prompting a focus on data-center, industrial, and international (Romania RoPower, Poland KGHM, Ghana, Standard Power) opportunities. NuScale's revenue model is power-module sales/leasing, EPC services, and plant lifecycle services — there is no public developer API, SDK, or open-source release. NPM design data, topical reports, and safety analysis are conveyed through NRC docket filings and topical reports rather than a developer portal.

providers.name: Pacific Fusion
providers.description: Pacific Fusion is a fusion energy company based in Fremont, California developing commercial fusion power using pulsed magnetic inertial fusion. Its modular system pairs a fast electric pulser, a meter-scale fusion chamber, and centimeter-scale fuel targets to pursue net facility gain with practical, affordable manufacturing. Building on breakthroughs from US National Laboratories (Lawrence Livermore, Sandia) and partners such as General Atomics, the company aims to deliver limitless, clean, on-demand power. Surfaced as a portfolio company of DCVC, General Catalyst, and Lightspeed Venture Partners, this profile has been enriched through the API Evangelist network. Pacific Fusion is a hardware and energy company and publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDK surface at this time.

providers.name: Quantumscape
providers.description: QuantumScape is a battery technology company developing next-generation solid-state lithium-metal batteries for electric vehicles and energy storage. Its anode-free cell design aims to deliver greater energy density, faster charging, longer life, and improved safety versus conventional lithium-ion cells, while simplifying manufacturing and lowering cost. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Khosla Ventures and Lightspeed Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. It publishes a corporate website, blog, and investor relations resources but no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: SOURCE Global
providers.description: SOURCE Global, PBC (founded as Zero Mass Water) is a Scottsdale, Arizona public benefit corporation started in 2014 by Arizona State University materials scientist Cody Friesen to make drinking water out of sunlight and air. Its SOURCE Hydropanel is an off-grid solar-thermal device that pulls water vapor from the atmosphere, condenses and mineralizes it, and delivers roughly five liters of drinking water a day; the panels were deployed in residential, commercial, community and humanitarian projects across more than 50 countries, and the company later moved into bottled water, acquiring Proud Source Water in 2023. It raised approximately USD 270 million in total, including a USD 50 million Series C led by BlackRock in 2020 and a USD 130 million Series D in 2022 co-led by Breakthrough Energy Ventures and the Drawdown Fund with Microsoft Climate Innovation Fund and Fifth Wall participating. SOURCE was a hardware and consumer-products business rather than a software vendor: it never published a developer portal, API reference, SDK or any machine-readable API contract, and the only machine-readable surface its site ever exposed was the Shopify platform behind its direct-to-consumer storefront. The company went quiet during 2025 — an April 2025 SEC filing showed a USD 75 million raise that closed at USD 19.3 million, and founder Cody Friesen announced his departure in June 2025 — and as of August 2026 source.co answers HTTP 402 "Store unavailable" on every path while the legacy zeromasswater.com domain resolves to a parked GoDaddy builder page.

providers.name: Supercritical
providers.description: Supercritical is a London-based carbon removal marketplace founded in 2021 by Michelle You and Aaron Randall, the team behind Songkick. The company builds the market infrastructure that turns carbon dioxide removal (CDR) commitments into delivered tonnes, connecting corporate buyers with vetted suppliers of durable, engineered, and nature-engineered carbon removal. Supercritical's marketplace covers the major durable CDR pathways — biochar, BECCS, enhanced weathering, direct air capture (DAC), DAC with ocean storage, woody biomass sinking, and bio-oil — with published per-tonne pricing and live availability data. The platform layers a proprietary 118-point vetting protocol on top of supplier listings, spanning climate science, environmental impact, delivery risk, and social benefits, and reports that 84% of assessed projects fail to meet its standards. Supercritical also provides supply sourcing and creation services to originate new CDR projects, buffer-pool-based delivery-risk mitigation, and policy and science advisory work (its team advises SBTi on CDR guidance). Customers include Virgin Atlantic, The Economist Group, Rothschild & Co, XTX Markets, and Tide, with reported coverage of roughly 80% of the global durable CDR market and 1.3M tonnes contracted across 200+ corporate buyers and 600+ tracked suppliers. The business is funded by Lightspeed Venture Partners, MMC Ventures, and GreenCode Ventures. Supercritical does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or open-source repository; transactions, supplier discovery, and pricing data are delivered through its hosted marketplace, advisor relationships, and contracted buyer accounts.

providers.name: TAE Technologies
providers.description: TAE Technologies (formerly Tri Alpha Energy) is a Foothill Ranch, California fusion energy company founded in 1998, pursuing commercial fusion power using aneutronic hydrogen-boron (p-B11) fuel in an advanced beam-driven field-reversed configuration (FRC). Because the p-B11 reaction is aneutronic, TAE's approach produces virtually no neutron flux or on-site radioactive waste compared with conventional deuterium-tritium concepts. The company has built a progression of plasma machines — Sewer Pipe, CBFR-SPS, C-2, C-2U, and C-2W ("Norman") — and is constructing Copernicus in Irvine, California to demonstrate net energy gain, with Da Vinci planned as the grid-connected power-plant demonstration. TAE has raised more than USD 1.2 billion from investors including Google, Chevron, NEA, Goldman Sachs, Vulcan, Venrock, Wellcome Trust, and the Kuwait Investment Authority, and runs research collaborations with Japan's National Institute for Fusion Science (NIFS). Two operating subsidiaries commercialize spin-off technology: TAE Life Sciences develops accelerator-based Boron Neutron Capture Therapy (BNCT) systems for cancer treatment, and TAE Power Solutions builds modular, software-controlled power-management systems for e-mobility and battery applications. TAE is a private hardware and deep-science company; it does not publish a developer API, SDK, OpenAPI specification, or public open-source code repository.

providers.name: Verra
providers.description: Verra is a Washington, D.C.-based nonprofit standards body that develops and manages the world's leading certification programs for climate action and sustainable development. Its flagship program, the Verified Carbon Standard (VCS), is the most widely used voluntary greenhouse gas crediting program globally, with more than 2,579 registered projects across 132+ countries and over 1.3 billion Verified Carbon Units (VCUs) issued. Verra also operates the Climate, Community & Biodiversity Standards (CCB), the Sustainable Development Verified Impact Standard (SD VISta), the Plastic Waste Reduction Standard (PWRP), the Scope 3 Standard Program, and the Jurisdictional and Nested REDD+ (JNR) framework. The Verra Registry at registry.verra.org is the system of record for projects, methodologies, issuances, retirements, and the AFOLU pooled buffer account across these programs; project documentation, public comment periods, and credit-lifecycle records are all surfaced through that registry. Verra recently launched VCS Version 5, modernizing program operations, strengthening safeguards, and clarifying credit rights. Verra does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or GitHub organization; programmatic data access is limited to the registry's web interface and filtered report exports, and there is no open-source code or machine-readable spec catalog associated with the organization.

providers.name: Volt14
providers.description: Volt14 Solutions Pte Ltd is a Singapore-based deep-tech startup developing silicon-majority anode materials for lithium-ion batteries. Its fully integrated, tunable, and ready-to-use anodes replace conventional graphite to deliver large gains in energy density and lower normalized cell cost, while remaining compatible with existing battery cell manufacturing infrastructure. Target application markets include electric vehicles, consumer electronics, appliances, and power tools. The company is a materials-science and battery-technology producer; it publishes a corporate and careers website but exposes no public developer or API product surface. Backed by 500 Global.

providers.name: X-energy
providers.description: X-energy is an advanced nuclear reactor and fuel company headquartered in Rockville, Maryland, founded in 2009 by Dr. Kam Ghaffarian. The company's flagship product is the Xe-100, an 80 MWe (320 MWe four-pack) high-temperature gas-cooled small modular reactor (SMR) using helium coolant and TRISO-X pebble fuel, designed to deliver both electricity and high-temperature process steam to industrial customers. X-energy's fuel subsidiary, TRISO-X, is building a commercial TRISO fuel fabrication facility in Oak Ridge, Tennessee. Project pipeline includes a four-unit Xe-100 plant for Dow Chemical at Seadrift, Texas (NRC environmental assessment completed May 2026, the first US advanced reactor environmental review to be completed), a 12-unit Xe-100 deployment with Energy Northwest at the Tri-Cities, Washington site, a collaboration with Amazon Web Services for data-center power, a feasibility study with LG&E and KU in Kentucky, work with Ontario Power Generation in Canada, and selection under the US Department of Energy's Advanced Reactor Demonstration Program (ARDP). X-energy is led by CEO J. Clay Sell and Chairman/founder Dr. Kam Ghaffarian. Investors include Amazon (Climate Pledge Fund), Ares Management, Citadel, Segra Capital Management, Jane Street, Ken Griffin, the University of Michigan, and others. X-energy completed an upsized IPO on Nasdaq in April 2026. The company does not publish a public developer API or SDK.

providers.name: Again
providers.description: Again is a Copenhagen-based carbon-utilization biotech spun out of research from the Danish Technical University, Stanford, and MIT. Rather than storing captured carbon, Again feeds industrial CO2 waste and hydrogen into bioreactors where AI-designed biocatalysts ferment the gas — much like brewing — into commercial-grade acetate and other green chemicals used in adhesives, solvents, plastics, textiles, cosmetics, aromas and flavors, industrial enzymes, proteins, and fertilizers. The company runs carbon-utilization facilities in Copenhagen (CPH-1), Texas City (TXS-1, with Dow and HELM AG), and Porsgrunn, Norway (NOR-1). Again raised a $43M Series A co-led by GV (Google Ventures) and HV Capital in 2024. No public developer API surface was found during API Evangelist enrichment.

providers.name: AgZen
providers.description: AgZen is an MIT spinout building RealCoverage, a sensor- and AI-based system that measures and controls how many droplets of crop-protection product land on every leaf during agricultural spraying. A boom-mounted computer-vision sensor analyzes spray coverage and droplet quality in real time and displays actionable data on an in-cab tablet, automatically optimizing foliar sprays on any sprayer as the operator drives. Growers use RealCoverage to cut chemical and water use by up to 50% while maintaining or improving efficacy and yield, with a typical payback in under a year. RealCoverage retrofits onto any generation of sprayer and won Crop Protection Solution of the Year in 2025. AgZen is headquartered at Greentown Labs in Somerville, Massachusetts and is backed by DCVC Bio, Material Impact, Astanor Ventures, and Syngenta Group Ventures.

providers.name: Axionorbital Space
providers.description: AxionOrbital Space is a San Francisco Bay Area startup (Y Combinator Winter 2026) building foundation models for continuous Earth observation through clouds and darkness. Its flagship model, ORION, converts Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) data into high-resolution, photorealistic optical imagery in real time using deterministic one-step diffusion, overcoming the limitation that traditional optical satellites are unusable roughly 70% of the time due to weather and night cycles. The technology targets 24/7 situational awareness for defense and intelligence, commodities and financial analytics, disaster response, agriculture, and climate monitoring. Founded in 2025 by Dhenenjay Yadav (CEO, former ISRO ML engineer) and Atharva Peshkar (CTO, PhD, CU Boulder / Harvard VCG). At the time of profiling the company is pre-product with no public API, developer portal, or specifications published; this record captures its identity for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Bowery
providers.description: Bowery Farming was an American indoor vertical-farming (controlled-environment agriculture) company headquartered in New York City that grew leafy greens and herbs in automated, pesticide-free indoor farms serving major East Coast metro areas. Once valued at roughly $2.3 billion and backed by investors including Bloomberg Beta and SV Angel, the company ceased operations in November 2024 and its facilities and equipment entered liquidation through 2025-2026. Bowery published no public developer API, SDK, documentation, or discovery surface; this API Evangelist profile records the company's identity and its probed domain-security posture only.

providers.name: Klima
providers.description: Klima was a Berlin-based consumer climate-action company operated by Climate Labs GmbH, founded in 2019 by Markus Gilles, Jonas Brandau and Andreas Pursian-Ehrlich. Its mobile app let individuals calculate a personal carbon footprint from a lifestyle questionnaire, then offset those emissions through a subscription funding Gold Standard and Verified Carbon Standard projects, with in-app education and reduction tips layered on top. The company raised roughly USD 16.7M across a 2020 seed round and a EUR 10M 2022 Series A, backed by HV Capital, Keen Venture Partners, Headline, 468 Capital and Adjacent. Klima was acquired by Wren on April 30, 2025; klima.com is now a single-page wind-down notice and the company exposes no public API, developer portal, SDKs or machine-readable artifacts.

providers.name: Krosslinker
providers.description: Krosslinker (KrossLinker) is a Singapore-based deep-tech advanced-materials company that designs and manufactures silica aerogels — among the most insulating solids known — using a proprietary, water-based and scalable chemistry and manufacturing platform the company calls Aspire. Its product line spans Cryar super-insulating aerogel composite board, QuintAero ultra-light silica aerogel powder, KrossShield SR Pro aerogel-powered cooling paint, and a flexible aerogel blanket in development, serving cold-chain pharma and food packaging, building and construction passive cooling, and industrial insulation. Krosslinker operates from CleanTech III in Singapore and is a 500 Global portfolio company. It is a physical-materials manufacturer and publishes no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable API artifacts; this profile captures its public web, product, and security posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Kuva Space
providers.description: Kuva Space is a Finnish space-data company headquartered in Espoo that operates a fleet of hyperspectral Earth observation microsatellites and delivers AI-driven planetary intelligence through its Kuva Sense platform. Founded in 2016 (originally as Reaktor Space Lab) by Tuomas Tikka and Janne Kuhno in collaboration with Reaktor, the company designs, builds, and operates its own 6U CubeSat-class spacecraft carrying a patented in-orbit tunable Fabry-Perot 2D snapshot hyperspectral imager. Its operational Hyperfield-1A (launched August 2024 on SpaceX Falcon 9 from Vandenberg) and Hyperfield-1B (launched June 2025) cover the 475–950 nm VNIR range with up to 160 tunable spectral bands at 25 m spatial resolution and a 50 km swath from a 500 km polar sun-synchronous orbit. The larger 70 kg Hyperfield-2 microsatellite, scheduled for H2 2026, expands coverage to 450–1,650 nm at 15 m resolution with an additional 3.6 m GSD RGB camera. By 2030 Kuva Space plans to grow the constellation to roughly 100 satellites to enable sub-daily revisit anywhere on Earth. Onboard AI handles cloud filtering, spectral band alignment, and compression so that downlinked products feed directly into Kuva Sense, where automated analytics generate insights-as-a-service for agriculture (crop identification, yield forecasting, harvest timing), aquaculture (water quality, algal bloom detection, biomass), environment and carbon (sequestration monitoring, deforestation, pollution tracking), and safety and security (vessel detection and tracking, illegal activity warning, rapid change detection). Kuva Space is part of the European Space Agency InCubed-co-funded HYPERFIELD program, was awarded a €1.8M ESA Civil Security from Space contract within the SMART-CONNECT consortium to demonstrate rapid hyperspectral insights for crisis response, and in 2026 signed a Letter of Intent with SSC Space to strengthen Nordic space capabilities. The commercial model is subscription-based insights-as-a-service rather than pay-per-pixel imagery sales, with current access offered through the Kuva Sense Early Adopter Program; the company markets "robust APIs and customizable data formats" for system integration but does not currently publish open public API reference documentation, an OpenAPI specification, or a self-service developer portal. The only public engineering surface is the open-source kuva-data-processing Python toolkit (kuva-metadata, kuva-reader, kuva-geometry) on GitHub and PyPI, which reads Kuva GeoTIFF-based L0/L1AB/L1C/L2A data products and their metadata sidecars.

providers.name: LyondellBasell
providers.description: LyondellBasell Industries N.V. (NYSE: LYB) is one of the world's largest producers of polymers and plastic resins, including polyethylene, polypropylene, and specialty polyolefins such as Catalloy and Polybutene-1. The company also produces chemicals, fuels, polyolefin process technology, and advanced polymer solutions, and operates a Circular & Low Carbon Solutions (CLCS) business marketing CirculenRecover and CirculenRenew recycled and renewable polymers. LyondellBasell has no public developer program, no API documentation, and no source code published in its (empty) GitHub organization. In January 2025 the company began the permanent closure of its Houston Refining facility — the 263,776 bpd, full-conversion plant that was the first refinery on the Houston Ship Channel when it opened in 1918 — eliminating more than 400 jobs and exiting the refining business entirely. Profiled as a Tier 3 industrial / no-APIs provider for portfolio completeness.

providers.name: Peerby
providers.description: Peerby is a Dutch peer-to-peer sharing platform that lets neighbors borrow and rent everyday goods from one another instead of buying them new. Through its website and mobile apps, members request or list items such as tools, party and event equipment, electronics, bicycles, and household goods, then arrange local pickup and return. Positioned as an affordable, convenient, and more sustainable alternative to ownership, Peerby aims to reduce consumption and waste by unlocking the underused items already sitting in people's homes. Backed by Techstars, it was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead. Peerby operates a consumer single-page web application and native apps; it does not publish a public developer/API program, OpenAPI definitions, SDKs, or a .well-known discovery surface at this time.

It leverages shareholder proposals, direct board and ESG-team engagement, and other shareholder rights on behalf of foundations, asset managers, universities, and pension funds. Backed by Speedinvest. Its consumer website (tulipshare.com) went offline in 2026 and the company publishes no public API surface.

providers.name: ValueCo
providers.description: ValueCo (ValueCo Metrics SAS) is a Paris-based fintech building an objective ESG market view from the proprietary ESG scores of asset managers and institutional investors. Its platform aggregates investor-side scoring into a consensus view so listed and non-listed companies can understand how the market actually perceives their ESG performance and improve their strategies. A Techstars portfolio company, ValueCo serves asset managers, institutional investors, enterprises, and ESG contributors; it currently publishes no public API or developer program.

providers.name: Kettle
providers.description: Kettle is a reinsurance company that uses machine learning to model climate risk, according to the venture portfolio listings of its investors. Its focus is climate and catastrophe risk modeling applied to reinsurance underwriting. Kettle is backed by Anthemis, DCVC, Homebrew and True Ventures, and was surfaced into the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead. No public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API surface has been verified for this provider yet; this profile remains a stub awaiting a successful enrichment run with network access.

providers.name: Raincoat
providers.description: Raincoat builds embedded, highly scalable parametric climate insurance products and the automated infrastructure that powers them. Founded in 2019 and headquartered in San Juan, Puerto Rico, the company combines real-time environmental and geospatial data with parametric risk models to automatically trigger coverage and deliver instant, direct payouts to beneficiaries after natural disasters such as hurricanes, earthquakes, floods and excess rainfall. Raincoat operates as B2B2C infrastructure, connecting insurers, reinsurers and distribution partners so they can offer embedded disaster protection across Latin America, the Caribbean, the United States and other climate-exposed markets. The company is backed by Anthemis and Two Sigma Ventures. Raincoat publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation at this time; integration is handled directly through partnership.

providers.name: Alpha Technologies
providers.description: Alpha Technologies is a power-systems manufacturer providing AC, DC, and renewable powering solutions for the telecom, cable-broadband, traffic, security, industrial, and alternative-energy industries. Its product line spans uninterruptible power supplies (UPS), standby and non-standby power systems, batteries, enclosures, network/fiber powering gear, and renewable-energy products. Founded in the 1980s and now part of EnerSys, Alpha operates as a hardware and stored-energy solutions provider rather than a public API platform; it was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as an Accel-associated portfolio lead and carries no public developer or API surface at the time of enrichment.

providers.name: Amphiform
providers.description: Amphiform is an energy technology company redefining the future of energy by developing new materials and manufacturing processes that create clean, abundant, and dense energy sources. Rather than scaling existing technologies, Amphiform engineers entirely new materials using precise manufacturing tools to address energy demands for decarbonization, computing, and space exploration. A General Catalyst portfolio company in the energy-infrastructure sector, it is pre-product and does not currently publish any public API, developer documentation, or SDKs.

providers.name: Arcturus
providers.description: Arcturus (Arcturus Technologies) is a Los Angeles advanced-materials company founded by Amir Mashal that infuses carbon nanomaterials into metals to create a new class of conductors, using lasers to embed carbon into copper and dramatically improve its electrical, thermal, and mechanical performance. Positioned in frontier climate/energy tech, its drop-in materials target motor windings, bus bars, heat sinks, data-center infrastructure, electric motors, drones, robotics, and — over time — transmission lines and grid infrastructure. The company emerged from stealth in June 2026 with an $8M seed round led by Initialized Capital, with 1517, Breakthrough Energy Discovery, Toyota Ventures, and Wireframe Ventures participating. This is a deep-tech hardware/materials company with no public API or developer program; the profile is maintained as an API Evangelist network company record.

providers.name: Blueprint Power
providers.description: Blueprint Power was a New York City software company, founded in 2017 by Robyn Beavers, that turned commercial real estate portfolios into virtual power plants. Its cloud platform connected to distributed energy assets in buildings — solar, batteries, cogeneration — and used data-driven and machine-learning models to aggregate, orchestrate and transact that surplus capacity into wholesale energy markets. It raised a $3.5M Series A (Congruent Ventures, MetaProp, Fifth Wall, Fred Wilson, Brad Burnham) and was acquired by bp in October 2021, joining the bp Launchpad portfolio. As of this enrichment pass the company operates no independent public surface: www.blueprintpower.com returns a 301 permanent redirect to bp.com/retailenergy, and no developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI, SDK, or public GitHub organization could be found. Retained in the network as an acquired-company record with no API surface.

providers.name: BTR New Material Group
providers.description: BTR New Material Group Co., Ltd. (贝特瑞新材料集团股份有限公司) is a globally leading supplier of lithium-ion battery materials headquartered in China. The company produces anode materials for high-capacity batteries across soft-pack, aluminum-shell, and cylindrical formats; cathode materials for consumer electronics, power tools, energy storage, and electric vehicles; and advanced new materials used in smartphones, tablets, PCs, and displays. BTR operates a central research institute of roughly 50,000 square meters staffed by about 900 researchers. It is a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners. BTR is a materials manufacturer and publishes no developer API, documentation portal, or SDK surface; this profile captures its public web and domain-security footprint.

providers.name: Circularity Fuels
providers.description: Circularity Fuels builds AI-controlled, mass-manufacturable reactors that turn waste carbon and cheap renewable power into drop-in hydrocarbons, starting with affordable sustainable aviation fuel (SAF). Its Ouro Reactor reforms waste carbon (methane and CO2 off-gassed by dairy farms, agricultural plants, and industrial facilities) into clean syngas, and its Aion Reactor uses next-generation Fischer-Tropsch synthesis to assemble that syngas into liquid fuels. The company is a portfolio company of DCVC and was added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile. It is a hardware and process company with no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: Edviro
providers.description: Edviro is an AI platform for building operations and energy optimization, aimed at facility managers and building operators of large commercial buildings. It pulls scattered building data - utility bills, smart meters, building management systems (BMS), submeters, sensors, and work-order platforms - into one place, then follows an Ingest, Detect, Act, and Verify workflow: it consolidates the data, catches energy waste and anomalies in real time, dispatches work orders and adjusts setpoints, and proves the resulting savings against meter data and utility bills. The platform also builds a digital twin of each building to simulate capital projects and forecast ROI before purchase, and produces audit-grade Measurement and Verification (M&V) reporting. Edviro is a Y Combinator (Summer 2026) company founded in 2025 and based in San Francisco.

providers.name: Electroflow
providers.description: Electroflow Technologies is a United States deep-tech company (founded 2023, headquartered in San Bruno, California) developing an electrochemical direct lithium extraction (DLE) process that pulls lithium from dilute North American brines containing under 200ppm lithium using renewable electricity and minimal chemicals. Its cell uses anodes that absorb lithium ions from brine on one pass and release them into a carbonate solution on the reverse pass, producing battery-grade lithium carbonate that is reacted with iron and phosphate to make lithium iron phosphate (LFP) cathode powder domestically — a three-step route versus the traditional ten-step process, targeting LFP material at roughly 40% below Chinese producers. The company raised a $10M seed round in October 2025 led by Union Square Ventures with Voyager Ventures, Fifty Years, and Harpoon Ventures, and counts Breakthrough Energy among its backers. Electroflow is a hardware and battery-materials company; it publishes no public API, SDK, or developer documentation, so this profile carries identity and domain-security signal only.

providers.name: Endurance Energy
providers.description: Endurance Energy is a renewable-energy developer building subsea geothermal power systems that harness volcanic activity beneath the seafloor to generate continuous, weather-independent electricity. Its first product, Adelie, is a planned 100 kW subsea power system slated for deployment in September 2026 at the Axial Seamount caldera off the Oregon coast, targeting island nations, industrial facilities, and data centers that need firm baseload power. The company is venture-backed (a Series A led by Founders Fund) and surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a Felicis portfolio company. As of this profile it publishes no public developer surface, API, SDK, or documentation; this entry captures the company identity and probed domain-security posture.

providers.name: EnerSys
providers.description: EnerSys is a global leader in stored energy solutions for industrial applications, manufacturing batteries, chargers, accessories, and outdoor equipment enclosures. EnerSys serves motive power, reserve power, aerospace and defense, and specialty markets. While EnerSys offers a number of customer-facing web tools (Battery Sizing Program, Motive Power configurator, CARB Compliance Calculator) and product-level telemetry such as the Wi-iQ battery monitoring system and NexSys iON connected fleet platform, no public developer APIs or open specifications have been published as of this index.

providers.name: ENGIE Insight Services
providers.description: ENGIE Insight Services (formerly Ecova, now operating as ENGIE Impact) is a sustainability and resource-management company that helps corporations, cities, and governments reduce their environmental footprint and operating costs. It provides energy, water, and waste expense management, utility bill auditing and payment, data management, sustainability consulting, and decarbonization strategy across a large portfolio of client sites. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Insight Partners and added to the API Evangelist network, this profile has been enriched with domain-security and discovery probes; the company publishes no public developer API surface at the time of enrichment.

providers.name: Envision Energy
providers.description: Envision Energy is a Chinese green-technology company founded in 2007 by Lei Zhang and headquartered in Shanghai. It designs and manufactures smart wind turbines, operates one of the world's largest fleets of connected wind and solar assets, and builds net-zero industrial parks. Its business spans energy storage and batteries (through Envision AESC), green hydrogen and green ammonia, and the EnOS AIoT operating system delivered by its Envision Digital arm, which connects and manages energy and IoT devices at scale. Envision was surfaced as a portfolio company of Hongshan (formerly Sequoia China) and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; its public digital surface is a marketing site and the EnOS platform, which is documented on region-restricted hosts not reachable for spec discovery in this pass.

providers.name: Fleetzero
providers.description: Fleetzero is a Houston-based maritime technology company, founded in 2021 and led by U.S. Navy veterans and shipping-industry experts, building battery-electric energy and robotics systems to decarbonize ocean shipping at cost parity with fossil fuels. Its Leviathan modular marine energy storage system, 3.8 MWh marine battery containers, and 55 MWh battery barges provide propulsion power and mobile charging infrastructure for cargo vessels. Backed by Obvious Ventures, Fleetzero was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub; it currently publishes no public developer, API, or documentation surface, so this profile carries company identity and infrastructure signals only.

providers.name: Fourth Power
providers.description: Fourth Power is a grid-scale thermal energy storage company building a "thermal battery" that stores electricity as heat. Surplus wind and solar power is used to heat blocks of graphite to roughly 2,400 degrees Celsius; molten tin, circulated by an all-ceramic pump, moves that heat in and out of storage, and thermophotovoltaic (TPV) cells convert the stored heat back into electricity when the grid needs it. The company positions the system as a cheaper, longer-duration alternative to lithium-ion for firming a clean grid, and operates a megawatt-scale demonstration facility near Boston. Fourth Power raised a Series A led by DCVC in 2023. This is a company profile in the API Evangelist network; Fourth Power is a hardware and energy company and does not publish a public developer API.

providers.name: GCL
providers.description: GCL System Integration Technology Co., Ltd. (GCL SI, Shenzhen: 002506) is one of the four listed companies of China's GCL Group and a global leading provider of photovoltaic and clean-energy solutions. Headquartered in Suzhou Industrial Park, Jiangsu Province, the company manufactures high-efficiency solar cells, large-size photovoltaic modules, energy-storage systems, and next-generation perovskite solar technology, with operations spanning six continents. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Balderton Capital and added to the API Evangelist network; GCL SI is an industrial manufacturer and publishes no public developer/API surface at this time.

providers.name: Greenchoice
providers.description: Greenchoice is a Dutch energy supplier focused on green electricity and gas, offering renewable energy contracts, solar panels, heat pumps, and EV charging services to consumers and businesses in the Netherlands.

providers.name: Hydro Wind Energy
providers.description: Hydro Wind Energy develops offshore renewable energy infrastructure at the convergence of dispatchable clean power, grid-scale energy storage, and freshwater production. Its OceanHydro Omni deep-sea offshore wind platform converts wind into mechanical lift with built-in storage; SubSea RO Wind couples wind energy directly to subsea reverse-osmosis desalination; and the Offshore AI Power Plant integrates both with floating data centres for off-grid AI infrastructure. The company also ships QuenchSea, a portable hand-powered desalination device deployed across 60+ countries. Backed by Techstars, Republic, and Shell StartUp Engine. The company publishes no public developer API, documentation, or SDK surface as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: illuminem
providers.description: illuminem is a global sustainability platform that brings together news, expert opinion, and ESG and sustainability data in a single place for professionals, investors, and organizations working on the energy transition and the broader climate and sustainability agenda. It publishes editorial and community-contributed "Voices" articles, curates sustainability and clean-energy news, and maintains a data hub of ESG and sustainability metrics. This API Evangelist profile was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and added to the network as an enrichment lead; the provider does not currently expose a public, machine-readable developer API surface that could be discovered during this pass (its web properties sit behind a bot-challenge), so this profile carries identity and domain-security signals only, awaiting a documented API to deepen it.

providers.name: Kazadi Enterprises
providers.description: Kazadi Enterprises develops grid-independent renewable energy systems for cold chain management and energy-intensive dehumidification. Its patented Ring Regenerator technology unlocks environmental heat from ambient air to regenerate liquid desiccant, reducing conventional energy consumption for food processing, controlled environment agriculture (CEA), and HVAC applications. The company was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead; it currently publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDKs.

providers.name: Molten Industries
providers.description: Molten Industries is a West Oakland, California climate-technology company that uses methane pyrolysis to split natural gas into clean hydrogen and solid graphite using electrical resistive heating, consuming significantly less energy than conventional methods. Founded by Stanford researchers Kevin Bush and Caleb Boyd, the company produces US-made graphite for lithium-ion battery anodes and hydrogen for heavy industry. It is a hardware and materials manufacturer with no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface; it is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Union Square Ventures.

providers.name: Natron Energy
providers.description: Natron Energy was a Santa Clara, California sodium-ion battery company spun out of Stanford University in 2012 by Colin Wessells, building cells based on a Prussian blue analog (PBA) chemistry that promised long cycle life, fast charge and discharge, non-flammability, and a domestic supply chain free of lithium, cobalt, and nickel. Natron's product line was aimed at critical power and industrial backup applications, including the BlueTray 4000 — a 48 VDC, 4 kW (6 kW peak), 50 V rack-mounted sodium-ion battery tray — and the BlueRack 250 / 500 kW battery cabinets targeted at data center UPS, peak shaving, and EV fast-charging support. The company stood up the first U.S. sodium-ion mass-production line in Holland, Michigan in 2024 (a converted Clarios facility, ~600 MW/yr nameplate) and announced a planned $1.4 billion factory in Kingsboro (Rocky Mount), North Carolina that was expected to create more than 1,000 jobs. Investors included Khosla Ventures, Chevron Technology Ventures, United Airlines Ventures, Aramco Ventures, and Sherwood Partners. After ~$373M raised, on August 27, 2025 Natron's board determined that ongoing fundraising and order-pipeline efforts were unsuccessful; the company filed a WARN notice and permanently ceased operations on September 3, 2025, terminating staff at both the Holland, MI and Santa Clara, CA sites and cancelling the North Carolina factory. Sherwood Partners, the largest shareholder, took over wind-down and asset disposition. Natron was a battery hardware OEM with no public developer API, SDK, GitHub organization, or programmable cloud surface.

providers.name: New Jersey Resources
providers.description: New Jersey Resources (NJR) is a Fortune 1000 energy services holding company that provides natural gas distribution through New Jersey Natural Gas, retail energy services, midstream assets, and clean energy investments. No public APIs or developer portal have been identified at this time.

providers.name: NextEra Energy
providers.description: NextEra Energy, Inc. is a Fortune 500 American energy company and one of the largest electric utility holding companies in the United States. It is the world's largest generator of renewable energy from the wind and sun, and a world leader in battery storage. NextEra Energy operates principally through its two subsidiaries, Florida Power & Light (FPL) and NextEra Energy Resources. This repository captures the public-facing digital surface, corporate touchpoints, and any developer or data resources for NextEra Energy. No public REST APIs, developer portal, or machine-readable data feeds have been identified at this time.

providers.name: Niko
providers.description: Niko (Niko Energy) is a Mexican clean-energy company focused on energy efficiency for multi-site enterprises. It designs, installs, and finances commercial and residential solar photovoltaic systems and battery storage, wrapping them in embedded financing options that include cash purchase, 12-month interest-free plans, multi-year subscriptions, and power purchase agreements (PPAs). Its Niko Hub dashboard centralizes energy-portfolio management across locations, Niko Care provides 24/7 monitoring and maintenance, and Niko Insurance covers panel hardware. Backed by fintech venture firm QED Investors, Niko pairs solar deployment with consumption analytics and ESG / consolidated reporting. No public developer API, documentation, or specification surface was found on niko.mx as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Oklo
providers.description: Oklo Inc. is a Santa Clara, California advanced fission company designing and deploying small modular reactors under the Aurora powerhouse brand. The Aurora is a liquid-metal (sodium) cooled, metal-fueled fast reactor derived from the Experimental Breeder Reactor-II (EBR-II) lineage, engineered as a "walk-away safe" passively cooled system that is self-stabilizing and self-controlling under loss-of-coolant and loss-of-shutdown conditions. Oklo's reactors are intended to run on recycled high-assay low-enriched uranium (HALEU) fuel, including legacy EBR-II material, with the company building out three vertically integrated fast-reactor businesses: clean power generation, advanced nuclear fuel fabrication and recycling, and medical radioisotope production. The first commercial Aurora is targeted for operation at Idaho National Laboratory (INL) in late 2027 to early 2028, supported by selection into the DOE Reactor Pilot Program and Fuel Line Pilot Projects, and the company has completed an NRC Phase 1 pre-application assessment. Oklo went public in May 2024 via merger with AltC Acquisition Corp (a SPAC co-founded by Sam Altman, who serves as chairman) and trades on the NYSE under ticker OKLO. Oklo's commercial posture is utility-scale and industrial — selling power, fuel cycle services, and isotopes to data center operators, defense customers, and industrial offtakers — and the company exposes no public developer API, SDK, or open source software.

providers.name: PurismEV Inc.
providers.description: PurismEV Inc. is an AI-driven electric-vehicle energy optimization platform that processes real-time vehicle data to help fleets, OEMs, leasing companies, and operators reduce energy consumption, extend battery lifespan, and lower operating costs. Its products include Smart Throttle Control technology (range extension), Battery-Aware Smart Charging, a Smart Mobility energy management system (EMS), and a Fleet Management Dashboard for real-time monitoring across cars, delivery trucks, forklifts, scooters, and drones. PurismEV is backed by 500 Global. The company publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or developer documentation at this time.

providers.name: Quanta Services
providers.description: Quanta Services is a Fortune 500 specialty contracting company that delivers infrastructure solutions to the electric power, renewable energy, oil and gas, pipeline, and communications industries throughout North America and Australia.

providers.name: Radiant
providers.description: Radiant is a nuclear technology company developing portable, transportable microreactors designed to deliver clean, reliable power to remote sites, military installations, disaster-relief operations, and industrial locations that today depend on diesel generators. Its flagship Kaleidos reactor is a factory-built, containerized ~1 MW microreactor intended to ship by truck, plane, or ship and be operational quickly on-site. Founded by former SpaceX engineers and headquartered in El Segundo, California, Radiant is backed by DCVC and Union Square Ventures. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes a corporate and careers web presence but no public developer program, API, SDK, or technical documentation surface.

providers.name: Salient Energy
providers.description: Salient Energy is a Dartmouth, Nova Scotia based clean-energy hardware company developing zinc-ion batteries as a safer, lower-cost alternative to lithium-ion for renewable energy storage and grid applications. Its cells use a non-toxic, water-based electrolyte that eliminates fire risk, and are built from low-cost zinc and manganese materials sourced in North America, with a roughly 50% lower production carbon footprint than lithium-ion. The company positions its technology as a scalable answer to lithium supply constraints for stationary energy storage. Salient Energy manufactures physical battery hardware and does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Solactron
providers.description: Solactron, Inc. is a Silicon Valley solar technology company developing high-performance, monolithically integrated thin-film solar modules on glass substrates. Its proprietary "Thin Film 2.0" process uses a tunable compound chemistry targeting greater than 34% efficiency by capturing over 95% of the solar spectrum, aiming for the highest efficiency and lowest cost at gigawatt scale. Backed by 500 Global, Solactron is a deep-tech hardware and materials manufacturer positioned in the renewable energy and utility-scale photovoltaic market. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes a marketing website only (Home, Technology, Company, Careers, Contact) and exposes no public API, developer portal, documentation, or machine-readable discovery surface.

providers.name: SolarBridge Technologies
providers.description: SolarBridge Technologies was a solar power-electronics company that developed AC photovoltaic (ACPV) technology for residential and commercial solar, including its TrueAC modules, the Pantheon and Pantheon II microinverters, and the SolarBridge Management System for monitoring installed systems. The company was acquired by SunPower in 2014 and no longer operates as an independent business; its former marketing site is preserved at solarbridgetech.com. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Battery Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network. SolarBridge was a hardware and embedded-electronics company and does not publish a public developer program, API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Solstice
providers.description: Solstice is a community solar platform that lets households, renters, and businesses benefit from renewable energy without installing rooftop panels. Subscribers reserve a portion of a nearby solar farm and earn monthly savings on their electric bill through solar credits, while businesses can purchase community solar subscriptions and renewable energy credits (RECs). Solstice also offers subscriber-management solutions for solar developers and asset owners. Surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network; no public API surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: SparkCharge
providers.description: SparkCharge operates one of the world's largest off-grid and mobile EV charging networks, delivering on-demand electric vehicle charging to commercial and fleet operators without fixed grid infrastructure. Its offerings span mobile battery-based charging dispatched by technicians, portable off-grid power hubs, and permanent charging installations, serving delivery, rideshare, automotive, ports, and event customers. As of this enrichment pass no public developer API, SDK, developer portal, or documentation surface was found.

providers.name: Spiritus
providers.description: Spiritus Technologies is a climate-tech company building low-cost direct air capture (DAC) technology that removes carbon dioxide from the atmosphere. Its core carbon-dioxide-removal system and its Orchard Power product (pairing DAC with waste heat for net-zero power) target dramatically lower energy use and capital cost than existing DAC. Backed by Khosla Ventures, Aramco Ventures, and Mitsubishi, with carbon-removal customers including Shopify, Stripe, and Frontier. Based in White Rock, New Mexico. This is a physical carbon-removal hardware company and does not currently publish a public API, SDK, or developer platform.

providers.name: SUNWODA
providers.description: Sunwoda Electronic Co., Ltd. (欣旺达电子股份有限公司, Shenzhen Stock Exchange 300207) is a global lithium-ion battery manufacturer headquartered in Shenzhen, China. Its business spans consumer batteries (smartphone and laptop battery packs), electric-vehicle power batteries, energy-storage systems, energy services, smart hardware, and an innovation ecosystem. Sunwoda supplies battery cells and packs to major consumer-electronics and automotive OEMs worldwide. As a hardware and manufacturing company it operates corporate, investor, supplier (SRM), and bidding platforms, but publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or SDKs. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of IDG Capital and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead; enrichment confirms there is no public API surface to catalog at this time.

providers.name: Terranox AI
providers.description: Terranox AI is the first vertically integrated, AI-powered uranium discovery company, founded in 2026 and part of Y Combinator's Winter 2026 batch. The company finds high-grade uranium deposits in North America by training machine learning models on more than seventy years of exploration outcomes locked in thousands of legacy PDFs, drill logs, and hand-drawn geological maps. Traditional uranium exploration has a hit rate below one percent and timelines measured in decades; Terranox aims to raise that hit rate and compress discovery time to help supply the fuel a global nuclear-energy resurgence needs — the world must roughly quadruple uranium production by 2050. Terranox is a private operating company focused on geoscience and mineral exploration and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal. It is backed by General Catalyst, 776 Ventures, and Y Combinator.

providers.name: yinglisolar
providers.description: Yingli Energy Development Co., Ltd. (Yingli Solar) is one of the earliest companies in China to commit to the photovoltaic industry, operating as an integrated photovoltaic smart-energy solution provider spanning technology research and development, smart manufacturing of high-efficiency solar PV modules (PANDA 3.0 and YLM 3.0 series), and the development, construction, and operation of power stations for residential, commercial, and utility-scale applications. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of balderton-capital and added to the API Evangelist network. As a solar-hardware manufacturer, Yingli publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; its only online service surfaces are a product anti-counterfeiting verification tool and product-specification downloads.

providers.name: Zap Energy
providers.description: Zap Energy is a Seattle, Washington fusion energy company pursuing commercial fusion power via the sheared-flow-stabilized Z-pinch — a compact, magnet-free pulsed-power approach in which a flowing column of deuterium plasma is compressed (pinched) to fusion conditions inside a roughly two-meter metal tube, with shear in the axial flow stabilizing the pinch in place of the heavy superconducting magnets used by tokamak and stellarator designs. Founded in 2017 by Benj Conway, Brian A. Nelson, and Uri Shumlak as a spinout of University of Washington and Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory research, the company has developed a lineage of devices — ZaP, ZaP-HD, FuZE, FuZE-Q, and FuZE-3 — culminating in 2024 with Century, a 100-kW-scale repetitive pulsed-power test platform with liquid-metal walls intended to demonstrate plant-relevant technologies. In November 2025 FuZE-3 reported plasma electron pressures of 830 MPa (1.6 GPa total), the highest pressure measured in any sheared-flow-stabilized Z-pinch and a marker on the path to scientific energy gain (Q>1). Zap Energy was selected for the U.S. Department of Energy's Milestone-Based Fusion Development Program in May 2023 and received DOE approval of the preconceptual design of its Fusion Pilot Plant. The company has raised over $325 million across Series A–D from Breakthrough Energy Ventures, Lowercarbon Capital, Energy Impact Partners, Chevron Technology Ventures, Shell Ventures, DCVC, Valor Equity Partners, and Addition. As of April 2026, Zabrina Johal serves as CEO with Conway as President, and the company has expanded its mandate to also pursue small modular fission alongside its fusion roadmap. Zap Energy has no public developer API, SDK, GitHub organization, or open-source release; the technical surface is published as peer-reviewed papers and DOE milestone reports.

providers.name: Arcstone
providers.description: Arcstone is a Singapore-based digital manufacturing technology company (founded 2013) that helps enterprises digitalize and gain real-time transparency across their shop floors and supply chains. Its product family spans arc.essentials (a lightweight Manufacturing Execution System for SMEs), arc.ops (a modular, next-generation MES for large enterprises), arc.net (multi-tier supply chain visibility), arc.studio (a low-code enterprise app and integration platform), arc.green (sustainability tracking), and arc.ai (an AI control tower for managed AI workforce deployment). Arcstone serves precision engineering, FMCG, mining, semiconductor, plastics, and biomedical manufacturers, and was named a Gartner Cool Vendor in Manufacturing Operations in 2022. The company is backed by 500 Global. No public API, developer portal, or SDKs are published at this time; this profile carries the identity and infrastructure signals harvested by the API Evangelist enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: BlackSky
providers.description: BlackSky Technology (NYSE: BKSY) is a Herndon, Virginia headquartered real-time space-based intelligence company that operates a high-revisit Earth observation constellation and delivers AI-enhanced tactical ISR (intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance) imagery and analytics to defense, intelligence, and global security customers. BlackSky's flagship product is the Spectra platform — a cloud-based intelligence hub that provides on-demand satellite tasking, sub-90-minute imagery delivery, automated AI-driven object detection and change monitoring, archived imagery access, and a secure tasking and delivery API. The company operates Gen-2 satellites at 83 cm resolution and a newer Gen-3 constellation delivering 35 cm class very-high-resolution imagery with infrared sensors, inter-satellite links, and on-board AI processing, manufactured at BlackSky's facility in Tukwila, Washington. Commercial offerings include BlackSky ON-DEMAND (flexible global tasking) and BlackSky ASSURED (dedicated, contracted persistent monitoring capacity). BlackSky's Spectra tasking and imagery API is integrated into partner platforms including Esri ArcGIS, UP42, and the STAT (Satellite Tasking API) community spec, however the API is access-controlled for vetted defense, intelligence, and enterprise customers and is not exposed as a public self-service developer portal — there is no public Spectra developer documentation site, OpenAPI specification, or open SDKs at the time of this entry. The customer revenue model is subscription-based Spectra ON-DEMAND and ASSURED contracts, Mission Solutions custom engagements, and through marketplace partners.

providers.name: Cabinet Health
providers.description: Cabinet Health is an end-to-end supply chain platform for private-label over-the-counter (OTC) medicines. The company develops, sources, manufactures, and delivers OTC products across 70+ active ingredients in tablet, softgel, capsule, liquid, powder, gummy, and chewable formats to retailers, wholesalers, and online marketplaces, emphasizing sustainable, refillable packaging and quality assurance at scale. Cabinet also produces its own certified B Corp consumer brand sold on Amazon and Target. It was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network; no public developer or API surface has been found for this provider.

providers.name: Ch4 Global
providers.description: CH4 Global is a climate-technology company working to reduce methane emissions from livestock at gigatonne scale. Its flagship product, Methane Tamer, is a feed supplement made from Asparagopsis red seaweed that has been shown to cut enteric methane emissions in cattle by up to 90 percent. In January 2025 the company began production at what it describes as the world's first commercial-scale Asparagopsis growing facility, its EcoPark in Louth Bay, South Australia, using a proprietary pond-based cultivation system to lower production costs. CH4 Global is a deep-tech and agriculture-focused company backed by DCVC; it operates as a physical-product and climate-impact business rather than a software or API provider. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-company lead and enriched with the identity and domain-security signals that are publicly available.

providers.name: Clairity
providers.description: Clairity Technology Inc. is a Los Angeles based climate-tech company building gigaton-scale carbon dioxide removal using Direct Air Capture (DAC) paired with ex-situ mineralization. Their approach removes CO2 from the atmosphere with readily available, inexpensive chemicals and standard construction materials to produce concentrated CO2 streams for permanent removal and storage. Clairity operates Project Juniper, a live carbon-removal facility in Southern Nevada, and raised a $6.75M seed round in 2024. As a hardware and carbon-removal operator the company publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or documentation surface at this time; this profile captures its public identity and domain-security posture in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Coolant
providers.description: Coolant (Coolant Climate, Inc.) is a climate-technology startup building AI-powered forest monitoring and carbon measurement from consumer-grade drone imagery. Its "3D spatial intelligence" platform reconstructs high-resolution 3D forest models from ordinary drone footage (DJI Mini, Mavic) and applies computer vision to measure biomass, tree height, diameter at breast height (DBH), tree counts, species, and growth rates — delivering LiDAR-grade accuracy at a fraction of the cost. The company positions this as the measurement, reporting, and verification (MRV) layer for scalable, verifiable carbon removal, reforestation success tracking, and conservation planning. Coolant raised a $4.3M seed round from General Catalyst and Floodgate in October 2025. As of this profile the company operates a marketing site, a demo web application, and a technical blog, but publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Dechert
providers.description: Dechert LLP is a global law firm founded in 1875 and headquartered in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, with "more than 900 lawyers" across 22 offices in the United States, Europe, the Middle East, and Asia (Wikipedia cites roughly 1,000 attorneys in 20 offices; the firm itself emphasizes a global footprint spanning the U.S., Europe, Asia, and the Middle East). The firm is known for market-leading practices in financial services and investment management, private equity, private credit, mergers and acquisitions, international arbitration, intellectual property, life sciences, white collar enforcement, and antitrust. Dechert publishes deep thought-leadership through its OnPoint series, Crypto Bytes, FSR Radar, THE CRED, and ReTorts; produces multiple podcasts (Dechert 4 Real, Committed Capital, Dechert On Reg); and operates proprietary information platforms including DAMITT (Dechert Antitrust Merger Investigation Timing Tracker), World Compass, World Passport, Dechert Direct, and a Box Portal. Despite these data-driven products, Dechert does not expose any public developer API, SDK, OpenAPI specification, GraphQL endpoint, webhook surface, status page, changelog, or developer portal, and does not publish an RSS feed for OnPoint or any blog series — its only public-facing subscription mechanism is an email preference form.

providers.name: Fyto
providers.description: Fyto is a Bay Area agricultural cleantech and robotics company, founded in 2019 by Jason Prapas with MIT origins, that builds automated cultivation systems for lemna — fast-growing aquatic "superplants" in the duckweed family. Its ReCover process, GrowGrid raised growbeds, and autonomous Harvester machine capture excess nutrients from dairy and livestock operations and convert them into high-protein animal feed, cutting nitrate pollution and greenhouse-gas emissions without arable land, synthetic fertilizer, or manual labor. Backed by GV, Fyto is scaling regenerative farming from California's San Joaquin Valley. No public API, developer portal, SDK, or documentation is currently published.

providers.name: GigaCrop
providers.description: GigaCrop is an agricultural biotechnology company engineering the photosynthesis pathway to dramatically increase crop productivity. Founded by Chris Eiben, PhD, the company combines enzyme engineering and machine learning to optimize the RuBisCo enzyme, aiming to roughly double yields in staple crops such as corn and soy and to break past the limits that have held annual yield gains near one percent for a century. Backed by Playground Global, GigaCrop is working to make agriculture both more sustainable and more abundant.

providers.name: Graphic Packaging
providers.description: Graphic Packaging International is a Fortune 500 global manufacturer of sustainable, paperboard-based consumer packaging. Products include folding cartons, multipack cartons, foodservice packaging (cups, lids, to-go containers), microwave and ovenable packaging, paperboard canisters, and packaging machinery. Markets served include food, beverage, foodservice, household, personal care, healthcare, pharmaceuticals, pet care, beauty, and e-commerce. No public developer APIs are documented at this time.

providers.name: Industrial Microbes
providers.description: Industrial Microbes (iMicrobes) is a synthetic-biology company in Alameda, California that engineers microorganisms to convert renewable, low-carbon feedstocks such as ethanol and methane into commercial-grade industrial chemicals and bio-based materials. Founded in 2014 (Y Combinator W15) by Liz Clarke, Derek Greenfield, and Noah Helman, the company has produced 100% bio-based acrylic acid and targets net-zero or negative-emission building-block chemicals for coatings, paints, carbon-fiber precursors, biopolymers, and biodegradable plastics. This is a company profile in the API Evangelist network; Industrial Microbes publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI definition, SDKs, or developer portal, so the enrichment pipeline captured only verified company identity and website link properties.

providers.name: Lithos Carbon
providers.description: Lithos Carbon delivers permanent carbon dioxide removal through enhanced rock weathering on agricultural land. The company applies crushed basalt to farm fields, where it captures atmospheric CO2 while raising soil pH, replenishing nutrients (iron, magnesium, phosphorus, calcium), improving crop yields, and building resilience to drought and pests. Lithos uses machine-learning soil models to optimize basalt application rates and provides measurement, reporting, and verification of the resulting carbon removal, managing delivery, sampling, and installation end to end for farmers and carbon-credit buyers. Backed by Bain Capital Ventures and Union Square Ventures.

providers.name: Mycotech
providers.description: MYCL (Mycotech Lab) is an Indonesian biomaterials company, founded in 2015 and based in Bandung, that cultivates mushroom mycelium on agricultural waste to produce sustainable, carbon-sequestering alternatives to animal leather, plastics, and construction materials. Its flagship product is Mylea, a mycelium-based leather-like material, alongside Biobo binder board, MYCL Composite for architecture and interior design, and Mylea Sea, a seaweed-based biopolymer. A certified B Corp and Good Design Award winner backed by 500 Global and the Unreasonable Group, MYCL sells physical materials and finished goods rather than software; it publishes no public API, developer portal, or developer documentation.

providers.name: Neoplants
providers.description: Neoplants is a French climate-biotechnology company building genetically and microbially engineered houseplants that capture and metabolize indoor air pollutants. Its consumer product line pairs bioengineered pothos plants with an enhanced root microbiome ("Power Drops") to remove volatile organic compounds such as formaldehyde, benzene, toluene and xylene from indoor air. Backed by Partech and other climate investors, Neoplants operates as a direct-to-consumer brand rather than an API provider. This API Evangelist profile was created from a venture-portfolio lead; an enrichment pass confirmed the company publishes no developer API, OpenAPI, developer portal, or machine-readable API surface as of July 2026.

providers.name: Rubicon
providers.description: Rubicon (formerly NYSE: RBT) is a waste, recycling, and sustainability technology company founded in 2008. It went public in 2022 via a SPAC merger with Founder SPAC at a pro forma valuation of roughly $1.7 billion, branding itself a "digital challenger" to the traditional waste-hauling industry with a marketplace connecting waste generators to independent haulers plus the RUBICONSmartCity fleet-and-routing platform used by more than 70 municipalities. Operating Status: the company subsequently faced severe financial distress - layoffs and debt restructuring in 2023, a June 2024 NYSE delisting, and a May 2024 divestiture of its entire fleet technology and smart-city business unit (RUBICONSmartCity, RUBICONPro, RUBICONPremier) to Rodina Capital for roughly $68 million plus a possible $12 million earnout; those assets were subsequently absorbed by Routeware. In early 2025 Rubicon deregistered its securities and became a privately held company, majority-owned by Jose Miguel Enrich through MBI Holdings, and remains the subject of shareholder litigation over the change-of-control terms. The surviving company operates as a smaller enterprise waste brokerage and sustainability-data business built around the RUBICONConnect platform (service, equipment, pickup, and cost visibility for enterprise customers such as Chipotle and FedEx), alongside RUBICONRegWatch compliance tooling, sustainability reporting, technical advisory services, and the Rubicon Now on-demand dumpster-rental service in a handful of cities. rubicon.com publishes no developer portal, no public API reference, and no OpenAPI specification. The only discoverable API artifact tied to the rubicon.com domain is a "Routeware Smartcity Public Api" Swagger UI hosted at a dev subdomain (haulerpublic-api.dev.aws.rubicon.com) - leftover infrastructure from the divested fleet/smart-city business - which returned a 503 Service Unavailable on every check during this review and is not publicly documented or reachable. Any hauler or municipal system integration Rubicon references (for example, connecting to city 311 systems) is negotiated per partner and gated behind sales and onboarding rather than exposed through self-serve developer documentation. Pricing across RUBICONConnect and Rubicon's enterprise services is entirely quote-based and negotiated per contract; no public pricing, tiers, or rate limits are published. This entry is maintained as an honest stub pending any future public API surface.

providers.name: Starcloud
providers.description: Starcloud is developing orbital data centers that run AI and high-performance compute in space. The company aims to deploy hyperscale, gigawatt-scale infrastructure in orbit, using continuous solar energy without batteries and radiative cooling into the vacuum to lower cost, scale beyond terrestrial siting and permitting limits, and deploy rapidly. Backed by Nvidia, Sequoia, Andreessen Horowitz, NFX and others, Starcloud is building a roadmap of Starcloud-1 through Starcloud-4 satellite compute platforms. As of this profile the company exposes no public API, SDK, developer portal, or technical documentation surface; it is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a space-compute infrastructure company and lead for future enrichment.

providers.name: The Data Guild
providers.description: The Data Guild is a San Francisco-based venture studio, founded in 2013, that builds data-driven companies addressing challenges in healthcare, life sciences, renewable energy, and climate change. Steeped in machine learning, data science, and artificial intelligence, the Guild pioneers a co-creation model that converts LP capital into equity across a portfolio of new ventures while applying its own team's efforts directly rather than simply allocating capital. It brings products to market through spinouts, alongside portfolio-company teams, and with strategic partners. Investors include Bloomberg Beta, David Gutelius, and Silicon Valley Data Capital. The Data Guild operates a marketing/company website and publishes no public API, developer documentation, SDKs, or MCP surface; this profile captures its identity and a domain-security probe.

providers.name: The Nuclear Company
providers.description: The Nuclear Company (TNC) is a U.S.-based nuclear energy infrastructure firm deploying nuclear power at fleet scale with a "design once, build many" standardized construction approach. Through its Powerhouse Resources arm it provides maintenance, outage execution, turbine, electrical, and instrumentation services to nuclear plants nationwide, and its proprietary AI-driven Nuclear Operating System (NOS) manages deployment and operations across the nuclear lifecycle. The company publishes no public API, developer portal, or documentation surface; this profile tracks it as an API Evangelist network company and portfolio company of True Ventures.

providers.name: Bolt Threads
providers.description: Bolt Threads, Inc. was a San Francisco Bay Area biomaterials company founded in 2009 to engineer protein- and mycelium-based materials. It is best known for Microsilk, a bioengineered spider-silk fiber; Mylo, a mycelium-derived leather alternative developed with partners including adidas, Kering, Lululemon, Patagonia and Stella McCartney; and b-silk protein, a silk-protein ingredient for beauty and personal care. The company went public on Nasdaq in August 2024 via a SPAC business combination under the ticker BSLK, halted Mylo production, was suspended from Nasdaq in January 2026, and now trades OTC Pink while deregistering with the SEC. Its website serves only a notice that the company is no longer operating. Bolt Threads was a materials manufacturer, not a software vendor, and never operated a developer program, public API, SDK, or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Forever Oceans
