The one machine-readable contract it publishes is the Directus headless CMS behind its marketing website.

providers.name: Clevergy
providers.description: Clevergy (The Clevergy Solution, SL) is a Madrid-based climate-tech SaaS company, founded in 2022, that sells white-label energy-management software to electricity and gas retailers, solar installers and energy advisors. Its platform ingests household consumption data — pulled directly from Spanish distributors and the Datadis smart-meter hub via the CUPS supply-point code, or from connected solar inverters and smart devices — and turns it into consumption analytics, invoice breakdowns, savings recommendations, appliance-level disaggregation, virtual battery and wallet balances, energy-community shares, and sales leads the retailer can act on. Integrators consume it two ways: the Connect API, a Swagger 2.0 REST API on connect.clever.gy with 83 operations spanning users, houses, contracts, invoices, tariffs, equipment, energy telemetry, tickets and sales opportunities; and a catalog of roughly thirty embeddable "microfrontend" web components that drop Clevergy's end-user experiences straight into the retailer's own app or webview, authenticated with a short-lived per-user JWT. Clevergy raised a €3.2M round in October 2025 co-led by Racine² (Serena and Makesense) and Axon Partners Group, with Satgana, Wayra and Angels participating.

providers.name: DCVC (Data Collective)
providers.description: DCVC (Data Collective) is a deep-tech venture capital firm founded in 2011 and headquartered in Palo Alto and San Francisco, California. Founded and led by managing partners Matt Ocko and Zachary Bogue, DCVC backs entrepreneurs using computational and AI-driven approaches to solve trillion-dollar problems in the real world across sectors that have often seen little material progress in decades. The firm invests from early through growth stages across AI, compute and quantum, computational biology and chemistry, cybersecurity and defense, energy and climate, finance and insurance, industrial transformation and advanced manufacturing, next-gen agriculture, space, TechBio and TechMed. Across 13+ funds DCVC manages roughly $4B in assets under management (self-reported / press), making it one of the larger dedicated deep-tech franchises. Notable portfolio outcomes include companies spanning fusion energy, carbon transformation, robotics, drug discovery, and data infrastructure.

providers.name: Disclosure Requirements
providers.description: Disclosure Requirements are the regulatory and legal obligations for organizations to reveal specific information to stakeholders, regulators, and the public. These requirements span financial disclosures (SEC, IFRS), sustainability and ESG reporting (CSRD, ESRS, IFRS S1/S2, TCFD, GRI, SASB), privacy notices (GDPR, CCPA), and corporate governance, helping ensure transparency and accountability across markets and jurisdictions.

providers.name: Electra
providers.description: Electra is a European operator of ultra-fast electric-vehicle charging, headquartered at 104 rue de Richelieu in the 2nd arrondissement of Paris and led by co-founder and CEO Aurelien de Meaux. It designs, finances, installs and operates its own DC fast-charging stations rather than reselling someone else's hardware, advertising 770+ live stations with 68 more under construction, charge rates up to 400 kW, and a target of 2,200 stations / 15,000 charge points across Europe by 2030. Its own pricing and station pages cover France, Belgium, Spain, Italy, Germany, Austria, the Netherlands and Switzerland, with city hubs in Paris, Lyon, Marseille, Brussels, Antwerp, Liege, Milan, Bologna, Turin, Madrid, Barcelona and Zurich. The commercial surface is consumer- and fleet-facing: a mobile app, an Electra+ subscription that cuts up to 0.20 EUR/kWh, an RFID charging card, Autocharge and Plug&Charge, and a fleet dashboard at business.go-electra.com. It is a Serena portfolio company and has raised a 160 MEUR round, a 304 MEUR Series B and a 433 MEUR debt facility. Electra publishes NO developer portal, NO API documentation, NO OpenAPI, NO llms.txt, NO MCP server and NO A2A agent card — every one of those was probed and missed on 2026-08-17. What it does run, and what almost nobody looking at the marketing site would find, is a real machine-readable API: a live Open Charge Point Interface implementation in the Charge Point Operator role at https://ocpi.go-electra.com/ocpi/cpo, serving BOTH OCPI 2.1.1 and OCPI 2.2.1 concurrently. Its version-negotiation endpoints answer anonymously with HTTP 200 and enumerate the full module inventory — cdrs, commands, credentials, locations, sessions, tariffs and tokens, with SENDER/RECEIVER roles declared on the 2.2.1 surface — while every data module itself returns HTTP 401 with `WWW-Authenticate: Token realm="Application"`, OCPI's own bilateral token scheme. That is a documented open industry standard, fully implemented, discoverable without credentials and readable only with a roaming agreement; its production use is evidenced by the 180+ e-mobility service provider cards Electra's own help centre lists as accepted at its chargers.

providers.name: Energy and Utilities
providers.description: Energy and Utilities is a topic profile in the API Evangelist Network cataloging the API surfaces that move data across the modern electricity, gas, and water value chain. It indexes utility data integration APIs, grid and wholesale market operator APIs, federal energy data programs, renewable energy research APIs, weather APIs that drive grid demand and solar forecasting, EV charging interoperability protocols, and the Green Button family of customer energy data standards. The repo provides a baseline catalog plus shared semantics (JSON Schema, JSON-LD, vocabulary, examples) for the meter reading / energy data point that ties every one of these surfaces together.

providers.name: EQT Ventures
providers.description: EQT Ventures is the early-stage venture capital business within EQT Group, launched in 2016 and operating out of Stockholm with investment-advisory offices in London, Berlin, Paris, Amsterdam, and the United States (San Francisco / New York); the funds themselves are domiciled in Luxembourg. The firm is a sector-agnostic, conviction-led lead investor that backs what it calls "Generation-Defining Companies" from pre-seed and seed through Series A and B, writing checks that reported ranges place between roughly EUR 1M and EUR 75M (most commonly EUR 2M-50M) and following on as companies scale. EQT Ventures has raised approximately EUR 2.3B across three funds (EQT Ventures I, II, and III) and is staffed largely by ex-founders and operators who provide hands-on support in addition to capital. Its focus spans AI, SaaS and developer tools, fintech, healthtech, climate and deeptech, robotics and aerospace, gaming, and consumer/marketplaces. Notable investments include Wolt, Depop, Typeform, AnyDesk, Netlify, Fly.io, Einride, Small Giant Games, Kry, and Beamery.

providers.name: Fifth Wall
providers.description: Fifth Wall is a venture capital firm founded in 2016 by Brendan F. Wallace and Brad Greiwe and headquartered in Los Angeles, California, with additional offices in New York, San Francisco, and London. It is the largest investment firm focused on technology for the built environment ("PropTech") and real estate, investing across the venture and growth stages into companies that make buildings and the physical world smarter, safer, more sustainable, and more energy efficient. The firm spans sub-themes including proptech, construction technology, residential real estate, fintech for real estate, smart buildings, logistics, and a dedicated climate/decarbonization strategy. Fifth Wall's distinctive model pairs its portfolio companies with a network of roughly 115 strategic limited partners — major real estate owner-operators such as CBRE, Hilton, Hines, Marriott, Public Storage, Related, and Starwood Capital — to drive strategic partnerships and distribution. With over $3 billion in assets under management and nearly 170 portfolio companies, Fifth Wall has backed category leaders including Opendoor, Procore, ServiceTitan, Blend, Hippo, SmartRent, and Bilt Rewards.

providers.name: Goodvest
providers.description: Goodvest is a French mission-driven fintech (entreprise à mission) based in Paris that sells climate-aligned retail savings and investment products: an ISR assurance-vie (Goodvie, insured by Generali), a euro-fund assurance-vie (Goodlife, insured by Spirica), a Plan Épargne Retraite, a minors' contract, a green Livret d'Épargne backed by CFCAL-Banque, and a Goodvest First private-management tier covering private equity, sustainable real estate, green infrastructure and structured products. Portfolios are screened against a published seven-filter methodology aligned with the Paris Agreement — fossil-fuel exclusion, carbon-footprint and biodiversity analysis — and every unit-linked support carries EU SFDR Article 8 or Article 9 sustainability disclosures. Goodvest SAS is registered with ORIAS (20007544) as an insurance broker and non-exclusive banking intermediary, is a member of ANACOFI-CIF, and is supervised by the ACPR and the AMF. It publishes a complete public fee schedule (0% entry, exit, arbitrage and performance fees) but no public API, SDK, webhook surface or developer portal of any kind.

providers.name: helios
providers.description: helios is a French sustainable-banking company (HELIOS SAS, Paris) offering current, Premium, joint, youth, Liberté and independent/professional accounts, a green savings passbook, sustainable life insurance and wooden or recycled-plastic Visa cards through iOS, Android and web. It is a société à mission and a certified B Corp whose promise is that no customer euro finances fossil fuels or polluting industry, and it publishes the list of transition projects it funds. helios is registered in REGAFI under 731225 as a payment services agent of OKALI, the ACPR-approved electronic money institution that services the accounts. It publishes no public API, SDK, webhook or developer portal; the one machine-readable document it serves is an llms.txt AI-usage policy.
